# epx — full documentation

Source: https://commerce-cloud-integrations.github.io/emporix-cli/

# Overview

> Read and manage your Emporix tenant from the command line.

epx is a command-line client for the [Emporix Commerce APIs](https://developer.emporix.io/api-references).
It helps you inspect, script, and change the data of an Emporix tenant right from the terminal.

With epx, you can:

- Read products, categories, catalogs, prices, availability, customers, orders, and nearly
  every other Emporix resource as a table, CSV, JSON, YAML, or JSON Lines.
- [Filter, sort, and page through lists](/emporix-cli/guides/lists) without writing paging code.
- [Change data safely](/emporix-cli/guides/writes): every write shows its exact request with `--dry-run` and
  asks before it sends.
- [Call any Emporix endpoint](/emporix-cli/guides/api) with `epx api`, using only the OAuth scopes you name.
- [Script reliably](/emporix-cli/guides/exit-codes) with stable output and exit codes that tell a missing item
  from a missing scope.

  <video autoPlay muted loop playsInline src="/images/demo.webm" aria-label="epx reading sites and products, previewing a write, and checking its API key" />

  epx is an unofficial project. It isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Emporix.

## Get started

    Install with npm, from a release archive, or with Go.
    Give epx an API key with only the scopes you need.
    Make your first reads in five minutes.

## Guides

    Choose tables, CSV, JSON, YAML, or JSON Lines, and pick columns and languages.
    Narrow lists with `--limit`, `--query`, and `--sort`.
    Send a request to any Emporix API path with `epx api`.
    Send writes with dry runs, confirmation, and explicit scopes.
    Write many items at once and wait for long-running jobs.
    Use epx in scripts and CI, and handle every failure.

## Reference

    Every command and flag, with the OAuth scopes it requests.
    How epx handles credentials, scopes, and the data it prints.
    Which Emporix API operations epx sends, per service.

# Install epx

> Install epx with npm, from a release archive, or with Go, and set up shell completion.

epx is a single binary for macOS, Linux, and Windows, on x64 (amd64) and arm64. Install it
with npm, from a release archive, or with Go.

## Install with npm

```sh
npm install --global epx-cli
```

npm installs the package `epx-cli`, which provides the `epx` command, and only the
package that holds the binary of your platform, such as `epx-cli-darwin-arm64`. Nothing is
compiled, no install script runs, and nothing is downloaded outside the npm registry, so a
private registry mirror works too. You need Node.js 18 or later.

To run epx once without installing it:

```sh
npx epx-cli version
```

  The `epx` command that npm installs is a small Node.js program that runs the binary.
  Under `nohup`, it still ends when the terminal closes. For such runs, call the binary
  itself (`bin/epx` in the package `epx-cli-<os>-<cpu>`), or install epx from a release
  archive.

## Install from a release archive

Each [release](https://github.com/commerce-cloud-integrations/emporix-cli/releases) holds
an archive per platform (`epx_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz`, or `.zip` on Windows) and a
checksums file. For example, on Linux x64:

```sh
version=v0.1.0
base=https://github.com/commerce-cloud-integrations/emporix-cli/releases/download/$version
curl -fsSLO "$base/epx_${version}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" &&
  curl -fsSLO "$base/epx_${version}_checksums.txt" &&
  sha256sum --check --ignore-missing "epx_${version}_checksums.txt" &&
  tar -xzf "epx_${version}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" &&
  sudo install "epx_${version}_linux_amd64/epx" /usr/local/bin/epx
```

Each step runs only when the one before it succeeds, so an archive that doesn't match the
checksums file is never installed. On macOS, use `shasum -a 256 --check --ignore-missing`
instead of `sha256sum --check --ignore-missing`.

## Install with Go

```sh
go install github.com/commerce-cloud-integrations/emporix-cli/cmd/epx@latest
```

You need Go 1.27.2 or later; an older Go toolchain downloads the required version
automatically. Go installs the binary in `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`, or in `$GOBIN` when it's
set. Make sure that directory is on your `PATH`.

## Build from source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/commerce-cloud-integrations/emporix-cli.git
cd emporix-cli
go build -o bin/epx ./cmd/epx
```

## Check the version

```sh
epx version
```

```text
epx v0.1.0 (go1.27.2)
```

A release prints its version. A build of an untagged commit prints the commit's date and
hash instead, such as `epx v0.0.0-20261014183651-ffca1e3d7f17 (go1.27.2)`.

## Upgrade epx

| Installed with | Upgrade |
| --- | --- |
| npm | `npm update --global epx-cli` |
| A release archive | Replace the binary with the one from the new release. |
| Go | Run `go install` again. |

## Set up shell completion

`epx completion` prints a completion script for bash, zsh, fish, or PowerShell. It
completes commands, flags, the values of `-o`, arguments that take only a few values,
profile names, and the file names of flags that take a file, such as `--file`, `--body`,
and `--out`.

Load it in the current shell:

```sh bash
eval "$(epx completion bash)"
```

```sh zsh
source <(epx completion zsh)   # needs compinit enabled
```

```sh fish
epx completion fish | source
```

```powershell PowerShell
epx completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

To load it in every new session, follow `epx completion <shell> --help`. For example, in
fish:

```sh
epx completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/epx.fish
```

bash completion needs the `bash-completion` package. Add `--no-descriptions` to any
script to leave out the descriptions of commands and flags.

### Complete IDs from your tenant

Set `EPX_COMPLETE_IDS=1` to let completion read IDs and site codes from the API, with the
API key in effect:

```sh
export EPX_COMPLETE_IDS=1
epx products get <TAB>       # product IDs, each with its name
epx prices list --site <TAB> # the codes of the active sites
```

Completion reads the first page of the matching list with that list's read scopes,
within 3 seconds, and offers up to 100 values that start with what you typed. It never
requests a write-capable scope. When the API can't be read, it offers nothing and prints
nothing.

An argument whose list needs a site completes once `--site` comes before it, or with the
default site of your profile.

## Uninstall epx

1. If you use [profiles](/emporix-cli/configure#store-keys-in-profiles), remove each one with
   `epx profile remove`, which also deletes its client secret from the OS keychain.
2. Remove epx: `npm uninstall --global epx-cli`, or delete the `epx` binary you installed
   from an archive or with Go.
3. Delete the `epx` folder from your configuration directory.

Once epx is installed, you can [authenticate](/emporix-cli/configure) with an API key and take the
[quickstart](/emporix-cli/quickstart).

Source: https://commerce-cloud-integrations.github.io/emporix-cli/configure/

# Authenticate

> Give epx an Emporix API key through environment variables or a profile, with only the scopes your commands need.

epx authenticates with an Emporix API key: the client ID and client secret of OAuth
client credentials. It reads the key from environment variables or from a
[profile](#store-keys-in-profiles), never from flags, and it never reads a client secret
from a file.

## Create an API key

In the [Emporix Developer Portal](https://app.emporix.io), open **Manage API Keys** and
create a custom key with only the scopes of the commands you run. Each command's help
ends with the scopes it requests, as does its entry in the [CLI reference](/emporix-cli/commands):

```sh
epx products list --help    # ... Requires the product.product_read_unpublished scope.
epx sites list --help       # ... No OAuth scope is needed.
```

Add write scopes, such as `product.product_manage`, only to keys that send
[writes](/emporix-cli/guides/writes). Keep them off keys you use only to read.

  Your tenant's default Emporix API key also works, but it grants every scope, including
  those that change data.

## Set environment variables

```sh
export EMPORIX_TENANT=acme1
export EMPORIX_CLIENT_ID=...
export EMPORIX_CLIENT_SECRET=...
```

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `EMPORIX_TENANT` | Your tenant, such as `acme1`. Required unless you pass `--tenant`. |
| `EMPORIX_CLIENT_ID` | The client ID of the API key. Required. |
| `EMPORIX_CLIENT_SECRET` | The client secret of the API key. Required. |
| `EMPORIX_API_URL` | The API host. Defaults to `https://api.emporix.io`. Must use HTTPS, except for a loopback address such as `localhost`. |
| `EPX_PROFILE` | The [profile](#store-keys-in-profiles) to use when you don't pass `--profile` and no `EMPORIX_` variable is set. |
| `EPX_COMPLETE_IDS` | Set to `1` to let [shell completion](/emporix-cli/install#complete-ids-from-your-tenant) read IDs from the API. |

When a required setting is missing, any command that calls Emporix, and any write's
`--dry-run`, fails with exit code 2 and names what to set.

## Store keys in profiles

A profile keeps an API key so you can switch between tenants and keys without exporting
variables. It holds a tenant, an API URL, a client ID, and optionally a default site and
language. The client secret goes to your OS keychain, never to a file.

```sh
epx profile add dev --tenant acme1 --client-id ... --site AcmeStore_NL --language nl
epx profile list
epx profile show dev     # its settings, and whether its client secret is stored
epx profile use dev      # make it the default profile
epx profile remove dev   # asks first; pass --yes in scripts
```

`profile add` asks for the client secret on a terminal without showing it. Elsewhere, it
reads the first line of standard input:

```sh
printf '%s\n' "$CLIENT_SECRET" | epx profile add ci --tenant acme1 --client-id ...
```

The first profile you add becomes the default. `profile add` sends nothing to Emporix;
check the new key with `epx --profile dev auth status`.

### Choose a profile

A command uses the profile that `--profile` names, then the one in `EPX_PROFILE`, then
the default profile. Profiles apply only when no `EMPORIX_` variable is set: the
environment or a profile supplies the whole API key, never a mix of both, so a client
secret only ever goes to its own API URL. Naming a profile while an `EMPORIX_` variable
is set is a usage error.

A profile's default site and language apply on its own tenant to commands that need a
site or show translations, when you don't pass `--site` or `--language`.

### Where profiles are stored

| Item | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Profiles | `epx/config.json` in your configuration directory: `~/.config` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS, `%AppData%` on Windows. epx writes it readable by you only. On Linux and macOS, it refuses to read it once other users can read or change it. |
| Client secrets | The macOS Keychain, the Windows Credential Manager, or a Secret Service such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet on Linux, under the service `epx` and the profile's name. |

Profile names have up to 64 characters: lowercase letters and digits, with `.`, `_`,
and `-` after the first. The Windows Credential Manager ignores case, so `Dev` and `dev` would share a
secret.

## Check your API key

```sh
epx auth status --scope product.product_read_unpublished --scope indexing.search_view
```

`auth status` requests a token for your tenant and each `--scope`, then shows the tenant,
the token's lifetime, and the scopes granted. It never prints the token. Emporix only
grants the scopes a token asks for, so pass every scope you want to check.

## Missing scopes

Emporix doesn't reject a token request for a scope your API key lacks. It leaves the
scope out of the token, and reads may then return less data, such as published products
only. To keep that from going unnoticed, epx compares every token with the scopes and
tenant it asked for, and fails with exit code 3 when one doesn't match:

```text
Error: credential for tenant "acme1" lacks required scopes: product.product_read_unpublished
```

Add the scope to your API key, or use another key. epx never retries with broader scopes.

## Write-capable scopes for reads

A few reads are allowed by Emporix only with a scope that can also change data, such as
`site.site_manage`. epx treats any scope whose name doesn't contain `read` or `view` as a
word as write-capable. These reads request such a scope only when you pass
`--allow-write-scope`, and their help marks them as opt-in:

```sh
epx sites codes --allow-write-scope
```

Without the flag, they fail with exit code 2 before anything is sent. The read still
changes nothing; the flag confirms that you accept a token that could. Writes don't take
this flag: they request the scopes in their help, or those you name with `--scope`.

## Global flags

These flags apply to every command:

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--profile <name>` | The profile to use. |
| `--tenant <tenant>` | The tenant, instead of the one from the environment or the profile. An empty value fails as missing configuration. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | The limit for each HTTP request. Defaults to `30s`. |

Once you've set up a key, take the [quickstart](/emporix-cli/quickstart) or read the
[security model](/emporix-cli/security).

# Quickstart

> Go from an Emporix API key to your first epx reads in five minutes.

This quickstart walks you through your first reads: you check your API key, list your
sites, read products, and call an endpoint directly.

Before you begin, [install epx](/emporix-cli/install) and [create an API key](/emporix-cli/configure#create-an-api-key)
with the `product.product_read_unpublished` scope.

    ```sh
    export EMPORIX_TENANT=acme1
    export EMPORIX_CLIENT_ID=...
    export EMPORIX_CLIENT_SECRET=...
    ```

    To keep the key between sessions, store it in a
    [profile](/emporix-cli/configure#store-keys-in-profiles) instead.

    ```sh
    epx auth status --scope product.product_read_unpublished
    ```

    The output shows your tenant, the token's lifetime, and the scopes granted. If the key
    lacks the scope, epx says so and exits with code 3.

    ```sh
    epx sites list
    ```

    Reads print a table by default. Add `-o json` to print the whole response, every value
    as Emporix sends it.

    ```sh
    epx products list --limit 5
    epx products get 100200 -o json
    ```

    `--limit 5` prints at most five products, and epx stops reading pages as soon as it
    can. Tables show English text by default; pass `--language` to pick another
    translation:

    ```sh
    epx products list --limit 5 --language nl
    ```

    ```sh
    epx products list --query 'name.en:~shirt published:true' --sort code:desc --limit 20
    ```

    `--query` takes an Emporix q filter and `--sort` an Emporix sort order, both passed as
    given.

    ```sh
    epx api get '/product/{tenant}/products' -p pageSize=5 --scope product.product_read_unpublished
    ```

    `epx api get` sends a GET request to any Emporix API path and prints the JSON
    response. epx replaces `{tenant}` with your tenant; quote the path so your shell
    leaves the braces alone.

## Next steps

    Tables, CSV, JSON, YAML, and JSON Lines.
    Which lists take which flags, and how paging works.
    Send your first write with a dry run.
    Every command, its flags, and its scopes.

# Format output

> Print what Emporix answers as a table, CSV, JSON, YAML, or JSON Lines, and choose columns and languages.

Every read prints a table by default. Use `-o` to choose another format:

| Format | Flag | Prints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table | `-o table` | A few selected columns per item. The default. |
| CSV | `-o csv` | The table's rows as CSV. |
| JSON | `-o json` | The whole response, as Emporix sends it. |
| YAML | `-o yaml` | The whole response, as YAML 1.2. |
| JSON Lines | `--stream` | One item per line, printed while the list is read. |

Results go to standard output and errors to standard error, so you can pipe and
redirect output safely.

## Tables

```sh
epx sites list
epx products list --limit 10
```

A table shows a few columns per item, with the identifier that `get` takes first. Tables
are for reading; use `-o json` in scripts.

To keep tables readable, epx shortens some long values, such as a setting's value or an
error message, to 60 characters ending in `…`. Tables and CSV also drop the trailing zeros of amounts beyond
the cents, so `35.7000000` shows as `35.70`. JSON and YAML print every value as sent.

### Choose columns

```sh
epx products list --columns code,name
epx sites list --columns code --no-headers
```

`--columns` picks the columns and their order by their headers, in any case. Quote a
header that contains a space: `--columns 'id,root product'`. Each read's help lists its
columns. `--no-headers` leaves out the header row.

`--columns` and `--no-headers` apply to tables and CSV only.

## CSV

```sh
epx products list -o csv > products.csv
```

`-o csv` prints the table's rows, quoted as RFC 4180 specifies, with the header row
first unless you pass `--no-headers`. Long values aren't shortened.

  CSV cells aren't made safe for spreadsheets. A cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, or
  `@`, such as a name a shopper typed, can run as a formula when a spreadsheet opens the
  file. Import such files as text.

## JSON

```sh
epx products get 100200 -o json
epx sites list -o json | jq -r '.[].code'
```

`-o json` prints the response as Emporix sends it, indented, with object keys sorted so
that output is stable and easy to compare. Values keep their exact text, and nothing is
redacted. A list prints the items of every page as one JSON array.

`epx api` and every write print their response as JSON, too.

## YAML

```sh
epx products get 100200 -o yaml
```

`-o yaml` prints the same data as `-o json`, as YAML 1.2 in block style. Every string is
double-quoted, so values such as `"no"`, `"1.0"`, and `"null"` stay strings, and numbers
keep their exact text.

  A YAML 1.1 parser reads a number with an exponent, such as `1e5`, as a string unless it
  has a decimal point and a signed exponent (`1.5e+5`).

## JSON Lines

```sh
epx products list --stream > products.jsonl
epx orders list --query status:CREATED --stream | jq -r .id
```

`--stream` prints each item on its own line as compact JSON as soon as its page is read
and checked. Long lists start printing at once and aren't held in memory.

- Most list commands take `--stream`; `epx <command> --help` shows whether one does.
- It works with `--limit`, `--query`, and `--sort`, but not with `-o`, `--columns`, or
  `--no-headers`.
- It reads up to 10,000 pages, where other lists stop at 1,000.
- The [paging checks](/emporix-cli/guides/lists#how-paging-works) still run. If a later page fails a
  check, the command exits with code 1 after printing the pages before it. Without
  `--stream`, a list prints nothing unless every check passes.

## Translations

Emporix stores many texts, such as names and descriptions, per language. epx requests
every translation, so `-o json` shows them all. Commands whose tables show text take
`--language` to choose the translation shown. It defaults to `en`, or to your profile's
default language.

```sh
epx products list --language nl
epx catalogs get AcmeStore_catalog --language de
```

When an item has no text in that language, the table shows another translation labeled
with its language, such as `Transistors (fr)`.

## Files

```sh
epx quotes pdf Q1001 --out Q1001.pdf --language de
epx quotes pdf Q1001 --out - | lpr
```

[`epx quotes pdf`](/emporix-cli/commands/quotes#epx-quotes-pdf) saves the quote's PDF with `--out`
instead of printing it. `--out -` writes the file to standard
output, but only when standard output isn't a terminal. epx writes the file readable by
you only, and replaces an existing file only once the new one is complete.

## Secrets in output

  JSON, YAML, `epx api`, and writes print every value of a response, secrets included:
  API keys of search providers, payment provider credentials, secured settings, card
  tokens, and webhook destinations. Handle such output, and any file you save it to, as a
  secret.

Characters that a terminal could act on, such as escape sequences, are replaced with
spaces in tables, CSV, and error messages, and escaped in JSON and YAML. See the
[security model](/emporix-cli/security#output).

# List, filter, and sort

> Read every page of a list, and narrow it with a limit, a query, and a sort order.

Commands that list items, such as `list`, `search`, and `categories subcategories ID`,
read every page of the collection and print the items together. You never write paging
code: narrow the list with flags instead.

```sh
epx products list --query 'name.en:~shirt published:true' --sort code:desc --limit 20
```

## Limit results

```sh
epx products list --sort metadataCreatedAt:desc --limit 10
```

`--limit` prints at most that many items. Paged reads stop requesting pages as soon as
they safely can. `--limit 0`, the default, prints every item.

  When a limited list spans several pages, end `--sort` with a unique field, such as
  `code:desc,id`. Items that share a sort value may come back in a different order on
  each page.

## Filter with a query

```sh
epx products list --query published:false
epx products list --query 'code:(A1,A2)'
epx orders count --query status:CREATED
```

`--query` filters with the Emporix
[q parameter](https://developer.emporix.io/api-documentation/standard-practices/q-param),
passed as given. Conditions separated by spaces must all match; quote the filter so your
shell keeps it in one piece.

Emporix rejects a malformed filter, but not an unknown field name, which may match
nothing or everything. When a command already filters with a query of its own, your
`--query` is added to it, so it can only narrow the result.

### Search commands

`search` commands, such as `products search`, send the query in the body of a POST
request that changes nothing, and print their results as the matching list does. Pass
`--body FILE` to send a whole JSON body instead of `--query`, or `--body -` to read it
from standard input.

## Sort results

```sh
epx products list --sort code:desc
epx categories list --sort 'name.en,code'
```

`--sort` orders a list with the Emporix sort parameter, passed as given: fields separated
by commas, each optionally followed by `:asc` or `:desc`.

## Which lists take which flags

Each list supports what its Emporix service supports. `epx <command> --help` shows the
flags of a command.

| Flags | Lists |
| --- | --- |
| `--query` and `--sort` | Most lists, such as products, categories, prices, customers, orders, coupons, segments, and IAM groups. |
| `--sort` only | Catalogs, units, currencies, countries, regions, taxes, price models, payment transactions, and IAM roles and permissions. |
| `--query` only | `changelog list` and `orders count`. |
| `--limit` only | Lists that Emporix neither filters nor sorts, such as configurations, fees, shipping zones, payment modes, and category trees. |

Field names for `--query` and `--sort` are mostly those of `-o json`, but not always.
Products, for example, sort by creation date as `metadataCreatedAt`. Check the
[Emporix API reference](https://developer.emporix.io/api-references) of the service.

## How paging works

A list reads 100 items per page, up to 1,000 pages (10,000 with
[`--stream`](/emporix-cli/guides/output#json-lines)). It fails with exit code 1 when paging is visibly
inconsistent: an item read twice, or a count that differs from the total Emporix
reports. Without `--stream`, it prints nothing unless every check passes.

Like any paged read, a list can't notice an item that changes while its pages are read.

Some services need a different read, and the command's help says so:

- Collections that Emporix returns whole, such as category trees and configurations, are
  read with one request.
- Some lists can't check their total, because Emporix sends none or fails when asked for
  it. An item that moves between pages while they're read can then show twice or be
  missed.
- Emporix orders countries and IAM users differently on every request, so epx reads each
  as one page. IAM users fit in one page of up to 500; on a tenant with more,
  `iam users list` fails.
- The change history (`changelog list`) covers the last 30 days unless you filter on
  `occurredAt`. On an active tenant, read a closed range in the past, or use `--limit`.

# Call any API endpoint

> Send a request to any Emporix API path with epx api, using only the OAuth scopes you name.

`epx api` sends a request to any Emporix API path and prints the response as JSON. Use it
for endpoints that have no command of their own, or to see a raw page of a collection.
The [API coverage](/emporix-cli/coverage) lists, per service, which operations have a command.

```sh
epx api get '/site/{tenant}/sites'
epx api get '/product/{tenant}/products/100200' --scope product.product_read_unpublished
```

## Send a GET request

```sh
epx api get '/product/{tenant}/products' -p pageSize=5 --scope product.product_read_unpublished
```

`epx api get PATH` reads one response: it doesn't page, filter, or print a table. It
prints the body as JSON with sorted keys and every value as sent, or as YAML with
`-o yaml`.

### Paths

A path starts with `/` and goes to your configured API host. epx refuses a full URL or
another host. It replaces `{tenant}` with your tenant, so quote the path to keep your
shell from expanding the braces.

### Query parameters

Add query parameters inline (`'/product/{tenant}/products?pageSize=5'`) or with
`-p key=value`, which you can repeat. A `-p` value replaces an inline value of the same
key.

### Scopes

`--scope` requests a scope for the token, and you can repeat it. Emporix only grants the
scopes a token asks for, and may silently return less data otherwise, so name every scope
the endpoint needs. If your API key lacks one, epx fails with exit code 3 before it sends
the request.

`epx api get` requests exactly the scopes you name, and it only ever sends GET, so it
doesn't need `--allow-write-scope`.

## Send a write

```sh
epx api post '/product/{tenant}/products' --scope product.product_manage --file product.json --dry-run
epx api delete '/product/{tenant}/products/100200' --scope product.product_manage
```

`epx api post`, `put`, `patch`, and `delete` send a write to any path, with the same
paths, query parameters, and scopes as `epx api get`. Like every write, they take their
body from `--file`, show the exact request with `--dry-run`, and ask before they send.
See [Change data](/emporix-cli/guides/writes).

`epx api` sends no headers of its own beyond the standard ones. A body with localized
text sent this way is sent without a `Content-Language` header; a write command of its
own sends the right one for its service.

## Responses and errors

| Situation | Exit code |
| --- | --- |
| Emporix answers with a 2xx status. | 0 |
| Your API key is rejected or lacks a scope. | 3 |
| Emporix answers 404, or an empty body to a GET. | 4 |
| Emporix answers 409 to a write. | 5 |
| The command is invalid: a full URL, a malformed `-p` or `--scope`, a body that isn't JSON, or a write without `--yes` where epx can't ask. Nothing was sent. | 2 |
| Any other error. | 1 |

See [Exit codes and scripting](/emporix-cli/guides/exit-codes) for the full list.

---

Source: https://commerce-cloud-integrations.github.io/emporix-cli/guides/writes/

# Change data

> Create, update, and delete data in your tenant with dry runs, confirmation, and explicit scopes.

Reads never change anything. Writes create, change, or delete data in your tenant, and
every write works the same way: it sends only what you give it, requests explicit
scopes, shows its exact request with `--dry-run`, and sends only once you confirm.

```sh
epx units create --file gram.json --dry-run   # show the request
epx units create --file gram.json             # send it after you confirm
```

## Write commands

Write commands are named after what they send:

| Command | Sends |
| --- | --- |
| `create` | A POST that creates an item. |
| `update ID` | A PUT that replaces an item. Some services also create a missing one. |
| `patch ID` | A PATCH that changes some fields of an item. |
| `delete ID` | A DELETE. |
| `bulk-create`, `bulk-update`, `bulk-patch`, `bulk-delete` | Many items in one request. See [Bulk writes](/emporix-cli/guides/bulk). |
| An action's verb, such as `reindex`, `capture`, or `redeem` | The action. |

The [CLI reference](/emporix-cli/commands) lists every write with its scopes. For an endpoint without
a command of its own, use [`epx api post|put|patch|delete`](/emporix-cli/guides/api#send-a-write).

## Provide a request body

```sh
epx prices update 6245aa0a78a8576e338fa9c4 --file price.json
jq -n '{active: false}' | epx sites patch AcmeStore_NL --file - --yes
```

`--file PATH` sends the JSON in a file byte for byte, and `--file -` reads it from
standard input. epx checks that it's one JSON value before anything else, and fails with
exit code 2 otherwise.

Some writes don't need a file:

- Writes with a small, fixed body build it from flags, such as
  `indexing reindex-jobs create --entity-type PRODUCT` or
  `orders transition ORDER_ID --status STATUS`. `--file` replaces those flags.
- A change of one configuration value is `configurations update KEY --file`, which sends the whole
  setting: `configurations get KEY -o json` shows it, to edit and send back.
- A delete of one item, and other writes that Emporix takes without a body, have no
  `--file`.
- Writes that upload a file, such as `schemas references create --json-schema PATH`,
  send a multipart form.

Each command's help shows which flags make its body.

### Localized text

Writes whose body holds localized text, such as a product's name, send a
`Content-Language` header. By default, `--content-language *`, each text is a map of
translations, as `-o json` prints it:

```json
{ "name": { "en": "Gram", "de": "Gramm" } }
```

With a language code, such as `--content-language en`, each text is a string in that
language. Some services refuse strings, so their writes take maps only and have no
`--content-language`. A few, such as the Shipping Service, refuse `Content-Language: *`,
so their writes send maps without the header. Each command's help says how it sends
text.

## Preview with a dry run

```sh
epx api put '/product/{tenant}/products/100200' --scope product.product_manage \
  --file product.json --dry-run
```

`--dry-run` prints the exact request and exits with code 0. It doesn't request a token
for the write and sends nothing. Every write works this way, with no read first.

```text
PUT https://api.emporix.io/product/acme1/products/100200
Accept: application/json
Accept-Language: *
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: emporix-cli/...

{"code":"100200", ...}
```

The output shows the method, the full URL with your tenant and query, every header except
`Authorization`, and the body. For a multipart form, it shows each part's name, file
name, content type, and size, and the content of JSON parts. A dry run still needs your
[API key settings](/emporix-cli/configure), because it shows the request for your tenant.

## Confirm a write

On a terminal, epx asks before it sends:

```text
Send PUT https://api.emporix.io/product/acme1/products/100200 to tenant acme1? [y/N]
```

Only `y` or `yes` sends the request. Any other answer sends nothing, and the command
fails with `not confirmed; nothing was sent` and exit code 1.

A delete can't be undone, so `y` isn't enough: you type what it deletes, as the prompt
shows. A delete of many items in one request says so:

```text
Send DELETE https://api.emporix.io/category/acme1/categories/c1/assignments to tenant acme1? It deletes the assignments of every product to the category with one request and cannot be undone: type c1 to confirm:
```

### Skip the confirmation

`--yes` sends without asking. epx requires it, and fails with exit code 2 before sending
anything, when it can't ask:

- Standard input isn't a terminal, as in scripts, pipelines, and CI jobs.
- The body comes from standard input (`--file -`).

## Scopes

A write requests only the write scopes of its operation, which its help names. Some
flags add a scope their query parameter needs, and the help says so. For example,
`categories create --publish` adds `category.category_publish`.

`epx api` writes request only the scopes you name with `--scope`.

If your API key lacks a scope, epx fails with exit code 3 before it sends the write.

## Read the response

epx prints the response body as JSON (or YAML with `-o yaml`) with sorted keys and every
value as sent. An empty response, such as a 204 No Content, prints nothing. Any 2xx
status is a success.

Payment operations, such as `payment-transactions capture`, are the exception: Emporix
answers with `successful`, which says whether the payment provider carried out the
operation. epx exits with code 1 unless it's `true`.

## Handle failures

| Failure | Exit code | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Conflict: the item changed since you read it, or already exists. | 5 | Read the item again, apply your change to its current state, and send it again. |
| The write may have been carried out: a 500, 502, 503, or 504 answer, or a network failure after the connection was made. | 1 | Read the item to check whether the change was made before you retry. The error says `it may have been carried out all the same`. |
| Authentication or a missing scope. | 3 | Fix the API key, or add the scope the help names. Emporix didn't carry out the write. |
| Not found. | 4 | Check the ID. |

Most services that check `metadata.version` answer a stale version with a conflict
(exit code 5), so a write sent with the version you read never overwrites someone else's
change. The Unit and Catalog services answer it with 404, which epx reports as a conflict
when your body carries `metadata.version`. Some services answer it as not found or as a
bad request instead; the command's help says how.

### No repeats

epx never sends a write again once it may have reached Emporix, whatever its method. It
retries only when Emporix certainly didn't act: after 429 Too Many Requests, honoring
`Retry-After` up to 30 seconds, or when the connection couldn't be made. It sends a
request at most three times.

## Best practices

- Run every new write with `--dry-run` first, and check the URL, tenant, and body.
- Try writes on a test tenant before you run them on a tenant that serves customers.
- Use an API key with only the write scopes you need, and keep write scopes off the keys
  your read-only scripts use.
- Read an item right before you change it, and send its `metadata.version` where the
  service checks it.
- In scripts, pass `--yes` explicitly and check the exit code.

---

Source: https://commerce-cloud-integrations.github.io/emporix-cli/guides/bulk/

# Bulk writes, chains, and jobs

> Write many items in one request, import files of any size, run cart command chains, and wait for jobs.

Some writes change many items at once, or start work that Emporix finishes later. They
follow the same rules as [every write](/emporix-cli/guides/writes), and they report each item that
failed so you know exactly what to send again.

## Bulk writes

```sh
epx availability bulk-update --file stock.json --dry-run
epx categories assignments bulk-create c1 --file assignments.json --yes
```

`bulk-create`, `bulk-update`, `bulk-patch`, and `bulk-delete` send a JSON array of items
to the service's bulk endpoint in one request. Each service takes a maximum number of
items per request, such as 200 for prices, products, and availability. epx refuses a
larger array with exit code 2 before sending anything.

Emporix carries out each item on its own and answers with the result of each. A few bulk
writes, such as `price-lists prices bulk-delete`, are answered as a whole; their help says
so. epx prints the response, and when items failed, it lists each one on standard error by its position
in your array (from 0) and its ID:

```text
item 3 (p-17): 409 Conflict: ...
```

The items that didn't fail were carried out. The command exits with the code the
failures share: 5 when each was a conflict, 4 when each wasn't found, 3 when each was
refused for a scope, and 1 otherwise.

  An item that failed with 500, 502, 503, or 504 may have been carried out all the same,
  as its line says. Read it before you send it again.

## Import products

```sh
epx products import --file products.json --dry-run
epx products import --file products.json --yes
```

`products import` takes a JSON array of any number of products and sends them in requests
of up to 200, in order. `--dry-run` prints every request, and the confirmation says how
many requests it sends.

epx lists the products that failed by their position in the whole file, and goes on
with the next request. If a request fails as a whole, the import stops and says from
which product on nothing was sent.

## Cart command chains

```sh
epx carts execute CART_ID --file commands.json
```

[`epx carts execute`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-execute) sends up to 10 cart commands,
which Emporix runs in order on one cart. By default, Emporix stops at the first command
that fails but keeps what the commands before it changed; pass `--on-error resume` to run
the rest anyway.

When a command fails, epx lists it by its position and type, says how many commands
didn't run, and exits with the code the failures share:

```text
command 1 (UpdateCartItem): 404 Not Found: ...
```

## Wait for jobs

```sh
epx indexing reindex-jobs create --entity-type PRODUCT --rag --wait
epx search indexes update vehicle vehicles --file index.json --wait --yes
```

Writes that start a job, such as a reindex, print the job as Emporix answers it. Add
`--wait` to follow the job until it ends:

```text
reindex job j1: IN_PROGRESS (2000 of 5000)
```

epx reads the job every `--poll-interval` (default `5s`) and prints a line to standard
error whenever its status or progress changes, until the job ends or `--wait-timeout`
(default `30m`) passes. It then prints the job as last read and exits:

| Result | Exit code |
| --- | --- |
| The job ended successfully. | 0 |
| The job failed, or `--wait-timeout` passed first. The job keeps running, and the error names the command that reads it. | 1 |
| Reading the job failed. | The code of that read, such as 4 when it isn't found. |

`--wait` also requests the scope that reads the job, so a key without it fails with exit
code 3 before the write is sent. A long wait gets a new token before the old one
expires.

---

Source: https://commerce-cloud-integrations.github.io/emporix-cli/guides/exit-codes/

# Exit codes and scripting

> Use epx in scripts and CI: what each exit code means, how errors look, and how epx retries.

epx is built for scripts. Output goes to standard output, errors go to standard error,
and the exit code tells you what went wrong, so a script can tell a missing product from
a missing scope.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Success | The command printed its result. |
| `1` | Error | Emporix answered with an error such as 400 or 500, a network failure or timeout, a [paging check](/emporix-cli/guides/lists#how-paging-works) that failed, a declined confirmation, or a write that may have been carried out. |
| `2` | Invalid usage or configuration | An unknown command or flag, a bad flag value, missing API key settings, a body that isn't JSON, or a write without `--yes` where epx can't ask. Nothing was sent. |
| `3` | Authentication failed or scopes missing | Emporix rejected the API key, the token belongs to another tenant, a scope wasn't granted, or Emporix answered 401 or 403. |
| `4` | Not found | Emporix doesn't know the item, such as `epx products get` with an unknown ID. |
| `5` | Conflict | Emporix answered a write with 409 Conflict: the item changed since you read it, or already exists. A stale version sent to `units update` or `catalogs patch`, and a bulk write whose failed items were all conflicts, exit 5 too. Read the item again before you retry. |

  Some commands get a 403 from Emporix that refuses their input rather than the
  credential, such as `orders transition` to a status the order can't take. These exit
  with 1 and show Emporix's message, unless the message names a scope or permission.
  Their help says so.

## Errors

Errors start with `Error:` and go to standard error. When Emporix answers with JSON, epx
shows its message, its error code, and the details of each field, and nothing else of the
response:

```text
Error: 400 Bad Request: The request violates validation constraints. (ENTITY-400001) (name: must not be blank)
```

Usage errors (exit code 2) add a hint to run `epx --help`.

## Retries

epx retries a request, up to three times in total, only when it can't change data twice:

- Any request after 429 Too Many Requests, honoring `Retry-After` up to 30 seconds.
- Any request whose connection couldn't be made, unless making it timed out.
- Reads, never writes, after 502, 503, or 504.

## Script examples

### Check whether a product exists

```sh
if epx products get 100200 -o json > product.json; then
  echo "found"
else
  case $? in
    4) echo "no such product" ;;
    3) echo "check the API key and its scopes" ;;
    2) echo "check the command or the environment" ;;
    *) echo "failed" ;;
  esac
fi
```

### Handle a conflict

```sh
jq -n '{active: false}' | epx api patch '/site/{tenant}/sites/AcmeStore_NL' \
  --scope site.site_manage --file - --yes
case $? in
  0) echo "done" ;;
  5) echo "the site changed meanwhile: read it again"; exit 5 ;;
  *) echo "failed: read the site before you send it again"; exit 1 ;;
esac
```

### Fail early on a missing scope

```sh
epx auth status --scope order.order_read > /dev/null || exit
epx orders count --query status:CREATED -o json
```

### Run in CI

```sh
export EMPORIX_TENANT=acme1
export EMPORIX_CLIENT_ID="$CI_EMPORIX_CLIENT_ID"
export EMPORIX_CLIENT_SECRET="$CI_EMPORIX_CLIENT_SECRET"
epx products list -o json > products.json
```

In CI, set the `EMPORIX_` variables from your CI system's secrets. Profiles keep their
client secret in an OS keychain, which CI runners usually don't have. See
[Authenticate](/emporix-cli/configure).

---

Source: https://commerce-cloud-integrations.github.io/emporix-cli/security/

# Security model

> How epx handles credentials, OAuth scopes, network requests, and the data it prints.

epx works with live commerce data, so it's designed to do only what you ask, with only the
access you grant. This page describes the guarantees it makes.

## Reads change nothing

Every read command only reads, including those that Emporix serves as POST or PUT, such
as searches, shipping quotes, and coupon validation.

## Writes are explicit

Every [write](/emporix-cli/guides/writes) sends only what you give it, shows its exact request with
`--dry-run`, and asks before it sends. A delete asks you to type what it deletes. In
scripts, writes require `--yes`. epx never sends a write again once it may have reached
Emporix.

## Least privilege

Every command requests a token with only the OAuth scopes it needs, and its help names
them. Emporix silently drops a scope your API key lacks and then returns less data, so
epx checks every token it receives:

- When a scope is missing, the command fails with exit code 3.
- When the token belongs to another tenant, the command fails with exit code 3.
- epx never falls back to broader scopes.

Reads that Emporix allows only with a write-capable scope request it only when you pass
`--allow-write-scope`. See [Authenticate](/emporix-cli/configure#write-capable-scopes-for-reads).

## Credentials

- epx reads its API key from environment variables or from a
  [profile](/emporix-cli/configure#store-keys-in-profiles), never from flags.
- A profile's client secret is stored in the OS keychain, never in a file.
- epx never prints its token or client secret.
- When epx rejects a setting, such as an API URL without HTTPS or an invalid tenant, the
  error names the rule, not the value, in case you put a credential in the wrong variable.

## Network

- Requests go only to the configured API host, over HTTPS. Plain HTTP is allowed only for
  a loopback address, for testing.
- epx never follows redirects.

## Output

epx prints responses as Emporix sends them, without redacting anything. JSON, YAML,
`epx api`, and writes print secrets that a response holds, such as API keys, payment
provider credentials, and secured settings. Tables and CSV show only their columns, but
those print values as sent too, such as the value of a secured setting.

Text from Emporix can hold characters that a terminal acts on, such as control
characters, escape sequences, bidirectional overrides, and zero-width characters. epx
replaces them with spaces in tables, CSV, and error messages, and escapes them in JSON
and YAML, where the document still decodes to the same data.

---

Source: https://commerce-cloud-integrations.github.io/emporix-cli/commands/index/

# CLI reference

> Every epx command and flag, with the OAuth scopes each one requests.

This reference documents every command and flag of epx. The same text is in `epx <command> --help`.

Command-line client for the Emporix Commerce APIs.

Credentials are read from the environment:

```text
EMPORIX_TENANT, EMPORIX_CLIENT_ID, EMPORIX_CLIENT_SECRET (and optionally EMPORIX_API_URL).
```

Where none of these is set, a profile ([`epx profile add`](/emporix-cli/commands/profile#epx-profile-add)) gives them, its client secret from the
OS keychain: the profile that `--profile` names, else EPX\_PROFILE, else the default profile ([`epx profile use`](/emporix-cli/commands/profile#epx-profile-use)). The two never mix, and naming a profile while one is set is a usage error.
`--tenant` overrides the tenant of either. A profile's default site and language apply where a
command needs a site or shows translations and the flag is not given, on the profile's tenant.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 invalid usage or configuration,
3 authentication or missing scopes, 4 not found, 5 conflict: a write that Emporix answered with
409 Conflict, as when the item changed since it was read or exists already, or a `units update`
or `catalogs patch` with metadata.version answered with 404 Not Found, as the Unit and Catalog
services answer a stale version. A 403 Forbidden that the help of a command calls a refusal
of its input exits 1.

## Global flags

Every command takes these flags.

- `-h, --help`\
  Help for epx.
- `--profile <name>`\
  Profile to use (default from EPX\_PROFILE, else the default profile).
- `--tenant <string>`\
  Emporix tenant (default from EMPORIX\_TENANT, else the profile).
- `--timeout <duration>`\
  Timeout for each HTTP request. Default: `30s`.

# epx ai

> Read and change AI agents and their setup, chat with them, generate texts.

## epx ai

Reads the AI Service's agents and what they are built from: agent templates, tools, tokens,
OAuth configurations and MCP servers, the LLM models of the supported providers and the
commerce events that can trigger an agent; what agents did: their jobs, conversations,
request and session logs and analytics; and which fields the AI RAG Indexer embeds.
Upserts, changes and deletes agents and what they are built from, exports and imports
agents, chats with them and generates texts, which consumes AI credits. [`epx ai rag reindex`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-rag-reindex) embeds the entities of a type again.

Its reads require the ai.agent\_read scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx ai [flags]`, `epx ai [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx ai agents`](#epx-ai-agents)\
  Read, create, upsert, change, delete, export and import AI agents.
- [`epx ai analytics`](#epx-ai-analytics)\
  Read the analytics of agents.
- [`epx ai chat`](#epx-ai-chat)\
  Send a message to an agent and print its reply (consumes AI credits).
- [`epx ai chat-async`](#epx-ai-chat-async)\
  Send a message to an agent, which replies in a job (consumes AI credits).
- [`epx ai commerce-events`](#epx-ai-commerce-events)\
  List the commerce events that can trigger an agent.
- [`epx ai conversations`](#epx-ai-conversations)\
  Read agent conversations.
- [`epx ai generate-completion`](#epx-ai-generate-completion)\
  Generate the next message of a chat history (consumes AI credits).
- [`epx ai generate-text`](#epx-ai-generate-text)\
  Generate a text from a prompt (consumes AI credits).
- [`epx ai jobs`](#epx-ai-jobs)\
  Read and delete agent jobs.
- [`epx ai logs`](#epx-ai-logs)\
  Read the logs of agent requests and sessions.
- [`epx ai mcp-servers`](#epx-ai-mcp-servers)\
  Read, upsert, change and delete MCP servers.
- [`epx ai models`](#epx-ai-models)\
  List the LLM models that agents can use.
- [`epx ai oauths`](#epx-ai-oauths)\
  Read, upsert, change and delete OAuth configurations.
- [`epx ai rag`](#epx-ai-rag)\
  Read which fields the AI RAG Indexer embeds and filters by; reindex.
- [`epx ai templates`](#epx-ai-templates)\
  Read agent templates.
- [`epx ai tokens`](#epx-ai-tokens)\
  Read, upsert, change and delete AI tokens.
- [`epx ai tools`](#epx-ai-tools)\
  Read, upsert, change and delete agent tools.

## epx ai agents attach

Attach a file to a chat with an agent.

Uploads the file that `--upload` names (jpg, jpeg, png, pdf, csv, text or txt), or assigns the
media asset that `--media` names ([`epx media list`](/emporix-cli/commands/media#epx-media-list)), to the agent AGENT\_ID, the ID that
[`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows, in the session that `--session` names, or a new one. Emporix
answers with the attachment's id and the sessionId, which [`epx ai chat`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-chat) with that agent
takes as `--attachment` and `--session`.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agentexecution\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents attach AGENT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--media <ID>`\
  The ID of a media asset to attach.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--session <ID>`\
  The ID of the session to go on with, the sessionId of an earlier chat or attachment; without it, a new one.
- `--upload <PATH>`\
  The file in PATH to upload (up to 30 MB including the form), sent with its name.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai agents attach complaint-agent --upload order.pdf --yes
```

## epx ai agents create

Create an agent from a template.

Creates an agent from the agent template TEMPLATE\_ID, the ID that [`epx ai templates list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-templates-list)
shows, which must be enabled, with the JSON in `--file`: its name and description, its
userPrompt and, optionally, its id. Emporix answers with the id of the agent.

Localized text in the body, such as a name, is a map of translations, e.g.
`{"en": "gram", "de": "Gramm"}`, as `-o json` of a read prints it, or with `--content-language`
LANGUAGE a string in that language, e.g. `"gram"` with `--content-language` en.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents create TEMPLATE_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--content-language <LANGUAGE>`\
  The LANGUAGE of localized text in the body, or \* for maps of translations. Default: `*`.
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai agents create complaint-template --file agent.json --dry-run
```

## epx ai agents delete

Delete an agent.

Deletes the agent ID. Emporix refuses to delete one that others use, unless
`--force` unassigns it from them.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--force`\
  Delete it even where other agents collaborate with it.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai agents export

Export agents, which creates an export job.

Exports the agents that `--agent` names (up to 100) with the tools and MCP servers they use,
and prints the export: data, the agents base64-encoded, and its checksum, which
[`epx ai agents import`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-import) takes on another tenant. Emporix keeps each export as a job of type
EXPORT, the jobId of the response, which [`epx ai jobs get JOB_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-jobs-get) reads.
It changes data although Emporix needs no write-capable scope for it.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents export [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--agent <ID>`\
  The ID of an agent to export (repeatable; required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai agents export --agent complaint-agent --yes > agents.json
```

- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.

  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

## epx ai agents list

List AI agents.

Reads AI agents: TYPE is generic, complaint or anti\_fraud, PROVIDER and MODEL the LLM an
agent uses and TRIGGERS what starts it (endpoint, slack, teams or commerce\_events). Their
prompts, tools and MCP servers are only in `-o json`.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, TYPE, ENABLED, PROVIDER, MODEL, TRIGGERS, NAME.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai agents patch

Change members of an agent.

Changes the agent ID with the JSON array of operations in `--file`, each with op
(ADD, REMOVE or REPLACE), path and value, e.g.
`[{"op": "REPLACE", "path": "/enabled", "value": false}]`; its other members keep their
values.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents patch ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai agents search

Search AI agents.

Reads the AI agents that an Emporix q filter finds (`--query`; without it,
every one).
It reads and shows them as [`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) does.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents search [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, TYPE, ENABLED, PROVIDER, MODEL, TRIGGERS, NAME.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai agents update

Upsert an agent.

Replaces the agent ID with the JSON in `--file`, or creates it with that ID where
none exists (an upsert): Emporix answers with the id of one it created and nothing for one it
replaced. With metadata.version, as [`epx ai agents get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-get) prints it,
Emporix replaces only that version: another is a conflict (exit 5).
The JSON holds its name and description, userPrompt, llmConfig, triggers and mcpServers,
and its nativeTools, agentCollaborations, enabledMemory and maxRecursionLimit.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows.

Localized text in the body, such as a name, is a map of translations, e.g.
`{"en": "gram", "de": "Gramm"}`, as `-o json` of a read prints it, or with `--content-language`
LANGUAGE a string in that language, e.g. `"gram"` with `--content-language` en.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai agents update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--content-language <LANGUAGE>`\
  The LANGUAGE of localized text in the body, or \* for maps of translations. Default: `*`.
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai analytics

Read the analytics of agents.

Reads what Emporix counts of the requests and sessions of agents, as its dashboards show them.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai analytics [flags]`, `epx ai analytics [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

  Show the request and session totals of one agent.
- [`epx ai analytics executions`](#epx-ai-analytics-executions)\

- [`epx ai analytics tenant`](#epx-ai-analytics-tenant)\
  Show the request and session totals of every agent.

## epx ai analytics agent

Show the request and session totals of one agent.

Reads the totals of the requests and sessions of one agent: AGENT\_ID is the ID that
[`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows; an unknown one counts nothing.
LOGS is requests or sessions, TOTAL how many there were in the last four weeks, WARNING and
ERROR how many of them had that severity and ERROR RATE their share with errors, as Emporix
computes it. The requests per session and the weekly trends are only in `-o json`.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai analytics agent AGENT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among LOGS, TOTAL, WARNING, ERROR, ERROR RATE.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai analytics executions

List how often agents ran per calendar quarter, month or week.

Reads how often agents ran (their sessions) per calendar quarter, Emporix's default
granularity, or per month or week (`--granularity`): each PERIOD that Emporix reports runs
from FROM (inclusive) to TO (exclusive), in UTC. AGENT\_IDS are the IDs that
[`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows, separated by commas without spaces (at most 100); an unknown
one ran 0 times.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai analytics executions AGENT_IDS [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among AGENT, PERIOD, FROM, TO, EXECUTIONS.
- `--granularity <period>`\
  The calendar period of each count: QUARTER, MONTH or WEEK.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai chat

Send a message to an agent and print its reply (consumes AI credits).

Sends the message that `--message` gives to the agent `--agent`, and prints its reply: the messages
of the agent and of those it collaborates with, each with the sessionId that `--session` takes to
go on.
A reply may take longer than the `--timeout` of a request (30s by default): then give a longer
one, e.g. `--timeout` 5m, or use chat-async.
It consumes AI credits: the LLM tokens of the agent's model, and of the agents it
collaborates with.
With `--session`, the chat goes on in that session, which the agent remembers where its
enabledMemory is true; an attachment must be one of the session, attached to the same agent
([`epx ai agents attach`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-attach)). `--file` gives the body instead, with the caption and purpose of
each attachment.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agentexecution\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai chat [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--agent <ID>`\
  The ID of the agent, as [`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows it (required without `--file`).
- `--attachment <ID>`\
  The ID of an attachment of the session to send with the message, as [`epx ai agents attach`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-attach) prints it (repeatable) (only with `--session`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--message <TEXT>`\
  The TEXT to send to the agent (required without `--file`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--session <ID>`\
  The ID of the session to go on with, the sessionId of an earlier chat or attachment; without it, a new one.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai chat --agent complaint-agent --message "Find order EON1243" --yes
```

## epx ai chat-async

Send a message to an agent, which replies in a job (consumes AI credits).

Sends the message that `--message` gives to the agent `--agent`, which replies in a job of type
AGENT\_CHAT: Emporix answers with its jobId, which [`epx ai jobs get JOB_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-jobs-get) reads.
It consumes AI credits: the LLM tokens of the agent's model, and of the agents it
collaborates with.
With `--session`, the chat goes on in that session, which the agent remembers where its
enabledMemory is true; an attachment must be one of the session, attached to the same agent
([`epx ai agents attach`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-attach)). `--file` gives the body instead, with the caption and purpose of
each attachment.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agentexecution\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai chat-async [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--agent <ID>`\
  The ID of the agent, as [`epx ai agents list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-list) shows it (required without `--file`).
- `--attachment <ID>`\
  The ID of an attachment of the session to send with the message, as [`epx ai agents attach`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-agents-attach) prints it (repeatable) (only with `--session`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--message <TEXT>`\
  The TEXT to send to the agent (required without `--file`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--session <ID>`\
  The ID of the session to go on with, the sessionId of an earlier chat or attachment; without it, a new one.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai chat-async --agent complaint-agent --message "Find order EON1243" --yes
```

## epx ai commerce-events

List the commerce events that can trigger an agent.

Reads the commerce events that can start an agent with a commerce\_events trigger, sorted.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai commerce-events [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among EVENT.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai conversations

Read agent conversations.

Reads the conversations of agents in Microsoft Teams channels and group chats: ID is the
conversation in Teams, NAME its channel or chat, SESSION the agent's session ([`epx ai logs sessions get`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-logs-sessions-get)) and LAST MESSAGE when it was last active. The channel and the context
reference are only in `-o json`.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai conversations [flags]`, `epx ai conversations [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx ai conversations list`](#epx-ai-conversations-list)\
  List agent conversations.
- [`epx ai conversations search`](#epx-ai-conversations-search)\
  Search agent conversations.

## epx ai conversations list

List agent conversations.

Reads the conversations of agents in Microsoft Teams channels and group chats: ID is the
conversation in Teams, NAME its channel or chat, SESSION the agent's session ([`epx ai logs sessions get`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-logs-sessions-get)) and LAST MESSAGE when it was last active. The channel and the context
reference are only in `-o json`.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai conversations list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, AGENT, SESSION, LAST MESSAGE.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).

## epx ai generate-completion

Generate the next message of a chat history (consumes AI credits).

Generates the next message of the chat history that `--message` gives, one message per
`--message` in their order, and prints it as result.
It consumes AI credits: the LLM tokens of the tenant's own OpenAI account where the tenant
configuration openAiApiToken holds its token, or else Emporix's, of which a tenant may use
3 million input and 1 million output tokens.
A reply may take longer than the `--timeout` of a request (30s by default): then give a longer
one, e.g. `--timeout` 5m.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.completion\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai generate-completion [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--message <ROLE:TEXT>`\
  A message of the chat history as ROLE:TEXT, ROLE SYSTEM, USER or ASSISTANT (repeatable; required without `--file`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai generate-completion --message "SYSTEM:You write product texts" \
  --message "USER:Describe product 100200"
```

## epx ai generate-text

Generate a text from a prompt (consumes AI credits).

Generates a text from the prompt that `--prompt` gives, such as a product description, and
prints it as result.
It consumes AI credits: the LLM tokens of the tenant's own OpenAI account where the tenant
configuration openAiApiToken holds its token, or else Emporix's, of which a tenant may use
3 million input and 1 million output tokens.
A reply may take longer than the `--timeout` of a request (30s by default): then give a longer
one, e.g. `--timeout` 5m.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.text\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai generate-text [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--max-tokens <TOKENS>`\
  The most LLM TOKENS to use (Emporix: 4097 without it).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--prompt <TEXT>`\
  The TEXT that asks for the text (required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai generate-text --prompt "Describe product 100200 in German" --max-tokens 500
```

## epx ai jobs

Read and delete agent jobs.

Reads the jobs of the AI Service: TYPE is AGENT\_CHAT (an agent's run), IMPORT or EXPORT (of
agents), STATUS in\_progress, success, failure or skipped, AGENT and SESSION the agent that
ran and its session ([`epx ai logs sessions get`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-logs-sessions-get)) and EVENT the commerce event that started
it. The agent's message and an import's or export's result are only in `-o json`.

Its reads require the ai.agent\_read scope.
Its writes require the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai jobs [flags]`, `epx ai jobs [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx ai jobs delete`](#epx-ai-jobs-delete)\
  Delete an agent job.
- [`epx ai jobs get`](#epx-ai-jobs-get)\
  Show one agent job.
- [`epx ai jobs list`](#epx-ai-jobs-list)\
  List agent jobs.
- [`epx ai jobs search`](#epx-ai-jobs-search)\
  Search agent jobs.

## epx ai jobs delete

Delete an agent job.

Deletes the agent job ID.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai jobs list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-jobs-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai jobs delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai logs requests

Read agent request logs.

Reads the logs of the requests to agents, one per request: ID is the log that get takes,
REQUEST the request it logs and SESSION the session it belongs to.
AGENT is the agent that was called, SEVERITY INFO, WARNING or ERROR, MESSAGES how many
messages were logged (empty when a log comes without them) and SECONDS how long it took; the
messages, the other agents that took part and the LLM tokens used are only in `-o json`.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai logs requests [flags]`, `epx ai logs requests [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).
