## epx ai mcp-servers patch

Change members of an MCP server.

Changes the MCP server ID with the JSON array of operations in `--file`, each with op
(ADD, REMOVE or REPLACE), path and value, e.g.
`[{"op": "REPLACE", "path": "/enabled", "value": false}]`; its other members keep their
values.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai mcp-servers list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-mcp-servers-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai mcp-servers patch ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `--force`\
  Disable it even where enabled agents use it, which disables them too.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai mcp-servers update

Upsert an MCP server.

Replaces the MCP server ID with the JSON in `--file`, or creates it with that ID where
none exists (an upsert): Emporix answers with the id of one it created and nothing for one it
replaced. With metadata.version, as [`epx ai mcp-servers get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-mcp-servers-get) prints it,
Emporix replaces only that version: another is a conflict (exit 5).
The JSON holds its type (custom: config with the server's url; dynamic: its tools), name
and transport, and whether it is enabled.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai mcp-servers list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-mcp-servers-list) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai mcp-servers update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `--force`\
  Disable it even where enabled agents use it, which disables them too.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

prints the response as Emporix sends it.

- [`epx ai oauths update`](#epx-ai-oauths-update)\

## epx ai rag

Read which fields the AI RAG Indexer embeds and filters by; reindex.

Reads the AI RAG Indexer, which embeds the entities of a type in a vector database for the
retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) tools of agents: the fields it can embed and those a
vector search can filter by; and embeds the entities of a type again.

Its reads require the ai.agent\_read scope.
Its writes require the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai rag [flags]`, `epx ai rag [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx ai rag fields`](#epx-ai-rag-fields)\
  List the fields of an entity type that can be embedded for RAG search.
- [`epx ai rag filter-fields`](#epx-ai-rag-filter-fields)\
  List the fields of an entity type that a vector search can filter by.
- [`epx ai rag reindex`](#epx-ai-rag-reindex)\
  Embed every entity of a type again for RAG search (deprecated by Emporix).

## epx ai rag fields

List the fields of an entity type that can be embedded for RAG search.

Reads the fields of an entity type, by path, that the AI RAG Indexer can embed.
TYPE is PRODUCT, ORDER or a custom entity type ([`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list)). The fields come whole, so they are read with one
request.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai rag fields TYPE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among FIELD.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai rag reindex

Embed every entity of a type again for RAG search (deprecated by Emporix).

Embeds every entity of a type again in the vector database, replacing its records there;
it sends no body. Emporix has deprecated this endpoint: [`epx indexing reindex-jobs create`](/emporix-cli/commands/indexing#epx-indexing-reindex-jobs-create)
with `--rag` starts a reindex job that embeds products too, which its `--wait` follows.
TYPE is PRODUCT, ORDER or a custom entity type ([`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list)). Emporix answers an unknown TYPE with 204 No Content (exit 0),
so check the TYPE first.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai rag reindex TYPE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx ai rag reindex PRODUCT --dry-run
```

## epx ai templates

Read agent templates.

Reads agent templates, from which agents are made: TYPE is generic, complaint or anti\_fraud,
PROVIDER and MODEL the LLM a template uses. Emporix reads no single template:
[`epx ai templates list --query id:ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-templates-list) shows one.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai templates [flags]`, `epx ai templates [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx ai templates list`](#epx-ai-templates-list)\
  List agent templates.
- [`epx ai templates search`](#epx-ai-templates-search)\
  Search agent templates.

## epx ai templates list

List agent templates.

Reads agent templates, from which agents are made: TYPE is generic, complaint or anti\_fraud,
PROVIDER and MODEL the LLM a template uses. Emporix reads no single template:
[`epx ai templates list --query id:ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-templates-list) shows one.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai templates list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, TYPE, ENABLED, PROVIDER, MODEL, NAME.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai templates search

Search agent templates.

Reads the agent templates that an Emporix q filter finds (`--query`; without it,
every one).
It reads and shows them as [`epx ai templates list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-templates-list) does.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.

Requires the ai.agent\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx ai templates search [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, TYPE, ENABLED, PROVIDER, MODEL, NAME.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai tokens

Read, upsert, change and delete AI tokens.

Reads the tokens that hold the API keys and secrets of LLMs, tools, OAuth configurations and
MCP servers, by name: the table shows no value, and the API reference documents none in a
response; `-o json` prints the response as Emporix sends it.

Its reads require the ai.agent\_read scope.
Its writes require the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai tokens [flags]`, `epx ai tokens [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx ai tokens delete`](#epx-ai-tokens-delete)\
  Delete an AI token.

  Show one token.
- [`epx ai tokens list`](#epx-ai-tokens-list)\
  List AI tokens.
- [`epx ai tokens patch`](#epx-ai-tokens-patch)\
  Change members of an AI token.
- [`epx ai tokens search`](#epx-ai-tokens-search)\
  Search AI tokens.
- [`epx ai tokens update`](#epx-ai-tokens-update)\
  Upsert an AI token.

## epx ai tokens delete

Delete an AI token.

Deletes the token ID. Emporix refuses to delete one that others use, unless
`--force` unassigns it from them.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai tokens list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-tokens-list) shows.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai tokens delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--force`\
  Delete it even where agents or MCP servers use it.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai tokens patch

Change members of an AI token.

Changes the token ID with the JSON array of operations in `--file`, each with op
(ADD, REMOVE or REPLACE), path and value, e.g.
`[{"op": "REPLACE", "path": "/enabled", "value": false}]`; its other members keep their
values.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai tokens list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-tokens-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai tokens patch ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx ai tokens update

Upsert an AI token.

Replaces the token ID with the JSON in `--file`, or creates it with that ID where
none exists (an upsert): Emporix answers with the id of one it created and nothing for one it
replaced. With metadata.version, as [`epx ai tokens get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-tokens-get) prints it,
Emporix replaces only that version: another is a conflict (exit 5).
The JSON holds its name and value, the API key or secret, which cannot change once the
token is created. A dry run prints the body, value included.
ID is the ID that [`epx ai tokens list`](/emporix-cli/commands/ai#epx-ai-tokens-list) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the ai.agent\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx ai tokens update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx api

> Send requests to any Emporix API path.

## epx api

**Command:** `epx api [flags]`, `epx api [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx api delete`](#epx-api-delete)\
  Send DELETE to an API path and print the JSON response.
- [`epx api get`](#epx-api-get)\
  GET an API path and print the JSON response.
- [`epx api patch`](#epx-api-patch)\
  Send PATCH to an API path and print the JSON response.
- [`epx api post`](#epx-api-post)\
  Send POST to an API path and print the JSON response.
- [`epx api put`](#epx-api-put)\
  Send PUT to an API path and print the JSON response.

## epx api delete

Send DELETE to an API path and print the JSON response.

Sends DELETE to PATH on the configured API host, with the JSON body that `--file` gives
(none without it), and prints the response body as JSON (YAML with `-o yaml`) with sorted
keys and every value as sent (nothing for an empty one). \{tenant\} in PATH is replaced with
the tenant; query values given with `-p` replace inline ones. It sends no other header, such
as the Content-Language that the Unit Service requires to create or update a unit.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type PATH at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requests only the scopes given with `--scope` besides the tenant: name every write scope
that the endpoint needs, as Emporix grants only requested scopes.

**Command:** `epx api delete PATH [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `-p, --param <key=value>`\
  Query parameter as key=value (repeatable).
- `--scope <strings>`\
  OAuth scope to request besides the tenant (repeatable).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx api delete /product/{tenant}/products/100200 --scope product.product_manage --yes
```

## epx api get

GET an API path and print the JSON response.

Sends GET to PATH on the configured API host and prints the response body as JSON
(YAML with `-o yaml`) with sorted keys and every value as sent.
\{tenant\} in PATH is replaced with the tenant; Accept-Language: \* requests every translation.
Query values given with `-p` replace inline ones. Request every scope the endpoint needs
with `--scope`: Emporix grants only requested scopes and may silently omit data otherwise.

**Command:** `epx api get PATH [flags]`

**Flags**

- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `-p, --param <key=value>`\
  Query parameter as key=value (repeatable).
- `--scope <strings>`\
  OAuth scope to request besides the tenant (repeatable).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx api get /site/{tenant}/sites
epx api get /product/{tenant}/products -p pageSize=5 --scope product.product_read_unpublished
```

## epx api patch

Send PATCH to an API path and print the JSON response.

Sends PATCH to PATH on the configured API host, with the JSON body that `--file` gives
(none without it), and prints the response body as JSON (YAML with `-o yaml`) with sorted
keys and every value as sent (nothing for an empty one). \{tenant\} in PATH is replaced with
the tenant; query values given with `-p` replace inline ones. It sends no other header, such
as the Content-Language that the Unit Service requires to create or update a unit.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requests only the scopes given with `--scope` besides the tenant: name every write scope
that the endpoint needs, as Emporix grants only requested scopes.

**Command:** `epx api patch PATH [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `-p, --param <key=value>`\
  Query parameter as key=value (repeatable).
- `--scope <strings>`\
  OAuth scope to request besides the tenant (repeatable).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx api patch /site/{tenant}/sites/AcmeStore_NL --scope site.site_manage --file site.json
```

## epx api post

Send POST to an API path and print the JSON response.

Sends POST to PATH on the configured API host, with the JSON body that `--file` gives
(none without it), and prints the response body as JSON (YAML with `-o yaml`) with sorted
keys and every value as sent (nothing for an empty one). \{tenant\} in PATH is replaced with
the tenant; query values given with `-p` replace inline ones. It sends no other header, such
as the Content-Language that the Unit Service requires to create or update a unit.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requests only the scopes given with `--scope` besides the tenant: name every write scope
that the endpoint needs, as Emporix grants only requested scopes.

**Command:** `epx api post PATH [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `-p, --param <key=value>`\
  Query parameter as key=value (repeatable).
- `--scope <strings>`\
  OAuth scope to request besides the tenant (repeatable).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx api post /brand/brands --scope brand.brand_manage --file brand.json
```

## epx api put

Sends PUT to PATH on the configured API host, with the JSON body that `--file` gives
(none without it), and prints the response body as JSON (YAML with `-o yaml`) with sorted

the tenant; query values given with `-p` replace inline ones. It sends no other header, such

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without

instead of sending it.

Requests only the scopes given with `--scope` besides the tenant: name every write scope
that the endpoint needs, as Emporix grants only requested scopes.

**Command:** `epx api put PATH [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `-p, --param <key=value>`\
  Query parameter as key=value (repeatable).

# epx auth

> Check Emporix credentials.

## epx auth

**Command:** `epx auth [flags]`, `epx auth [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx auth status`](#epx-auth-status)\
  Request a token and show the tenant and scopes it grants.

## epx auth status

Request a token and show the tenant and scopes it grants.

Requests a service token for the tenant plus the given scopes and shows what was granted.
Emporix grants only requested scopes, so pass `--scope` to check specific permissions;
a missing scope fails with exit code 3. The token itself is never printed.

**Command:** `epx auth status [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among TENANT, EXPIRES IN, SCOPES.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--scope <strings>`\
  Scope the credential must grant (repeatable).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx auth status --scope product.product_read_unpublished --scope indexing.search_view
```

# epx availability

> Read and change availability.

## epx availability

Reads product availability (stock), the tenant's own availability: on a site with list and
get, which require `--site`, and on every site with search. create, update and delete change
the availability of a product on a site, bulk-create, bulk-update and bulk-delete that of
many.

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require the availability.availability\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx availability [flags]`, `epx availability [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx availability bulk-create`](#epx-availability-bulk-create)\
  Create availability in bulk.
- [`epx availability bulk-delete`](#epx-availability-bulk-delete)\
  Delete availability in bulk.
- [`epx availability bulk-update`](#epx-availability-bulk-update)\
  Upsert availability in bulk.
- [`epx availability create`](#epx-availability-create)\
  Create the availability of a product on a site.
- [`epx availability delete`](#epx-availability-delete)\
  Delete the availability of a product on a site.
- [`epx availability get`](#epx-availability-get)\
  Show the availability of a product on a site.
- [`epx availability list`](#epx-availability-list)\
  List the availability of every product on a site.
- [`epx availability search`](#epx-availability-search)\
  Search the availability of products.
- [`epx availability update`](#epx-availability-update)\
  Upsert the availability of a product on a site.

## epx availability bulk-create

Create availability in bulk.

Creates the availability records in `--file`, a JSON array of records, each with the
productId and site it is for and the fields that create takes. Emporix advises against a
record on a site named main, which aggregates the availability of the other sites.

Emporix takes up to 200 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the availability.availability\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx availability bulk-create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability bulk-delete

Delete availability in bulk.

Deletes the availability records that `--file` names, a JSON array of objects with the
productId and site of each, such as `[{"productId": "100200", "site": "AcmeStore_NL"}]`.
The availability of a bundle is that of its scarcest product and cannot be deleted.

Emporix takes up to 200 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Deletes the availability that `--file` names with one request, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type the tenant at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the availability.availability\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx availability bulk-delete [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability bulk-update

Upsert availability in bulk.

Replaces the availability records in `--file`, a JSON array of records as bulk-create
takes them, or creates those that do not exist (an upsert).

Emporix takes up to 200 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the availability.availability\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx availability bulk-update [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability create

Create the availability of a product on a site.

Creates the availability of the product PRODUCT\_ID on the site `--site` names, from `--file`:
a JSON object with stockLevel, available, popularity and distributionChannel (ASSORTMENT,
HOME\_DELIVERY or PICKUP), as [`epx availability get PRODUCT_ID --site S -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/availability#epx-availability-get) prints
them. Emporix answers 409 Conflict when the product has one on that site already. It
advises against a record on a site named main, which aggregates the availability of the
other sites.
PRODUCT\_ID is the product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)), not its code.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the availability.availability\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx availability create PRODUCT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability delete

Delete the availability of a product on a site.

Deletes the availability of the product PRODUCT\_ID on the site `--site` names.
The availability of a bundle is that of its scarcest product and cannot be deleted.
PRODUCT\_ID is the product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)), not its code.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type PRODUCT\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the availability.availability\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx availability delete PRODUCT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability get

Show the availability of a product on a site.

Reads product availability (stock) on the site `--site` names, the tenant's own
availability.
PRODUCT\_ID is the product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)), not its code.
The availability of a bundle's products is only in `-o json` (bundleAvailabilities).

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx availability get PRODUCT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among PRODUCT, SITE, STOCK, AVAILABLE, CHANNEL.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability list

List the availability of every product on a site.

Reads product availability (stock) on the site `--site` names, the tenant's own
availability.
A bundle is listed as a whole and per product; an unknown site lists nothing.

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx availability list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among PRODUCT, SITE, STOCK, AVAILABLE, CHANNEL.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability search

Search the availability of products.

Reads the availability records, on every site, that an Emporix q filter finds (`--query`;
without it, every record), shown as list shows them, bundles left out. `--body` with a JSON
array of product ids reads theirs instead, bundles included.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx availability search [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among PRODUCT, SITE, STOCK, AVAILABLE, CHANNEL.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx availability update

Upsert the availability of a product on a site.

Replaces the availability of the product PRODUCT\_ID on the site `--site` names with the one
in `--file`, a JSON object as create takes it, or creates it where there is none (an

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without

Requires the availability.availability\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx availability update PRODUCT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).

# epx brands

> Read, create, change and delete brands.

## epx brands

Reads brands.

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require the brand.brand\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx brands [flags]`, `epx brands [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx brands create`](#epx-brands-create)\
  Create a brand.
- [`epx brands delete`](#epx-brands-delete)\

- [`epx brands patch`](#epx-brands-patch)\
  Change members of a brand.
- [`epx brands update`](#epx-brands-update)\
  Replace a brand.

## epx brands create

Create a brand.

Creates a brand from the JSON in `--file`, such as
`{"name": "Acme", "localizedName": {"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}}`, and prints the brand that
Emporix answers with, including its id. Emporix generates the id unless the JSON names one;
an id that exists already is a conflict, while a name that exists already makes a second
brand.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the brand.brand\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx brands create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx brands delete

Delete a brand.

Deletes the brand ID.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the brand.brand\_manage scope.

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx brands patch

Change members of a brand.

Changes the members of the brand ID that the JSON in `--file` names, such as name or
localizedDescription; the others keep their values. A map of translations in it, such as
localizedName, adds to the brand's: the languages it names change, the others stay. Unlike
update, Emporix does not check a metadata.version in it. An unknown ID is not found. It prints the brand that Emporix answers with.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the brand.brand\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx brands patch ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx brands update

Replaces the brand ID with the JSON in `--file`: a member that it leaves out is removed.
An unknown ID is not found. It prints the brand that Emporix answers with.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request

Requires the brand.brand\_manage scope.

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx carts

> Read and change carts and their items and discounts.

## epx carts

Reads shopping carts, personal data included, with their items, discounts, delivery
restrictions and validation; creates, changes and deletes carts, their items and discounts.

Its reads require the cart.cart\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.
Its writes require the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts [flags]`, `epx carts [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx carts change-currency`](#epx-carts-change-currency)\
  Change the currency of a cart.
- [`epx carts change-site`](#epx-carts-change-site)\
  Move a cart to another site.
- [`epx carts create`](#epx-carts-create)\
  Create a customer's cart.
- [`epx carts delete`](#epx-carts-delete)\
  Delete a cart.
- [`epx carts delivery-restrictions`](#epx-carts-delivery-restrictions)\
  Show the lead time and non-delivery days of a cart.
- [`epx carts discounts`](#epx-carts-discounts)\
  Read, apply and remove the discounts of a cart.
- [`epx carts execute`](#epx-carts-execute)\
  Run a chain of cart commands.
- [`epx carts find`](#epx-carts-find)\
  Show the cart of a customer or of an anonymous session on a site.
- [`epx carts get`](#epx-carts-get)\
  Show one cart.
- [`epx carts items`](#epx-carts-items)\
  Read and change the items of a cart.
- [`epx carts merge`](#epx-carts-merge)\

  Search carts.

  Update a cart.
- [`epx carts validate`](#epx-carts-validate)\
  Check the prices of a cart's items.

## epx carts change-currency

Change the currency of a cart.

Changes the currency of the cart CART\_ID to the one that `--currency` names; Emporix
matches the prices of the cart's items in it.
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts change-currency CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--currency <code>`\
  The three-letter code of the currency, e.g. USD (required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts change-site

Move a cart to another site.

shipping, tax and payment the cart then takes; where the site's currency differs, Emporix
matches the prices of the cart's items in it.
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts change-site CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <code>`\
  The code of the site to move the cart to (required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts create

Create a customer's cart.

Creates a customer's cart from the JSON object of `--file`: its customerId, siteCode,
currency and type (such as shopping or wishlist; a customer may hold one open cart of
each type: another is a conflict, exit 5), and optionally legalEntityId, channel,
deliveryWindow, addresses and mixins. Emporix answers with the cartId. A cart of an
anonymous customer needs, instead of a customerId, the session-id header of the
customer's session, which epx does not send: without either, Emporix answers 400 Bad
Request.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type CART\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts delete CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts delivery-restrictions

Show the lead time and non-delivery days of a cart.

Reads what limits the delivery of a cart's items: LEAD HOURS is the time needed to prepare
them for delivery, the longest leadTime of the items' own mixins.productCustomAttributes,
and NON-DELIVERY DAYS the days on which they cannot be delivered, the union of their
nonDelivery days, as numbers from 0 (Monday). An item gets these mixins where it is added
([`epx carts items create`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-items-create) takes them); Emporix ignores those of the item's
product and of its product member. The cart itself also carries leadTime and nonDelivery.
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx carts delivery-restrictions CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting cart.cart\_manage, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among LEAD HOURS, NON-DELIVERY DAYS.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts discounts create

Apply a discount to a cart.

Applies a discount to the cart CART\_ID: the coupon that `--code` names, or the JSON
object of `--file`, with the coupon's code and optionally its name, amount or discountRate,
currency and discountCalculationType (SUBTOTAL or TOTAL). One discount per request.
Emporix may limit the coupons per cart (a tenant setting; one tenant allows one: a second is
refused with 400 Bad Request, exit 1). It refuses a coupon restricted to customers
(restrictions.validFor), even to the cart's own customer, with 403 Forbidden (exit 1),
`"User not authorized."`, when an API key credential such as epx's applies it.
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts discounts create CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--code <code>`\
  The code of the coupon to apply (required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts discounts delete

Remove a discount from a cart.

Removes the discount at INDEX from the cart CART\_ID. The discounts after it then move
up by one: list them again before you remove another by INDEX, or remove discounts by

CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.
INDEX is the INDEX that [`epx carts discounts list CART_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-discounts-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type INDEX at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts discounts delete CART_ID INDEX [flags]`

**Flags**

  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

Deletes every discount of the cart (or those that `--codes` names) with one request, which cannot be undone.

## epx carts discounts list

List the discounts of a cart.

Reads the discounts (coupons) applied to a cart: AMOUNT is a fixed amount, RATE a percentage
of the price, APPLIES TO is SUBTOTAL or TOTAL, and INDEX its position among the cart's
discounts. Whether Emporix counts a discount when it calculates the cart (valid) is not
sent here, only with the cart's own discounts: [`epx carts get CART_ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-get).
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx carts discounts list CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting cart.cart\_manage, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CODE, NAME, AMOUNT, RATE, APPLIES TO, INDEX.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts execute

Run a chain of cart commands.

Runs a chain of commands on the cart CART\_ID in one request, from the JSON object of
`--file`: `{"commands": [...]}`, each with its type (AddCartItem, UpdateCartItem,
DeleteCartItem, DeleteCartItems, GetCart, AddCartItemsBatch, UpdateCartItemsBatch,
UpdateCart, ApplyCartDiscount, GetCartDiscounts, DeleteCartDiscounts, DeleteCartDiscount,
RefreshCart or ValidateCart), the body of that operation as data, and the rest of its
request as options (itemId, partial, expandCalculation, resourceVersion, codes,
discountIndex, …). epx prints the result of each command that ran, the data of each
as its operation answers. Without `--on-error` resume, Emporix runs no command after one
that failed, but keeps what those before it changed. With `--versioning` explicit, Emporix
answers a stale resourceVersion as a failed command with code 500 (its message names 409
CONFLICT), so epx exits 1 and says it may have been carried out; it was not.
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Emporix takes up to 10 commands in one request (epx refuses more), runs them in
order and answers with the result of each that ran: when one failed, epx prints the
response, lists the commands that failed on standard error (of a command that adds
or updates items in a batch, the items that failed; Emporix carried out the others)
and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--allow-external-prices` also requests the cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices scope.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts execute CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-external-prices`\
  Allow a command with an external price, product, fee or discount (requests cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices too).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `--on-error <string>`\
  Whether Emporix stops after a command that failed (fail, the default) or runs the rest (resume): fail or resume.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--versioning <string>`\
  How the writes check the cart's version (default skip): skip checks none, explicit each command's options.resourceVersion, follow the first's, then the version each write makes: skip, explicit or follow.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx carts execute 6a86b20c2f5961330a8b3eb6 --file add-then-get.json --dry-run
epx carts execute 6a86b20c2f5961330a8b3eb6 --file chain.json --on-error resume --yes
```

## epx carts find

Show the cart of a customer or of an anonymous session on a site.

Reads the one cart of a site that the criteria identify, personal data included: a
customer's (`--customer`) or an anonymous session's (`--session`). Without `--legal-entity`, it
is the cart without a legal entity, and without `--type` the cart without a type. epx never
asks Emporix to create a missing cart; when none matches, Emporix answers not found (exit 4).
STATUS is OPEN or CLOSED (sent by search only), CUSTOMER the customer id
(empty for an anonymous cart, whose sessionId `-o json` shows), ITEMS the number of items and
TOTAL the gross final price (items, shipping and payment fee) in the cart's currency.
A CLOSED cart, such as one merged into another, is listed by search but not found by get.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx carts find [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting cart.cart\_manage, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, STATUS, SITE, TYPE, CUSTOMER, LEGAL ENTITY, ITEMS, TOTAL, MODIFIED.
- `--customer <ID>`\
  The customer ID whose cart to read.
- `--legal-entity <ID>`\
  The legal entity ID of the cart.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--session <ID>`\
  The ID of the anonymous session whose cart to read.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--type <type>`\
  The cart's type.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts items bulk-update

Update items of a cart.

cart CART\_ID and the whole item, as update takes it without `--partial`. Emporix
refuses an entry with only quantity for that item (400 "The Price must be
defined."). [`epx carts execute`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-execute) changes some members of several items
(UpdateCartItemsBatch with options.partial).
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Emporix takes up to 50 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--allow-external-prices` also requests the cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices scope.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts items bulk-update CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-external-prices`\
  Allow an item with an external price, product, fee or discount (requests cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices too).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts items create

Add a product to a cart.

Adds a product to the cart CART\_ID as a new item, from the JSON object of `--file`: its
product (its id) or itemYrn, quantity and price (priceId, originalAmount,
effectiveAmount and currency, as [`epx prices match`](/emporix-cli/commands/prices#epx-prices-match) finds them), and optionally
keepAsSeparateLineItem, externalFees, externalDiscounts and mixins.
`--site` names the cart's site. Emporix answers 201 with the itemId (e.g. 0 for the first
item) and yrn. A product that the cart holds already, added without
keepAsSeparateLineItem, raises the quantity of its item (the same itemId), so a create
sent twice adds twice. A product object
in the body is stored as sent, in place of the one Emporix would store. The item's
mixins.productCustomAttributes (leadTime, nonDelivery) feed
[`epx carts delivery-restrictions`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-delivery-restrictions).
Emporix refuses a product that is not published with 400 Bad Request (exit 1), and an
item with an external price without `--allow-external-prices` with 403 Forbidden
(exit 3).
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--allow-external-prices` also requests the cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices scope.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts items create CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-external-prices`\
  Allow an item with an external price, product, fee or discount (requests cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices too).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts items get

Show one item of a cart.

Reads one item of a cart.
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.
ID is the ID that [`epx carts items list CART_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-items-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.
PRODUCT is the product id, NAME the product's name, PRICE the price that matched the item,
per unit and as the price states it (net or gross), and GROSS the gross value of the item's
quantity before discounts, one per tax line. Emporix does not always send an item's gross
unit price and total (after discounts, with fees) here: only for the items that the cart
held when it was last calculated (by a read of the cart or a discount, for example), not
for those added since. The cart always has them: [`epx carts get CART_ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-get).

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx carts items get CART_ID ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting cart.cart\_manage, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, PRODUCT, NAME, QUANTITY, PRICE, GROSS.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts merge

longer find them.

instead of sending it.

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

## epx carts search

Search carts.

Reads the carts, personal data included, that an Emporix q filter finds (`--query`; without
it, every cart), e.g. `--query` `'status:OPEN siteCode:AcmeStore_NL'`.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.
STATUS is OPEN or CLOSED (sent by search only), CUSTOMER the customer id
(empty for an anonymous cart, whose sessionId `-o json` shows), ITEMS the number of items and
TOTAL the gross final price (items, shipping and payment fee) in the cart's currency.
A CLOSED cart, such as one merged into another, is listed by search but not found by get.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx carts search [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting cart.cart\_manage, which can also change data (required).
- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, STATUS, SITE, TYPE, CUSTOMER, LEGAL ENTITY, ITEMS, TOTAL, MODIFIED.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts update

Update a cart.

Updates the cart CART\_ID with the JSON object of `--file`: customerId, currency, type,
status (OPEN or CLOSED), deliveryWindow, zipCode and countryCode (both or neither: one
alone is answered 400 Bad Request, exit 1), addresses, mixins and externalDiscounts, as
[`epx carts get CART_ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-get) shows them. Emporix creates no missing cart, and
ignores metadata.version in the body: only [`epx carts execute --versioning`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-execute) checks the
cart's version.
CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--allow-external-prices` also requests the cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices scope.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts update CART_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-external-prices`\
  Allow external discounts (externalDiscounts) (requests cart.cart\_manage\_external\_prices too).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx carts validate

Check the prices of a cart's items.

Reads whether a cart's items pass Emporix's checks, which find prices that are no longer
valid and prices duplicated for a product; it changes nothing. VALID is true or false and

CART\_ID is the ID that [`epx carts search`](/emporix-cli/commands/carts#epx-carts-search) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Requires the cart.cart\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx carts validate CART_ID [flags]`

  Opt in to requesting cart.cart\_manage, which can also change data (required).

  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among VALID, ERRORS.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx catalogs

> Read and change catalogs.

## epx catalogs

Reads catalogs, visible or not. STATUS and VISIBLE are separate Emporix fields and can
disagree. ROOT CATEGORIES counts the categories assigned directly to the catalog.

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require the catalog.catalog\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx catalogs [flags]`, `epx catalogs [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx catalogs create`](#epx-catalogs-create)\
  Create a catalog.
- [`epx catalogs delete`](#epx-catalogs-delete)\
  Delete a catalog.
- [`epx catalogs for-category`](#epx-catalogs-for-category)\
  List the catalogs a category is assigned to.
- [`epx catalogs get`](#epx-catalogs-get)\
  Show one catalog.
- [`epx catalogs list`](#epx-catalogs-list)\
  List catalogs.
- [`epx catalogs patch`](#epx-catalogs-patch)\
  Change members of a catalog.
- [`epx catalogs update`](#epx-catalogs-update)\
  Upsert a catalog.

## epx catalogs create

Create a catalog.

Creates a catalog from the JSON in `--file`, shaped as [`epx catalogs get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/catalogs#epx-catalogs-get) shows
one: name and description (maps of languages to text), visibility, publishedSites and
categoryIds (root categories); Emporix generates the id unless the body gives one. It
answers with the id; an id that exists already is a conflict (exit 5).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the catalog.catalog\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx catalogs create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx catalogs patch

others. Emporix requires metadata.version in the body, as [`epx catalogs get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/catalogs#epx-catalogs-get)
shows it, and answers a version that is not the catalog's as it answers an unknown
catalog, with 404 Not Found: epx then exits with 5, a conflict (read the catalog again
before you retry), also for an unknown ID, and with 4 without a version.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the catalog.catalog\_manage scope.

- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx catalogs update

Upsert a catalog.

Replaces the catalog ID with the JSON in `--file`, or creates it with that id when there
is none (an upsert); the body has the members of create's but the id.
With metadata.version, as [`epx catalogs get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/catalogs#epx-catalogs-get) shows it, Emporix refuses
the write as a conflict (exit 5) when the catalog changed since it was read.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the catalog.catalog\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx catalogs update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx categories

> Read and change categories and the products assigned to them.

## epx categories

Reads categories, published and unpublished.

Its reads require the category.category\_read\_unpublished scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx categories [flags]`, `epx categories [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx categories assignments`](#epx-categories-assignments)\
  Read and change the products assigned to a category.
- [`epx categories create`](#epx-categories-create)\
  Create a category.
- [`epx categories delete`](#epx-categories-delete)\
  Delete a category.
- [`epx categories for-product`](#epx-categories-for-product)\
  List the categories a product is assigned to.
- [`epx categories get`](#epx-categories-get)\
  Show one category.
- [`epx categories list`](#epx-categories-list)\
  List categories.
- [`epx categories parents`](#epx-categories-parents)\
  List the categories above a category.
- [`epx categories patch`](#epx-categories-patch)\
  Change members of a category.
- [`epx categories search`](#epx-categories-search)\
  Search categories.
- [`epx categories subcategories`](#epx-categories-subcategories)\
  List the categories below a category.
- [`epx categories update`](#epx-categories-update)\
  Upsert a category.

## epx categories assignments

Read and change the products assigned to a category.

Reads the products assigned to a category, assigns products to it and unassigns them.

Its reads require the category.category\_read\_unpublished scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx categories assignments [flags]`, `epx categories assignments [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx categories assignments bulk-create`](#epx-categories-assignments-bulk-create)\
  Assign products to a category.
- [`epx categories assignments bulk-update`](#epx-categories-assignments-bulk-update)\
  Upsert the assignments of products to a category.
- [`epx categories assignments create`](#epx-categories-assignments-create)\
  Assign a product to a category.
- [`epx categories assignments delete`](#epx-categories-assignments-delete)\
  Unassign a product from a category.
- [`epx categories assignments delete-all`](#epx-categories-assignments-delete-all)\
  Unassign every product from a category.
- [`epx categories assignments delete-assignment`](#epx-categories-assignments-delete-assignment)\
  Delete an assignment of a product to a category.
- [`epx categories assignments delete-product-everywhere`](#epx-categories-assignments-delete-product-everywhere)\
  Unassign a product from every category.
- [`epx categories assignments list`](#epx-categories-assignments-list)\
  List the products assigned to a category.
- [`epx categories assignments update`](#epx-categories-assignments-update)\
  Upsert the assignment of a product to a category.

## epx categories assignments bulk-create

Assign products to a category.

Assigns products to a category: the JSON in `--file` is an array of assignments, each as
in `{"ref": {"id": "100200", "type": "PRODUCT"}}`.
CATEGORY\_ID is the ID that [`epx categories list`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Emporix takes up to 200 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the category.category\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx categories assignments bulk-create CATEGORY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
