Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the category.category\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx categories assignments bulk-update CATEGORY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).

## epx categories assignments delete

Unassign a product from a category.

Deletes the assignment of the product PRODUCT\_ID to the category CATEGORY\_ID: the PRODUCT
that [`epx categories assignments list CATEGORY_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-assignments-list) shows, as update assigns it. The product and the category stay.
PRODUCT\_ID is the product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)), not its code.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type PRODUCT\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the category.category\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx categories assignments delete CATEGORY_ID PRODUCT_ID [flags]`

## epx categories assignments list

List the products assigned to a category.

Reads the products assigned to a category, published and unpublished. PRODUCT is the
product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)) and TYPE the kind of item, a product.
CATEGORY\_ID is the ID that [`epx categories list`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Requires the category.category\_read\_unpublished scope.

**Command:** `epx categories assignments list CATEGORY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, PRODUCT, TYPE, PUBLISHED, NAME.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx categories create

Create a category.

Creates a category from the JSON in `--file`, shaped as [`epx categories get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-get)
shows one: localizedName (a map of languages to text, as are the other localized
members), published, which Emporix requires, parentId (a root category without one)
and the other members; Emporix generates the id unless the body gives one, and answers
with it. To create it published, give published: true in the body and `--publish`, which
sends the publish parameter that Emporix requires to match it, with the scope it requires
for it.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--publish` also requests the category.category\_publish scope.

Requires the category.category\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx categories create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--publish`\
  Publish the category: sends publish=true, which needs published: true in the body (requests category.category\_publish too).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx categories delete

Delete a category.

Deletes the category ID. Without `--with-subcategories`, the categories directly below it
move to the category above it and keep the categories below them; Emporix refuses to
delete a root category with categories below it (400 Bad Request, exit 1). With it,
Emporix deletes every category below it too.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
With `--with-subcategories`, it deletes the category and every category below it with one request.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the category.category\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx categories delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--with-subcategories`\
  Delete every category below the category too.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx categories patch

Change members of a category.

Changes the members of the category ID that the JSON in `--file` gives, and keeps the
others. Emporix requires metadata.version in the body, as [`epx categories get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-get)
shows it, and refuses a version that is not the category's with 400 Bad Request (exit 1),
not as a conflict. published in the body publishes or unpublishes the category as sent,
without the publish scopes. A move (parentId) shows in [`epx categories parents`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-parents) at once,
in [`epx category-trees`](/emporix-cli/commands/category-trees#epx-category-trees) a few seconds later.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the category.category\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx categories patch ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx categories search

Search categories.

Reads the categories, published and unpublished, that an Emporix q filter finds
(`--query`; without it, every category).
It reads and shows them as [`epx categories list`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-list) does.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.

Requires the category.category\_read\_unpublished scope.

**Command:** `epx categories search [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, CODE, TYPE, PUBLISHED, NAME.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx categories subcategories

List the categories below a category.

Reads every category below a category, at all levels, published and unpublished; PARENT
is the id of the category each one lies directly below.
CATEGORY\_ID is the ID that [`epx categories list`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Requires the category.category\_read\_unpublished scope.

**Command:** `epx categories subcategories CATEGORY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, PARENT, CODE, TYPE, PUBLISHED, NAME.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx categories update

Upsert a category.

Replaces the category ID with the JSON in `--file`, or creates it with that id when
there is none (an upsert); the body has the members of create's, published included, but
id, type and ownClassificationMixins. Without parentId, the category becomes a root
category.
With metadata.version, as [`epx categories get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/categories#epx-categories-get) shows it, Emporix refuses
the write as a conflict (exit 5) when the category changed since it was read.
To publish or unpublish it, give published in the body and `--publish` or `--unpublish`,
which sends the publish parameter that Emporix requires to match it, with the scope it
requires for it. Emporix requires `--publish` for any body with published: true, also of a
category that is published already.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--publish` also requests the category.category\_publish scope.
`--unpublish` also requests the category.category\_unpublish scope.

Requires the category.category\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx categories update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--publish`\
  Publish the category: sends publish=true, which needs published: true in the body (requests category.category\_publish too).
- `--unpublish`\
  Unpublish the category: sends publish=false, which needs published: false in the body (requests category.category\_unpublish too).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx category-trees

> Read and rebuild category trees.

## epx category-trees

Reads category trees, published and unpublished: each root category followed by its
subcategories, depth first, in the order Emporix sends them; NAME is indented by the
category's level. get takes the id of a root category: Emporix answers another
category's id as not found. list's `--limit` counts trees, each shown whole. A move of a
category shows in its tree a few seconds later; a root category moved below another may
keep its old tree until it is deleted.

Its reads require the category.category\_read\_unpublished scope.
Its writes require the category.category\_manage, category.category\_read\_unpublished scopes.

**Command:** `epx category-trees [flags]`, `epx category-trees [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

  Rebuild a category tree.
- [`epx category-trees search`](#epx-category-trees-search)\
  Search category trees.

## epx category-trees search

Search category trees.

Reads the category trees, published and unpublished, that hold any of the categories
`--category` names, each whole; without `--category`, every tree. `--limit` counts trees.

# epx changelog

> Read the change history (audit log).

## epx changelog

Reads the tenant's change history, an audit log (personal data: who changed what, with
the old and new values in `-o json`), ordered by when the changes occurred. AT is when, TYPE
create, update or delete, ENTITY and ENTITY ID the changed document (an order, customer,
product, site, …), ACTOR who changed it (a name, system, external or unknown) and FIELDS
the changed fields. Without a lower bound on occurredAt (not only inside OR), Emporix
returns the last 30 days, a window that moves while the pages are read: on an active
tenant, read a closed range in the past, e.g. `--query`
`'occurredAt:(>"2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z" AND <"2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z")'`, or use
`--limit`; otherwise a change can come or go between pages, so the read fails or misses
it. One document's history: `--query` `'entity:order entityId:ID'`.

Requires the changelog.changelog\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx changelog [flags]`, `epx changelog [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx changelog list`](#epx-changelog-list)\
  List changes.

## epx changelog list

List changes.

Reads the tenant's change history, an audit log (personal data: who changed what, with
the old and new values in `-o json`), ordered by when the changes occurred. AT is when, TYPE
create, update or delete, ENTITY and ENTITY ID the changed document (an order, customer,
product, site, …), ACTOR who changed it (a name, system, external or unknown) and FIELDS
the changed fields. Without a lower bound on occurredAt (not only inside OR), Emporix
returns the last 30 days, a window that moves while the pages are read: on an active
tenant, read a closed range in the past, e.g. `--query`
`'occurredAt:(>"2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z" AND <"2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z")'`, or use
`--limit`; otherwise a change can come or go between pages, so the read fails or misses
it. One document's history: `--query` `'entity:order entityId:ID'`.

Requires the changelog.changelog\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx changelog list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among AT, TYPE, ENTITY, ENTITY ID, NAME, ACTOR, FIELDS.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx completion

> Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell.

## epx completion

Generate the autocompletion script for epx for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

With EPX\_COMPLETE\_IDS=1 in the environment, the arguments that name items (such as ID of
[`epx products get ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-get)) and `--site` complete too, with up to 100 of the IDs and site codes that
the first page of their list shows (the whole list where Emporix sends it in one response),
read with the API key in effect and the scopes of that list within 3s.
Without it, completion never calls the API; when the API cannot be read, it offers no IDs
and prints nothing.

**Command:** `epx completion [flags]`, `epx completion [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx completion bash`](#epx-completion-bash)\
  Generate the autocompletion script for bash.
- [`epx completion fish`](#epx-completion-fish)\
  Generate the autocompletion script for fish.
- [`epx completion powershell`](#epx-completion-powershell)\
  Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.
- [`epx completion zsh`](#epx-completion-zsh)\
  Generate the autocompletion script for zsh.

## epx completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for bash.

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the `'bash-completion'` package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(epx completion bash)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

**Linux:**

```text
epx completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/epx
```

**macOS:**

```text
epx completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/epx
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

**Command:** `epx completion bash`

**Flags**

- `--no-descriptions`\
  Disable completion descriptions.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx completion fish

Generate the autocompletion script for fish.

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
epx completion fish | source
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

```text
epx completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/epx.fish
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

**Command:** `epx completion fish [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--no-descriptions`\
  Disable completion descriptions.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx completion powershell

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
epx completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.

**Command:** `epx completion powershell [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--no-descriptions`\
  Disable completion descriptions.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx completion zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for zsh.

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

```text
echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc
```

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(epx completion zsh)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

**Linux:**

```text
epx completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_epx"
```

**macOS:**

```text
epx completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_epx
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

**Command:** `epx completion zsh [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--no-descriptions`\
  Disable completion descriptions.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx configurations

> Read and change tenant configurations.

## epx configurations

Reads tenant configurations (settings such as project\_lang).
Tables show values as sent, secured ones included, and cut long ones (`-o json` prints
them whole).
A setting that was never set is not found (exit 4): Emporix then applies its default.
[`epx configurations global`](/emporix-cli/commands/configurations#epx-configurations-global), `clients`, `for-client` and `client-setting` read global
settings and those of clients. [`epx configurations create`](/emporix-cli/commands/configurations#epx-configurations-create), `update` and `delete`
change settings, and `client-create`, `client-update` and `client-delete` those
of a client.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Its writes require the configuration.configuration\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx configurations [flags]`, `epx configurations [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx configurations client-create`](#epx-configurations-client-create)\
  Create configurations of a client.
- [`epx configurations client-delete`](#epx-configurations-client-delete)\
  Delete a configuration of a client.
- [`epx configurations client-setting`](#epx-configurations-client-setting)\
  Show one configuration of a client.
- [`epx configurations client-update`](#epx-configurations-client-update)\
  Replace a configuration of a client.
- [`epx configurations clients`](#epx-configurations-clients)\
  List the clients that have configurations.
- [`epx configurations create`](#epx-configurations-create)\
  Create tenant configurations.
- [`epx configurations delete`](#epx-configurations-delete)\
  Delete a tenant configuration.
- [`epx configurations for-client`](#epx-configurations-for-client)\
  List the configurations of a client.
- [`epx configurations get`](#epx-configurations-get)\
  Show one configuration.
- [`epx configurations global`](#epx-configurations-global)\
  List global configurations.
- [`epx configurations list`](#epx-configurations-list)\
  List configurations.
- [`epx configurations update`](#epx-configurations-update)\
  Replace a tenant configuration.

## epx configurations client-create

Create configurations of a client.

Creates configurations of the client CLIENT from the JSON array of settings that `--file` gives,
each with its key and value (and optionally secured, description, readOnly, restricted and
schemaUrl), and prints the settings created. Emporix answers 409 Conflict (exit 5) when one of
the keys exists already (the other keys of the request may be created then): change it with [`epx configurations client-update`](/emporix-cli/commands/configurations#epx-configurations-client-update).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the configuration.configuration\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx configurations client-create CLIENT [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type KEY at its prompt.

# epx contact-assignments

> Read and change which customers are contacts of which legal entities.

## epx contact-assignments

Reads and changes contact assignments, the customers that act as contacts of a legal
entity, personal data included.
create and update ID (an upsert) send the JSON body of `--file`; delete ID sends none.

Its reads require the customermanagement.contactassignment\_read scope.
Its writes require the customermanagement.contactassignment\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx contact-assignments [flags]`, `epx contact-assignments [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx contact-assignments create`](#epx-contact-assignments-create)\
  Create one contact assignment.
- [`epx contact-assignments delete`](#epx-contact-assignments-delete)\
  Delete one contact assignment.
- [`epx contact-assignments get`](#epx-contact-assignments-get)\
  Show one contact assignment.
- [`epx contact-assignments list`](#epx-contact-assignments-list)\
  List contact assignments.
- [`epx contact-assignments update`](#epx-contact-assignments-update)\
  Upsert one contact assignment.

## epx contact-assignments create

Create one contact assignment.

Creates the contact assignment that the JSON body of `--file` describes, shaped as
[`epx contact-assignments get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/contact-assignments#epx-contact-assignments-get) prints one:
legalEntity and customer (required, each as `{"id": ...}` of one that exists: 400 Bad Request,
exit 1, otherwise; the customer's id, not its number), type (PRIMARY, BILLING, LOGISTICS
or CONTACT, the default) and primary (true or false).
Without an id, Emporix makes one, and answers with it; an id that exists already is a
conflict (exit 5).
A second assignment of a customer to the same legal entity is a conflict (exit 5) too.
Assigning a customer to a subsidiary also assigns it to the parent company, as a CONTACT
in an assignment of its own, which takes a delete of its own.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the customermanagement.contactassignment\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx contact-assignments create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx contact-assignments delete

Delete one contact assignment.

Deletes the contact assignment ID; it sends no body.
ID is the ID that [`epx contact-assignments list`](/emporix-cli/commands/contact-assignments#epx-contact-assignments-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the customermanagement.contactassignment\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx contact-assignments delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx countries

> Read countries, and activate or deactivate them.

## epx countries

Reads all countries known to the tenant, active or not (ACTIVE shows which ones the
tenant uses). REGIONS lists region codes (see [`epx regions`](/emporix-cli/commands/regions#epx-regions)).

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require the country.country\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx countries [flags]`, `epx countries [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx countries get`](#epx-countries-get)\
  Show one country.
- [`epx countries list`](#epx-countries-list)\
  List countries.
- [`epx countries patch`](#epx-countries-patch)\
  Activate or deactivate a country.

## epx countries get

Show one country.

Reads all countries known to the tenant, active or not (ACTIVE shows which ones the
tenant uses). REGIONS lists region codes (see [`epx regions`](/emporix-cli/commands/regions#epx-regions)).

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx countries get CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CODE, NAME, ACTIVE, REGIONS.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx countries list

List countries.

Reads all countries known to the tenant, active or not (ACTIVE shows which ones the
tenant uses). REGIONS lists region codes (see [`epx regions`](/emporix-cli/commands/regions#epx-regions)).

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx countries list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CODE, NAME, ACTIVE, REGIONS.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx countries patch

Activate or deactivate a country.

Activates the country CODE for the tenant (`--active`) or deactivates it (`--active=false`):
Emporix lets a PATCH change active only. epx takes the country's metadata.version as read
(`--version`, as [`epx countries get CODE -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/countries#epx-countries-get) prints it), which the reference asks for;
Emporix does not check it, so a stale version is accepted and applied. `--file` gives the JSON body
instead, e.g. `{"active": true, "metadata": {"version": 1}}`. An unknown CODE is not found
(exit 4).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the country.country\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx countries patch CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--active`\
  Activate the country, or with `--active=false` deactivate it (required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--version <VERSION>`\
  The VERSION of the country as read (metadata.version; required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx countries patch NL --active --version 1
```

# epx coupons

> Read, create, change and redeem coupons.

## epx coupons

Reads coupons, customer ids included (issuedTo, validFor in `-o json`). DISCOUNT is a
percentage, an amount or FREE\_SHIPPING. STATUS is VALID, INACTIVE, EXPIRED or USED, as
Emporix computes it: `--query` status:VALUE matches no coupon and `--sort` status is ignored.
REDEEMED counts redemptions, out of the maximum when there is one; Emporix counts those for
a legal entity apart, per legal entity (legalEntityRedemptions, only in `-o json`). Other
restrictions (valid from, minimum order value, customers, categories, segments) are only in
`-o json`.
[`epx coupons redemptions`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-redemptions) and `redemption` read the redemptions of a coupon, all or one.
[`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) leaves out deleted coupons; [`epx coupons get CODE`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-get) still shows one, in
the table as a live one (`-o json` has deleted: true). Deleted coupons are listed too, one
page at a time, by
[`epx api get /coupon/{tenant}/coupons -p showDeleted=true --scope coupon.coupon_read`](/emporix-cli/commands/api#epx-api-get).
[`epx coupons create`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-create), `update`, `patch` and `delete` change coupons, `redeem` redeems one
outside a checkout, `redemption-delete` deletes a redemption, and `referral-create` creates
the referral coupon of a customer.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx coupons [flags]`, `epx coupons [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx coupons create`](#epx-coupons-create)\
  Create a coupon.
- [`epx coupons delete`](#epx-coupons-delete)\
  Delete a coupon.
- [`epx coupons get`](#epx-coupons-get)\
  Show one coupon.
- [`epx coupons list`](#epx-coupons-list)\
  List coupons.
- [`epx coupons patch`](#epx-coupons-patch)\
  Change members of a coupon.
- [`epx coupons redeem`](#epx-coupons-redeem)\
  Redeem a coupon.
- [`epx coupons redemption`](#epx-coupons-redemption)\
  Show one redemption of a coupon.
- [`epx coupons redemption-delete`](#epx-coupons-redemption-delete)\
  Delete a redemption of a coupon.
- [`epx coupons redemptions`](#epx-coupons-redemptions)\
  List the redemptions of a coupon.
- [`epx coupons referral`](#epx-coupons-referral)\
  Show the referral coupon of a customer.
- [`epx coupons referral-create`](#epx-coupons-referral-create)\
  Create the referral coupon of a customer.
- [`epx coupons update`](#epx-coupons-update)\
  Replace a coupon.
- [`epx coupons validate`](#epx-coupons-validate)\
  Check whether a coupon can be redeemed.

## epx coupons create

Create a coupon.

Creates the coupon in `--file`, a JSON object with at least its name and, for a discount,
discountType (PERCENT with discountPercentage, ABSOLUTE with discountAbsolute, or
FREE\_SHIPPING), and prints `{"id": CODE}`: the code of the JSON, or one that Emporix makes
without one. Emporix saves codes in upper case unless the tenant configuration
enableCouponCodeCaseSensitivity is true. A coupon with the code exists already: a conflict
(exit 5), also for a deleted one, whose code stays taken.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the coupon.coupon\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx coupons create --file coupon.json --dry-run
```

## epx coupons delete

Delete a coupon.

Deletes the coupon CODE, which [`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) then leaves out. Emporix keeps it as
deleted: [`epx coupons get CODE`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-get) still shows it, and its code stays taken. An unknown CODE is
not found (exit 4).
Emporix refuses a deleted coupon with 403 Forbidden (exit 1).

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type CODE at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the coupon.coupon\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons delete CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx coupons get

Show one coupon.

Reads coupons, customer ids included (issuedTo, validFor in `-o json`). DISCOUNT is a
percentage, an amount or FREE\_SHIPPING. STATUS is VALID, INACTIVE, EXPIRED or USED, as
Emporix computes it: `--query` status:VALUE matches no coupon and `--sort` status is ignored.
REDEEMED counts redemptions, out of the maximum when there is one; Emporix counts those for

restrictions (valid from, minimum order value, customers, categories, segments) are only in
`-o json`.
[`epx coupons redemptions`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-redemptions) and `redemption` read the redemptions of a coupon, all or one.
[`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) leaves out deleted coupons; [`epx coupons get CODE`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-get) still shows one, in
the table as a live one (`-o json` has deleted: true). Deleted coupons are listed too, one
page at a time, by
[`epx api get /coupon/{tenant}/coupons -p showDeleted=true --scope coupon.coupon_read`](/emporix-cli/commands/api#epx-api-get).

Requires the coupon.coupon\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons get CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CODE, NAME, DISCOUNT, STATUS, REDEEMED, VALID UNTIL.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx coupons list

List coupons.

Reads coupons, customer ids included (issuedTo, validFor in `-o json`). DISCOUNT is a
percentage, an amount or FREE\_SHIPPING. STATUS is VALID, INACTIVE, EXPIRED or USED, as
Emporix computes it: `--query` status:VALUE matches no coupon and `--sort` status is ignored.
REDEEMED counts redemptions, out of the maximum when there is one; Emporix counts those for
a legal entity apart, per legal entity (legalEntityRedemptions, only in `-o json`). Other
restrictions (valid from, minimum order value, customers, categories, segments) are only in
`-o json`.
[`epx coupons redemptions`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-redemptions) and `redemption` read the redemptions of a coupon, all or one.
[`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) leaves out deleted coupons; [`epx coupons get CODE`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-get) still shows one, in
the table as a live one (`-o json` has deleted: true). Deleted coupons are listed too, one
page at a time, by
[`epx api get /coupon/{tenant}/coupons -p showDeleted=true --scope coupon.coupon_read`](/emporix-cli/commands/api#epx-api-get).

Requires the coupon.coupon\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CODE, NAME, DISCOUNT, STATUS, REDEEMED, VALID UNTIL.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx coupons patch

Change members of a coupon.

Changes the members of the coupon CODE that the JSON in `--file` names, such as status or
restrictions; the others keep their values. An unknown CODE is not found (exit 4).
Send its metadata.version as read to change it only if nobody changed it since:
Emporix answers 409 Conflict (exit 5) otherwise.
Without one, Emporix changes the coupon anyway.
Emporix refuses a deleted coupon with 403 Forbidden (exit 1).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the coupon.coupon\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons patch CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx coupons redeem

Redeem a coupon.

Redeems a coupon for an order of `--order-total` that it takes `--discount` off, by
`--customer` (a customer number) where given, outside a checkout, and prints what Emporix
answers with: `{"id": ID}`, the redemption's id. Sent twice, it redeems the coupon twice.
Emporix refuses a coupon that cannot be redeemed and says why:
one redeemed as often as it may be with 400 Bad Request (exit 1); one that the customer may
not redeem, or that needs a customer where `--customer` is not given, with
403 Forbidden (exit 1). An unknown coupon is not found (exit 4).
`--legal-entity` names the legal entity that the customer is assigned to: Emporix
refuses it, with 400 Bad Request (exit 1), for a customer without a legal entity and for an
unknown one.
[`epx coupons validate`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-validate) runs the same checks without redeeming it.
`--customer` needs the scope below: Emporix refuses it to a token with coupon.coupon\_manage
alone (403 Forbidden).
COUPON\_CODE is the CODE that [`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the coupon.coupon\_redeem\_on\_behalf scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons redeem COUPON_CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--customer <CUSTOMER_NUMBER>`\
  The CUSTOMER\_NUMBER of the customer who redeems it.
- `--discount <AMOUNT CURRENCY>`\
  What the coupon takes off as AMOUNT CURRENCY (required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--legal-entity <ID>`\
  The ID of the customer's legal entity.
- `--order <CODE>`\
  The CODE of the order.
- `--order-total <AMOUNT CURRENCY>`\
  The order's total as AMOUNT CURRENCY, e.g. `"100 EUR"` (required without `--file`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx coupons redeem SAVE7 --order-total "100 EUR" --discount "7 EUR" --customer 10001 --dry-run
```

## epx coupons redemption

Show one redemption of a coupon.

Reads one redemption of a coupon (personal data).
COUPON\_CODE is the CODE that [`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.
ID is the ID that [`epx coupons redemptions COUPON_CODE`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-redemptions) shows; an unknown one is not found.
ORDER TOTAL is the order's value and DISCOUNT the amount the coupon took off it. The
narrower coupon.coupon\_redeem scope reads only the redemptions a caller made itself.

Requires the coupon.coupon\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx coupons redemption COUPON_CODE ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting coupon.coupon\_manage, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, ORDER, CUSTOMER, LEGAL ENTITY, ORDER TOTAL, DISCOUNT, REDEEMED AT.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx coupons redemption-delete

Delete a redemption of a coupon.

Deletes the redemption ID of a coupon, which then counts one redemption less: one that was
redeemed as often as it may be can be redeemed again.
COUPON\_CODE is the CODE that [`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.
ID is the ID that [`epx coupons redemptions COUPON_CODE`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-redemptions) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the coupon.coupon\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons redemption-delete COUPON_CODE ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).

  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.

## epx coupons referral-create

[`epx customers list`](/emporix-cli/commands/customers#epx-customers-list) shows; an unknown one is not found (exit 4).

instead of sending it.

- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

## epx coupons validate

Check whether a coupon can be redeemed.

Checks whether a coupon can be redeemed for an order of `--order-total` that it takes
`--discount` off, by `--customer` (a customer number) where given: Emporix runs every check of
a redemption without redeeming the coupon. REDEEMABLE is true when it can be. Emporix
refuses a coupon that cannot be redeemed with an error that says why: one that the customer
may not redeem with 403 Forbidden (exit 1). An unknown coupon is not found (exit 4).
`--legal-entity` names the legal entity that the customer is assigned to: Emporix
refuses it, with 400 Bad Request (exit 1), for a customer without a legal entity and for an
unknown one.
Emporix answers a redeemable coupon without a body; `-o json` prints true then. The scope,
which epx requests also without `--customer`, lets a credential redeem coupons on a
customer's behalf too.
COUPON\_CODE is the CODE that [`epx coupons list`](/emporix-cli/commands/coupons#epx-coupons-list) shows.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.

Requires the coupon.coupon\_redeem\_on\_behalf scope.

**Command:** `epx coupons validate COUPON_CODE [flags]`

  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.

  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among REDEEMABLE.
- `--customer <CUSTOMER_NUMBER>`\
  The CUSTOMER\_NUMBER of the customer who redeems it.
- `--discount <AMOUNT CURRENCY>`\
  What the coupon takes off as AMOUNT CURRENCY (required without `--body`).
- `--legal-entity <ID>`\
  The ID of the customer's legal entity.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `--order <CODE>`\
  The CODE of the order.
- `--order-total <AMOUNT CURRENCY>`\
  The order's total as AMOUNT CURRENCY, e.g. `"100 EUR"` (required without `--body`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx currencies

> Read, create, change and delete currencies.

## epx currencies

Reads the tenant's currencies.

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require the currency.currency\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx currencies [flags]`, `epx currencies [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx currencies create`](#epx-currencies-create)\
  Create a currency.
- [`epx currencies delete`](#epx-currencies-delete)\
  Delete a currency.
- [`epx currencies get`](#epx-currencies-get)\
  Show one currency.
- [`epx currencies list`](#epx-currencies-list)\
  List currencies.
- [`epx currencies update`](#epx-currencies-update)\
  Rename a currency.

## epx currencies create

Create a currency.

Creates a currency from the JSON in `--file`: its code (ISO 4217) and name, e.g.
`{"code": "CHF", "name": {"en": "Swiss franc", "de": "Schweizer Franken"}}`, in languages
that the tenant has. Emporix answers with the code; a code that exists already is a
conflict (exit 5).

Localized text in the body, such as a name, is a map of translations, e.g.
`{"en": "gram", "de": "Gramm"}`, as `-o json` of a read prints it, or with `--content-language`
LANGUAGE a string in that language, e.g. `"gram"` with `--content-language` en.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the currency.currency\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx currencies create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--content-language <LANGUAGE>`\
  The LANGUAGE of localized text in the body, or \* for maps of translations. Default: `*`.
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx currencies delete

Delete a currency.

Deletes the currency CODE; it sends no body. The reference says Emporix also deletes the
prices in the currency, asynchronously (not checked here). The exchange rates stay, and a site
that lists the currency keeps listing it. It sends no forceDelete, which the reference documents
(default false) without saying what it changes.
Emporix answers an unknown CODE as one that it deleted (204 No Content).

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type CODE at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the currency.currency\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx currencies delete CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

No OAuth scope is needed.

# epx custom-entities

> Read and change custom entity types and their instances.

## epx custom-entities

Reads and changes custom entity types: entities a tenant defines. create, update
and delete change types; export exports types with their schemas (opt-in), which
import imports.
[`epx custom-entities instances`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-instances) reads and changes the instances of a type.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx custom-entities [flags]`, `epx custom-entities [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx custom-entities create`](#epx-custom-entities-create)\
  Create a custom entity type.
- [`epx custom-entities delete`](#epx-custom-entities-delete)\
  Delete a custom entity type.
- [`epx custom-entities export`](#epx-custom-entities-export)\
  Export custom entity types with their schemas.
- [`epx custom-entities get`](#epx-custom-entities-get)\
  Show one custom entity.
- [`epx custom-entities import`](#epx-custom-entities-import)\
  Import custom entity types with their schemas.
- [`epx custom-entities instances`](#epx-custom-entities-instances)\
  Read and change the instances of a custom entity type.
- [`epx custom-entities list`](#epx-custom-entities-list)\
  List custom entity types.
- [`epx custom-entities update`](#epx-custom-entities-update)\
  Upsert a custom entity type.

## epx custom-entities create

Create a custom entity type.

Creates the custom entity type in `--file`, a JSON object with its id and name, such as
`{"id": "CUSTOM_DOCUMENT", "name": {"en": "Document"}}`, and prints the id that Emporix answers
with; one that exists already is a conflict. The id has capital letters, digits and
underscores, the first a letter. Emporix also creates the scopes that read and manage the
instances of the type, such as custom.custom\_document\_manage, which it grants only minutes
later: until then, the instance commands of the type exit with code 3.
Built-in types, such as AVAILABILITY and LOCATION, cannot be created.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the schema.schema\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx custom-entities create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities delete

Delete a custom entity type.

Deletes the custom entity type ID. Emporix refuses to delete a type that schemas or
instances use (400 Bad Request), and answers an unknown ID as deleted, not as not found.
The scopes that Emporix created with the type remain granted: the instances of a deleted
type then read as an empty list.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the schema.schema\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx custom-entities delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities export

Export custom entity types with their schemas.

Reads an export package of the custom entity types that `--type` names (the ID that
[`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list) shows): each type with its schemas, without metadata, and
none of their instances. Emporix leaves out an ID that names no custom entity type (a
built-in type such as PRODUCT too); if none is left, it answers with an empty package
(exit 0).
Emporix refuses an empty selection (`--body` with \[\], exit 1).

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.
DATA is the package, base64-encoded and cut in the table; `-o json` prints the package
whole, as an import on another tenant takes it.

Requires the schema.schema\_manage scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx custom-entities export [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting schema.schema\_manage, which can also change data (required).
- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among DATA, EXPORTED AT.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--type <ID>`\
  A custom entity type ID to export (repeatable; required without `--body`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities get

Show one custom entity.

Reads custom entity types: entities a tenant defines.
[`epx custom-entities instances`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-instances) reads and changes the instances of a type.

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx custom-entities get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, VERSION.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities import

[`epx custom-entities export -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-export) prints it, e.g. on another tenant. A type or schema
that exists already is created again, its id followed by \_COPY, such as
CUSTOM\_DOCUMENT\_COPY, and the references of its schemas then name the copy.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without

instead of sending it.

Requires the schema.schema\_manage scope.

- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities instances

Read and change the instances of a custom entity type.

Reads the instances of a custom entity type, every one (list), those a filter finds
(search) or one (get), and creates, changes and deletes them, one at a time or in bulk.

Its reads require the custom.&lt;type\>\_read scope.
Its writes require the custom.&lt;type\>\_manage scope.
&lt;type\> is the custom entity type in lower case (custom.document\_manage, custom.document\_read for DOCUMENT).

**Command:** `epx custom-entities instances [flags]`, `epx custom-entities instances [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

  Delete instances of a custom entity type in bulk.

  Change instances of a custom entity type in bulk.
- [`epx custom-entities instances bulk-update`](#epx-custom-entities-instances-bulk-update)\
  Upsert instances of a custom entity type in bulk.
- [`epx custom-entities instances create`](#epx-custom-entities-instances-create)\
  Create an instance of a custom entity type.
- [`epx custom-entities instances delete`](#epx-custom-entities-instances-delete)\
  Delete an instance of a custom entity type.

## epx custom-entities instances bulk-create

Create instances of a custom entity type in bulk.

Creates instances of the custom entity type CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID from `--file`, a JSON array of
instances, each as create takes it.
CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID is the ID that [`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list) shows.

With `--validate-references` true, Emporix checks the items that the references of each
instance name with epx's token, which reads the instances of CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID alone: an
instance with a reference to an item that does not exist fails with 500 Internal Server
Error (nothing is created), as one with a reference to an instance of
another custom entity type is expected to, and one with a reference to another kind of
item, such as a product, may.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Emporix takes up to 200 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Where `--validate-references` is true, epx also requests
the custom.&lt;type\>\_read scope.

Requires the custom.&lt;type\>\_manage scope.
&lt;type\> is the custom entity type in lower case (custom.document\_manage for DOCUMENT).

**Command:** `epx custom-entities instances bulk-create CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--validate-references <string>`\
  Whether Emporix checks that the items that references in the body name exist (false without it), requesting custom.&lt;type\>\_read where it is true: true or false.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities instances bulk-delete

Delete instances of a custom entity type in bulk.

Deletes the instances of the custom entity type CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID whose ids `--file` lists, a
JSON array of strings, such as `["123", "124"]`; Emporix answers an unknown id as deleted.
CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID is the ID that [`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list) shows.

Emporix takes up to 1000 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Deletes the instances of a custom entity type that `--file` names with one request, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the custom.&lt;type\>\_manage scope.
&lt;type\> is the custom entity type in lower case (custom.document\_manage for DOCUMENT).

**Command:** `epx custom-entities instances bulk-delete CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,

may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

## epx custom-entities instances create

Create an instance of a custom entity type.

Creates an instance of the custom entity type CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID from the JSON object in
`--file`, such as `{"id": "123", "name": {"en": "Report"}, "mixins": {…}}`, and prints the id
that Emporix answers with; it makes one unless the object names it, and an id that exists
already is a conflict. An owner, such as `{"type": "EMPLOYEE", "userId": "…"}`, cannot change
once set. The attributes of a schema go under its id, which metadata.mixins maps to its
URL: `{"mixins": {"SCHEMA_ID": {…}}, "metadata": {"mixins": {"SCHEMA_ID": "URL"}}}`, the URL
being the metadata.url that [`epx schemas get SCHEMA_ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/schemas#epx-schemas-get) prints. A localized
attribute, unlike the name, is a list of translations, such as
`[{"language": "en", "value": "Report"}]`.
CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID is the ID that [`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list) shows.

Emporix checks the items that the references of the instance name (unless
`--validate-references` false) with epx's token, which reads the instances of CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID
alone: a reference to an instance of another custom entity type is then expected to fail
with 400 Bad Request, as one to the type fails without that scope, and one to another kind
of item, such as a product, may fail too.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Where `--validate-references` is true or not given, epx also requests
the custom.&lt;type\>\_read scope.

Requires the custom.&lt;type\>\_manage scope.
&lt;type\> is the custom entity type in lower case (custom.document\_manage for DOCUMENT).

**Command:** `epx custom-entities instances create CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--validate-references <string>`\
  Whether Emporix checks that the items that references in the body name exist (true without it), requesting custom.&lt;type\>\_read where it is true or not given: true or false.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

Delete an instance of a custom entity type.

Deletes the instance ID of the custom entity type CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID; Emporix answers an

ID is the ID that [`epx custom-entities instances list CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-instances-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.
OWNER is an instance's owner, by default who created it (EMPLOYEE, CUSTOMER or SERVICE,

- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities instances list

List the instances of a custom entity type.

Reads the instances of a custom entity type ([`epx custom-entities instances get`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-instances-get) shows one).
CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID is the ID that [`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list) shows; an unknown one has no scope that Emporix grants (exit code 3), and a type created in the last minutes has none yet.
OWNER is an instance's owner, by default who created it (EMPLOYEE, CUSTOMER or SERVICE,
and the user or client id); attribute values (mixins) are only in `-o json`. epx requests
the scope of the type, not the tenant-wide schema.custominstance\_read that Emporix also
accepts.

Requires the custom.&lt;type\>\_read scope.
&lt;type\> is the custom entity type in lower case (custom.document\_read for DOCUMENT).

**Command:** `epx custom-entities instances list CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, OWNER, VERSION.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities instances patch

Change an instance of a custom entity type.

Changes the instance ID of the custom entity type CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID with the JSON array of
JSON Patch (RFC 6902) operations in `--file`, such as
`[{"op": "replace", "path": "/name", "value": {"en": "Report"}}]`; an add whose path ends in
/- appends to an array. An unknown ID is not found.
CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID is the ID that [`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list) shows, and ID the one that
[`epx custom-entities instances list CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-instances-list) shows.

Emporix checks the items that the references of the instance name (unless
`--validate-references` false) with epx's token, which reads the instances of CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID
alone: a reference to an instance of another custom entity type is then expected to fail
with 400 Bad Request, as one to the type fails without that scope, and one to another kind
of item, such as a product, may fail too.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Where `--validate-references` is true or not given, epx also requests
the custom.&lt;type\>\_read scope.

Requires the custom.&lt;type\>\_manage scope.
&lt;type\> is the custom entity type in lower case (custom.document\_manage for DOCUMENT).

**Command:** `epx custom-entities instances patch CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--validate-references <string>`\
  Whether Emporix checks that the items that references in the body name exist (true without it), requesting custom.&lt;type\>\_read where it is true or not given: true or false.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx custom-entities instances search

Search the instances of a custom entity type.

Reads the instances of a custom entity type that an Emporix q filter finds (`--query`;
without it, every one).
It reads and shows them as [`epx custom-entities instances list CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-instances-list) does.
CUSTOM\_ENTITY\_ID is the ID that [`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list) shows; an unknown one has no scope that Emporix grants (exit code 3), and a type created in the last minutes has none yet.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.
OWNER is an instance's owner, by default who created it (EMPLOYEE, CUSTOMER or SERVICE,
and the user or client id); attribute values (mixins) are only in `-o json`. epx requests
the scope of the type, not the tenant-wide schema.custominstance\_read that Emporix also
accepts.

Requires the custom.&lt;type\>\_read scope.
&lt;type\> is the custom entity type in lower case (custom.document\_read for DOCUMENT).

**Command:** `epx custom-entities instances search CUSTOM_ENTITY_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, OWNER, VERSION.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).
