# epx customer-locations

> Read and change the locations of B2B customers.

## epx customer-locations

Reads and changes the locations of B2B customers (legal entities), contact emails
included. A legal entity names its locations in entitiesAddresses, each as `{"id": ...}`.
create and update ID (an upsert) send the JSON body of `--file`; delete ID sends none.

Its reads require the customermanagement.location\_read scope.
Its writes require the customermanagement.location\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx customer-locations [flags]`, `epx customer-locations [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx customer-locations create`](#epx-customer-locations-create)\
  Create one customer location.
- [`epx customer-locations delete`](#epx-customer-locations-delete)\
  Delete one customer location.
- [`epx customer-locations get`](#epx-customer-locations-get)\
  Show one customer location.
- [`epx customer-locations list`](#epx-customer-locations-list)\
  List customer locations.
- [`epx customer-locations update`](#epx-customer-locations-update)\
  Upsert one customer location.

## epx customer-locations create

Create one customer location.

Creates the customer location that the JSON body of `--file` describes, shaped as
[`epx customer-locations get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/customer-locations#epx-customer-locations-get) prints one:
type (required: HEADQUARTER, WAREHOUSE or OFFICE), contactDetails (required: emails,
phones, addressLine1, addressLine2, city, state, postcode, countryCode and tags) and name;
leave out `"phones"`: \[\] (an empty list), which Emporix refuses (exit 1).
Without an id, Emporix makes one, and answers with it; an id that exists already is a
conflict (exit 5).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the customermanagement.location\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx customer-locations create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

ID is the ID that [`epx customer-locations list`](/emporix-cli/commands/customer-locations#epx-customer-locations-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.
A legal entity that names it in entitiesAddresses no longer does.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the customermanagement.location\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx customer-locations delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

Reads the addresses of a customer, personal data included.
CUSTOMER\_NUMBER is the NUMBER that [`epx customers list`](/emporix-cli/commands/customers#epx-customers-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.
DEFAULT marks the default address; TAGS are labels such as BILLING or SHIPPING. Phone
numbers, states and extra address lines are only in `-o json`.

Requires the customer.customer\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx customers addresses list CUSTOMER_NUMBER [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, CONTACT, COMPANY, STREET, ZIP, CITY, COUNTRY, DEFAULT, TAGS.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx customers import

Import customers with their passwords.

Imports the customer profiles in `--file`, a JSON array of profiles as create takes them,
each with an account that holds its email and exactly one of passwordHash, a hash that
Emporix checks as its own, or legacyAuth, the hash of another system and its algorithm,
which Emporix replaces with its own as the customer signs in. Customers with legacyAuth
need a password migration retention: [`epx customers password-migration update`](/emporix-cli/commands/customers#epx-customers-password-migration-update) sets it.
Emporix ignores a customerNumber that a profile gives (no error).

Emporix takes up to 200 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the customer.import\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx customers import [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx customers password-migration

Read and set until when imported customers' passwords are migrated.

Reads, sets and removes the password migration retention of customer imports, until when
customers imported with a password hash from another system get an Emporix one.

Its reads require the customer.import\_read scope.
Its writes require the customer.import\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx customers password-migration [flags]`, `epx customers password-migration [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

  Remove the password migration retention.
- [`epx customers password-migration get`](#epx-customers-password-migration-get)\
  Show until when imported customers' passwords are migrated.
- [`epx customers password-migration update`](#epx-customers-password-migration-update)\
  Set until when imported customers' passwords are migrated.

## epx customers password-migration delete

Remove the password migration retention.

Removes the password migration retention. Emporix refuses it (400 Bad Request, exit 1)
while a customer still has a legacy password hash to migrate: move `--ends` of update
earlier instead to end the migration sooner. update sets the whole retention, so give
`--reminder` and `--emails` again where it should keep them.

Deletes the password migration retention of the tenant with one request, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type the tenant at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the customer.import\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx customers password-migration delete [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx customers password-migration get

Show until when imported customers' passwords are migrated.

Reads the password migration retention of customer imports: a customer imported with a
password hash from another system gets an Emporix one on signing in until ENDS; after
that, the customers not yet migrated must reset their password. REMINDER is when Emporix
asks them by email to sign in once, and EMAILS whether customers get these reminder and
reset emails. A tenant without this setting is not found (exit 4).

Requires the customer.import\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx customers password-migration get [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ENDS, REMINDER, EMAILS.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx customers password-migration update

Set until when imported customers' passwords are migrated.

Sets the whole password migration retention, or creates it where the tenant has none
(an upsert), from its flags or the JSON object of `--file`: until when customers imported
with legacyAuth get an Emporix password on signing in (`--ends`), when Emporix asks those
not yet migrated by email to sign in once (`--reminder`; without it, 7 days before `--ends`,
or tomorrow if that has passed, also where the retention it replaces had another date)
and whether customers get these reminder and reset emails (`--emails`: without it, epx
sends emailNotificationsEnabled=false; a `--file` without it gets Emporix's default, true).
Emporix answers with the retention.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the customer.import\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx customers password-migration update [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--emails`\
  Email customers the reminder and the password reset.
- `--ends <DATE>`\
  The DATE the migration ends, e.g. 2027-01-31 (required without `--file`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--reminder <DATE>`\
  The DATE of the reminder email, before `--ends`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx customers password-migration update --ends 2027-01-31 --reminder 2027-01-24 --emails
epx customers password-migration update --ends 2027-01-31 --yes
```

## epx customers patch

Change a customer.

Changes the members of the customer profile NUMBER that `--file` gives, a JSON object such

- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx delivery-times

> Read and change delivery times and their time slots; read the delivery windows of a cart.

## epx delivery-times

Reads and changes delivery times, the days on which a site delivers to a zone, and their
time slots; reads the delivery windows open to a cart, checks and counts the orders of a
delivery window and names its delivery cycle.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Its writes require the shipping.shipping\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx delivery-times [flags]`, `epx delivery-times [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx delivery-times bulk-create`](#epx-delivery-times-bulk-create)\
  Create delivery times in bulk.
- [`epx delivery-times create`](#epx-delivery-times-create)\
  Create a delivery time.
- [`epx delivery-times delete`](#epx-delivery-times-delete)\
  Delete a delivery time.
- [`epx delivery-times generate-cycle`](#epx-delivery-times-generate-cycle)\
  Name the delivery cycle of a delivery window.
- [`epx delivery-times get`](#epx-delivery-times-get)\
  Show one delivery time.
- [`epx delivery-times increment-counter`](#epx-delivery-times-increment-counter)\
  Count one more order in a delivery window.
- [`epx delivery-times list`](#epx-delivery-times-list)\
  List delivery times.
- [`epx delivery-times patch`](#epx-delivery-times-patch)\
  Change a delivery time.
- [`epx delivery-times slots`](#epx-delivery-times-slots)\
  Read and change the time slots of a delivery time.
- [`epx delivery-times update`](#epx-delivery-times-update)\
  Replace a delivery time.
- [`epx delivery-times validate`](#epx-delivery-times-validate)\
  Check whether a delivery window can take an order.
- [`epx delivery-times windows`](#epx-delivery-times-windows)\
  List the delivery windows open to a cart.

## epx delivery-times bulk-create

Create delivery times in bulk.

Creates the delivery times in `--file`, a JSON array of delivery times, each as create
takes it.

Emporix takes up to 50 items in one request (epx refuses more), carries out each on
its own and answers with the result of each: when one failed, epx prints the response,
lists the items that failed on standard error (one that failed with 500, 502, 503 or 504
may have been carried out all the same) and exits with the code that their failures
share (for example 5 for a 409 Conflict, 4 for a 404), else 1.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the shipping.shipping\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx delivery-times bulk-create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--validate-overlap <string>`\
  Whether Emporix refuses slots of one shipping method whose time ranges overlap (it does unless given false): true or false.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx delivery-times create

Create a delivery time.

Creates a delivery time from the JSON in `--file`: its siteCode and zoneId (or isForAllZones,
for a day without delivery on every zone of the site), its day (a weekday, singleDate or
datePeriod), isDeliveryDay, timeZoneId and deliveryDayShift, the slots of a delivery day
and optionally the delivery time's id and name, as [`epx delivery-times get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/delivery-times#epx-delivery-times-get)
prints one; a slot with a cutOffDayShift needs a delivery time without deliveryDayShift.
Emporix answers with its id, and refuses a delivery time that overlaps another of its
zone, or is not valid otherwise, with 400 Bad Request (exit 1).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the shipping.shipping\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx delivery-times create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).

## epx delivery-times generate-cycle

Name the delivery cycle of a delivery window.

Prints the name of the delivery cycle of a delivery window, as Emporix names it in the
delivery windows of a cart and in orders (deliveryCycle in
[`epx delivery-times windows CART_ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/delivery-times#epx-delivery-times-windows)): the delivery date, the hour (UTC) of the
slot's cut-off time and the deliveryCycleName of its cutOffTime, such as 2026-06-20-6morning.
The delivery window is the delivery time `--delivery-time` on `--date`, an ISO 8601
date and time such as 2026-11-02T12:00:00.000Z, in its `--slot`: [`epx delivery-times list`](/emporix-cli/commands/delivery-times#epx-delivery-times-list)
and [`epx delivery-times slots list`](/emporix-cli/commands/delivery-times#epx-delivery-times-slots-list) show their IDs.

flags make or `--body` gives whole.

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx delivery-times generate-cycle [flags]`

  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CYCLE.
- `--date <DATE>`\
  The delivery DATE and time, ISO 8601 (required without `--body`).

  Print table and csv without the header row.

  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--slot <ID>`\
  The ID of the delivery time's slot (required without `--body`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx delivery-times get

Show one delivery time.

Reads delivery times, the days on which a site delivers to a zone. ZONE is a zone id
([`epx shipping zones list --site S`](/emporix-cli/commands/shipping#epx-shipping-zones-list)), or `"all zones"` for a day without delivery on every
zone; DAY is a weekday, a date or a date period (from/to); DELIVERS is false for a day
without delivery; DAY SHIFT is how many days the delivery follows an order placed before
the cut-off, when the delivery time sets it (a weekday's slots may set their own); SLOTS
counts the time slots, which [`epx delivery-times slots list DELIVERY_TIME_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/delivery-times#epx-delivery-times-slots-list) lists.

Requires the shipping.shipping\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx delivery-times get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, SITE, ZONE, DAY, DELIVERS, TIME ZONE, DAY SHIFT, SLOTS.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).

## epx delivery-times slots create

Create a time slot of a delivery time.

Creates a time slot of a delivery day from the JSON in `--file`: its shippingMethod (a method
of the delivery time's zone), deliveryTimeRange (timeFrom and timeTo, local times such as
08:00), cutOffTime (its time, an ISO 8601 timestamp whose time of day counts, and for a
weekday its cutOffDayShift, which the delivery time must not combine with a
deliveryDayShift), capacity (the orders it takes) and optionally its id, as
[`epx delivery-times slots get DELIVERY_TIME_ID ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/delivery-times#epx-delivery-times-slots-get) prints one. Emporix answers
with its id, and a slot id that exists already with 400 Bad Request (exit 1), not as a
conflict.
DELIVERY\_TIME\_ID is the ID that [`epx delivery-times list`](/emporix-cli/commands/delivery-times#epx-delivery-times-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the shipping.shipping\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx delivery-times slots create DELIVERY_TIME_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).

  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--validate-overlap <string>`\
  Whether Emporix refuses slots of one shipping method whose time ranges overlap (it does unless given false): true or false.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx exchange-rates

> Read, create, change and delete currency exchange rates.

## epx exchange-rates

Reads currency exchange rates. CODE names a rate, e.g. EUR\_CHF.

Its reads require the currency.currency\_read scope.
Its writes require the currency.currency\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx exchange-rates [flags]`, `epx exchange-rates [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx exchange-rates create`](#epx-exchange-rates-create)\
  Create an exchange rate.
- [`epx exchange-rates delete`](#epx-exchange-rates-delete)\
  Delete an exchange rate.
- [`epx exchange-rates get`](#epx-exchange-rates-get)\
  Show one exchange rate.
- [`epx exchange-rates list`](#epx-exchange-rates-list)\
  List exchange rates.
- [`epx exchange-rates update`](#epx-exchange-rates-update)\
  Change an exchange rate.

## epx exchange-rates create

Create an exchange rate.

Creates the exchange rate from the currency `--source` into `--target` (both defined in the
tenant, as [`epx currencies list`](/emporix-cli/commands/currencies#epx-currencies-list) shows them), or the one in the JSON of `--file`. Emporix
answers with its code, SOURCE\_TARGET; a rate that exists already is a conflict (exit 5).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the currency.currency\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx exchange-rates create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--rate <RATE>`\
  The RATE: what one unit of the source currency is worth in the target currency, e.g. 0.95 (sent as a string; required without `--file`).
- `--source <CODE>`\
  The CODE of the currency to convert from (required without `--file`).
- `--target <CODE>`\
  The CODE of the currency to convert into (required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx exchange-rates create --source EUR --target CHF --rate 0.95
```

## epx exchange-rates delete

Delete an exchange rate.

Deletes the exchange rate CODE; it sends no body.
Emporix answers an unknown CODE as one that it deleted (204 No Content).

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type CODE at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the currency.currency\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx exchange-rates delete CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx exchange-rates get

Show one exchange rate.

Reads currency exchange rates. CODE names a rate, e.g. EUR\_CHF.

Requires the currency.currency\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx exchange-rates get CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CODE, SOURCE, TARGET, RATE.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx exchange-rates list

List exchange rates.

Reads currency exchange rates. CODE names a rate, e.g. EUR\_CHF.

Requires the currency.currency\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx exchange-rates list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among CODE, SOURCE, TARGET, RATE.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx exchange-rates update

Change an exchange rate.

Changes the rate of the exchange rate CODE (its currencies cannot change) to `--rate`, with
its metadata.version as read (`--version`, as [`epx exchange-rates get CODE -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/exchange-rates#epx-exchange-rates-get) prints
it), or to the JSON of `--file`. A stale version and an unknown CODE are both not found (exit 4):
Emporix answers 404 to both.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the currency.currency\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx exchange-rates update CODE [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--rate <RATE>`\
  The RATE: what one unit of the source currency is worth in the target currency, e.g. 0.95 (sent as a string; required without `--file`).
- `--version <VERSION>`\
  The VERSION of the rate as read (metadata.version; required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx exchange-rates update EUR_CHF --rate 0.96 --version 2
```

# epx fees

> Read and change fees and which items have them.

## epx fees

Reads and changes fees, surcharges on items such as products or payment types, and in
`assignments` which items have which fees. Emporix filters fees by site and documents main as
the default site, so list, for-product and for-item require `--site`. create, update and delete
change one fee.

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx fees [flags]`, `epx fees [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx fees assignments`](#epx-fees-assignments)\
  Read and change which items have which fees.
- [`epx fees create`](#epx-fees-create)\
  Create a fee.
- [`epx fees delete`](#epx-fees-delete)\
  Delete a fee.
- [`epx fees for-item`](#epx-fees-for-item)\
  List the fees of an item on a site.
- [`epx fees for-product`](#epx-fees-for-product)\
  List the fees of a product on a site.
- [`epx fees get`](#epx-fees-get)\
  Show one fee.
- [`epx fees list`](#epx-fees-list)\
  List the fees of a site.
- [`epx fees update`](#epx-fees-update)\
  Replace or change a fee.

## epx fees assignments

Read and change which items have which fees.

Reads item fees: which fees apply to which item (a product or a payment type) on a site.
Its writes assign fees to an item, by its YRN, or to a product, by its id.

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments [flags]`, `epx fees assignments [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx fees assignments create`](#epx-fees-assignments-create)\
  Assign fees to an item on a site.
- [`epx fees assignments delete`](#epx-fees-assignments-delete)\
  Delete the item fee of an item.
- [`epx fees assignments delete-fee`](#epx-fees-assignments-delete-fee)\
  Remove a fee from an item.
- [`epx fees assignments delete-product`](#epx-fees-assignments-delete-product)\
  Delete the item fee of a product.
- [`epx fees assignments delete-product-fee`](#epx-fees-assignments-delete-product-fee)\
  Remove a fee from a product.
- [`epx fees assignments list`](#epx-fees-assignments-list)\
  List the item fees of a site.
- [`epx fees assignments search`](#epx-fees-assignments-search)\
  Search the item fees of items.
- [`epx fees assignments search-by-product`](#epx-fees-assignments-search-by-product)\
  Search the item fees of a product on sites.
- [`epx fees assignments search-by-products`](#epx-fees-assignments-search-by-products)\
  Search the item fees of products on a site.
- [`epx fees assignments update`](#epx-fees-assignments-update)\
  Add fees to an item.
- [`epx fees assignments update-product`](#epx-fees-assignments-update-product)\
  Add fees to a product on a site.

## epx fees assignments create

Assign fees to an item on a site.

Assigns the fees that `--fee` names to the item that `--item` names on the site that `--site`
names, or those of `--file`, a JSON object with itemYrn, siteCode and feeIds, and prints
the id and YRN of the item fee. `--item` takes the YRN of an item,
e.g. `'urn:yaas:saasag:caasproduct:product:TENANT;PRODUCT_ID'`
(quoted, because the shell would end the command at ;).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.item\_create scope.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--fee <ID>`\
  The ID of a fee, as [`epx fees list`](/emporix-cli/commands/fees#epx-fees-list) shows it (repeatable; required without `--file`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--item <YRN>`\
  The YRN of the item to assign the fees to (required without `--file`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <code>`\
  The code of the site that the fees apply on (required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx fees assignments create --item 'urn:yaas:saasag:caasproduct:product:acme1;100200' \
  --site AcmeStore_NL --fee f1 --fee f2
```

## epx fees assignments delete

Delete the item fee of an item.

Deletes the item fee of the item YRN, which then has no fees.
Without `--site`, Emporix acts on the item fee on site main.
Emporix answers an unknown YRN as one that it deleted (204 No Content).
YRN names the item, e.g. `'urn:yaas:saasag:caasproduct:product:TENANT;PRODUCT_ID'`
(quoted, because the shell would end the command at ;).

Deletes every fee of the item YRN with one request, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type YRN at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.item\_delete scope.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments delete YRN [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <CODE>`\
  The site CODE of the item fee, sent as siteCode.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments delete-fee

Remove a fee from an item.

Removes the fee FEE\_ID from the item fee of the item YRN;
Emporix deletes the item fee once it has no fees.
Emporix answers an unknown FEE\_ID as one that it deleted (204 No Content).
YRN names the item, e.g. `'urn:yaas:saasag:caasproduct:product:TENANT;PRODUCT_ID'`
(quoted, because the shell would end the command at ;).
FEE\_ID is the ID that [`epx fees list`](/emporix-cli/commands/fees#epx-fees-list) shows.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type FEE\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.item\_delete scope.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments delete-fee YRN FEE_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments delete-product

Delete the item fee of a product.

Deletes the item fee of the product PRODUCT\_ID, which then has no fees.
Without `--site`, Emporix acts on the item fee on site main.
Emporix answers an unknown PRODUCT\_ID as one that it deleted (204 No Content).
PRODUCT\_ID is the product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)), not its code.

Deletes every fee of the product PRODUCT\_ID with one request, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type PRODUCT\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.item\_delete scope.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments delete-product PRODUCT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--site <CODE>`\
  The site CODE of the item fee, sent as siteCode.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments delete-product-fee

Remove a fee from a product.

Removes the fee FEE\_ID from the item fee of the product PRODUCT\_ID on the site of the fee;
Emporix deletes the item fee once it has no fees.
Emporix answers an unknown FEE\_ID as one that it deleted (204 No Content).
PRODUCT\_ID is the product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)), not its code.
FEE\_ID is the ID that [`epx fees list`](/emporix-cli/commands/fees#epx-fees-list) shows.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type FEE\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.item\_delete scope.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments delete-product-fee PRODUCT_ID FEE_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments list

Reads item fees: which fees apply to which item (a product or a payment type) on a site.
Emporix documents main as the default site, so `--site` is required; an unknown site lists
nothing.
ITEM is the item's YRN, ID the item fee's id and FEES the ids of its fees, as [`epx fees list`](/emporix-cli/commands/fees#epx-fees-list)

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments list [flags]`

**Flags**

  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ITEM, ID, SITE, FEES.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments search

Search the item fees of items.

Reads item fees: which fees apply to which item (a product or a payment type) on a site.
Reads the item fees of the items that `--item` names. Emporix requires a site, which `--site`
names in the query and in the body the flags make, but does not filter by it: the item
fees of other sites come too. `--item` takes the YRN of an item,
e.g. `'urn:yaas:saasag:caasproduct:product:TENANT;PRODUCT_ID'`
(quoted, because the shell would end the command at ;).

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.
ITEM is the item's YRN, ID the item fee's id and FEES the ids of its fees, as [`epx fees list`](/emporix-cli/commands/fees#epx-fees-list)
shows them; `-o json` shows the response as sent.

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments search [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ITEM, ID, SITE, FEES.
- `--item <YRN>`\
  The YRN of an item whose fees to read (repeatable; required without `--body`).
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments search-by-products

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments update

Add fees to an item.

Adds the fees that `--fee` names, or the feeIds of `--file`, a JSON object such as
`{"feeIds": ["f1", "f2"]}`, to those of the item YRN, creating its item fee where it
has none. Emporix removes no fee, with or without `--partial`, and an empty list changes
nothing: delete-fee removes one.
Without `--site`, Emporix acts on the item fee on site main.
YRN names the item, e.g. `'urn:yaas:saasag:caasproduct:product:TENANT;PRODUCT_ID'`
(quoted, because the shell would end the command at ;).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.item\_update scope.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments update YRN [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--fee <ID>`\
  The ID of a fee, as [`epx fees list`](/emporix-cli/commands/fees#epx-fees-list) shows it (repeatable; required without `--file`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--partial`\
  Send partial=true instead of partial=false, which Emporix treats alike.
- `--site <CODE>`\
  The site CODE of the item fee, sent as siteCode.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees assignments update-product

Add fees to a product on a site.

Adds the fees that `--fee` names, or the feeIds of `--file`, a JSON object such as
`{"feeIds": ["f1", "f2"]}`, to those of the product PRODUCT\_ID
on the site that `--site` names, creating its item fee where it
has none. Emporix removes no fee, with or without `--partial`, and an empty list changes
nothing: delete-product-fee removes one.
PRODUCT\_ID is the product id (as in [`epx products list`](/emporix-cli/commands/products#epx-products-list)), not its code.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.item\_update scope.

**Command:** `epx fees assignments update-product PRODUCT_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--fee <ID>`\
  The ID of a fee, as [`epx fees list`](/emporix-cli/commands/fees#epx-fees-list) shows it (repeatable; required without `--file`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--partial`\
  Send partial=true instead of partial=false, which Emporix treats alike.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees create

Create a fee.

Creates the fee in `--file`, a JSON object with code (unique in the tenant), name, feeType
(PERCENT, ABSOLUTE or ABSOLUTE\_MULTIPLY\_ITEMQUANTITY), feePercentage or feeAbsolute (amount
and currency), siteCode and active, and optionally itemType (PRODUCT or PAYMENTTYPE),
taxable with taxCode, and activeTimespan, e.g. `{"code": "deposit", "name": {"en": "Deposit"}, "feeType": "ABSOLUTE", "feeAbsolute": {"amount": 0.25, "currency": "EUR"}, "siteCode": "AcmeStore_NL", "active": true}`. Without an id, Emporix makes one; the response
gives it and its YRN. A code that the tenant has already is a conflict (exit 5).

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. The Fee Service ignores
Content-Language: it stores a string as sent, in no language, in place of any
translations.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.fee\_create scope.

**Command:** `epx fees create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees delete

Delete a fee.

Deletes the fee ID, which no item has then.
Emporix answers an unknown ID as one that it deleted (204 No Content).

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the fee.fee\_delete scope.

**Command:** `epx fees delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees for-item

List the fees of an item on a site.

Reads fees, surcharges on items such as products or payment types. Emporix filters fees
by site and documents main as the default site, so list, for-product and for-item require
`--site`; an unknown site lists nothing. TYPE is PERCENT, ABSOLUTE or
ABSOLUTE\_MULTIPLY\_ITEMQUANTITY (the amount times the item quantity), AMOUNT the percentage
or the amount in its currency, ITEM TYPE the type of item the fee applies to (PRODUCT or
PAYMENTTYPE), and FROM and TO the active time span.
YRN names the item, e.g. `'urn:yaas:saasag:caasproduct:product:TENANT;PRODUCT_ID'`
(quoted, because the shell would end the command at ;). An unknown item lists nothing;
Emporix fails on a malformed YRN.

No OAuth scope is needed.

**Command:** `epx fees for-item YRN [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, CODE, NAME, TYPE, AMOUNT, ITEM TYPE, SITE, ACTIVE, TAXABLE, FROM, TO.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--site <site>`\
  Site code, e.g. main (required).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx fees update

# epx iam

> Read and change IAM users, groups and access rights.

## epx iam

Reads the tenant's IAM (identity and access management) data: user accounts, the groups they
belong to and what these may do: roles, permissions, scopes, resources, access controls and
templates. Its writes change users, groups and their users, access controls and custom
scopes, and with them who may do what in the tenant.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx iam [flags]`, `epx iam [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx iam access-controls`](#epx-iam-access-controls)\
  Read, upsert and delete access controls.
- [`epx iam groups`](#epx-iam-groups)\
  Read, create, upsert and delete IAM groups and their users.
- [`epx iam permissions`](#epx-iam-permissions)\
  Read IAM permissions.
- [`epx iam resources`](#epx-iam-resources)\
  Read IAM resources.
- [`epx iam roles`](#epx-iam-roles)\
  Read IAM roles.
- [`epx iam scopes`](#epx-iam-scopes)\
  Read, upsert and delete OAuth scopes.
- [`epx iam templates`](#epx-iam-templates)\
  Read IAM templates.
- [`epx iam users`](#epx-iam-users)\
  Read, create, replace and delete IAM users; read what they may do.

## epx iam access-controls

Read, upsert and delete access controls.

Reads IAM access controls, the scopes they grant the users of the groups that hold them, and
upserts and deletes them.
Its writes change who may do what in the tenant.

Its reads require the iam.access\_read scope.
Its writes require the iam.access\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam access-controls [flags]`, `epx iam access-controls [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx iam access-controls delete`](#epx-iam-access-controls-delete)\
  Delete an access control.
- [`epx iam access-controls get`](#epx-iam-access-controls-get)\
  Show one access control.
- [`epx iam access-controls list`](#epx-iam-access-controls-list)\
  List IAM access controls.
- [`epx iam access-controls update`](#epx-iam-access-controls-update)\
  Upsert an access control.

## epx iam access-controls delete

Delete an access control.

Deletes the access control ID. Emporix deletes only those made for the tenant, not the
predefined ones (PREDEFINED in [`epx iam access-controls list`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-access-controls-list)).
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the iam.access\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam access-controls delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam access-controls get

Show one access control.

Reads IAM access controls.
SCOPES counts the scopes an access control grants (`-o json` lists them); RESOURCE
and ROLE are the ids of the resource and role older access controls refer to.
list sorts by id unless `--sort` says otherwise; end another order with ,id:asc (e.g.
name.en:asc,id:asc), as Emporix wants a direction on every field, so pages do not overlap.

Requires the iam.access\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx iam access-controls get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, SCOPES, PREDEFINED, RESOURCE, ROLE.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam access-controls list

List IAM access controls.

Reads IAM access controls.
SCOPES counts the scopes an access control grants (`-o json` lists them); RESOURCE
and ROLE are the ids of the resource and role older access controls refer to.
list sorts by id unless `--sort` says otherwise; end another order with ,id:asc (e.g.
name.en:asc,id:asc), as Emporix wants a direction on every field, so pages do not overlap.

Requires the iam.access\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx iam access-controls list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, SCOPES, PREDEFINED, RESOURCE, ROLE.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).

  Print table and csv without the header row.

- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam access-controls update

Upsert an access control.

Replaces the access control ID with the JSON in `--file`, or creates it with that id where
none exists (an upsert): the scopes it grants (at least one), and optionally its name and
description, domains and restrictedTo (CUSTOMER or EMPLOYEE: the only kind of group that may
grant it, set when it is created only).
With metadata.version as read, Emporix changes it only if that is still its version.
Emporix answers with the id of one it created, and with nothing when it replaced one.
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the iam.access\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam access-controls update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).

## epx iam groups delete

Delete a group.

Deletes the group ID. Emporix refuses to delete a group that users belong to (400 Bad
Request, exit 1; [`epx iam groups users list ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-users-list) lists them) unless `--force-delete` is
given, which removes every user from it too.
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
With `--force-delete`, it deletes the group and the membership of every user of it with one request.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

`--force-delete` also requests the iam.assignment\_manage scope.

Requires the iam.group\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam groups delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--force-delete`\
  Delete the group also when users belong to it, removing every user from it (requests iam.assignment\_manage too).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam groups get

Show one group.

Reads the tenant's user groups. TYPE is the kind of user a group is for (e.g. EMPLOYEE,
CUSTOMER), and ACCESS CONTROLS counts the access controls it grants (`-o json` lists their
ids, [`epx iam groups access-controls`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-access-controls) reads them).

Requires the iam.group\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx iam groups get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, CODE, NAME, TYPE, ACCESS CONTROLS.
- `--language <language>`\

  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam groups list

List IAM groups.

Reads the tenant's user groups. TYPE is the kind of user a group is for (e.g. EMPLOYEE,
CUSTOMER), and ACCESS CONTROLS counts the access controls it grants (`-o json` lists their
ids, [`epx iam groups access-controls`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-access-controls) reads them).

Requires the iam.group\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx iam groups list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, CODE, NAME, TYPE, ACCESS CONTROLS.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam groups update

Upsert a group.

Replaces the group ID with the JSON in `--file`, as create takes it without id, or
creates it with that id where none exists (an upsert): give its name and every other
member to keep, as [`epx iam groups get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-get) prints it.
With metadata.version as read, Emporix changes it only if that is still its version.
Emporix answers with the id of one it created, and with nothing when it replaced one.
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Localized text in the body is a map of translations, e.g. `{"en": "Acme", "de": "Acme"}`,
as `-o json` of a read prints it, sent with Content-Language: \*. Emporix refuses a string in
its place.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the iam.group\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam groups update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam groups users

Read the users of a group, add and remove them.

Reads the users of a group, adds users to it and removes them from it.
Its writes change who may do what in the tenant.

Its reads require the iam.user\_read scope.
Its writes require the iam.assignment\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam groups users [flags]`, `epx iam groups users [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx iam groups users create`](#epx-iam-groups-users-create)\
  Add a user to a group.
- [`epx iam groups users delete`](#epx-iam-groups-users-delete)\
  Remove a user from a group.
- [`epx iam groups users delete-all`](#epx-iam-groups-users-delete-all)\
  Remove every user from a group.
- [`epx iam groups users list`](#epx-iam-groups-users-list)\
  List the users of a group.
- [`epx iam groups users update`](#epx-iam-groups-users-update)\
  Upsert the membership of a user in a group.

## epx iam groups users create

Add a user to a group.

Adds the user that `--user` names, of the kind that `--user-type` names (EMPLOYEE when left
out), to the group GROUP\_ID, or the one in `--file`, a JSON object with its userId and
userType. Emporix answers with the id of the membership; a user already in the group is
answered with a new id that is not the listed membership's, and no second membership is made
(read the members with [`epx iam groups users list`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-users-list)).
The user then gets the scopes of the group's access controls; a group of a vendor takes
only the vendor's employees.
GROUP\_ID is the ID that [`epx iam groups list`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the iam.assignment\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam groups users create GROUP_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--user <USER_ID>`\
  The USER\_ID of the user to add: the ID that [`epx iam users list`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-users-list) shows, or a customer's id (required without `--file`).
- `--user-type <TYPE>`\
  The TYPE of user: CUSTOMER or EMPLOYEE.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam groups users delete

Remove a user from a group.

Removes the user USER\_ID from the group GROUP\_ID: the user no longer gets the scopes of
its access controls.
GROUP\_ID is the ID that [`epx iam groups list`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-list) shows; an unknown GROUP\_ID or USER\_ID is answered as one that Emporix deleted (204 No Content).
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type USER\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the iam.assignment\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam groups users delete GROUP_ID USER_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

Remove every user from a group.

Removes every user from the group GROUP\_ID, which stays.
GROUP\_ID is the ID that [`epx iam groups list`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-groups-list) shows; an unknown one is answered as one that Emporix deleted (204 No Content).
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Deletes the membership of every user of the group with one request, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type GROUP\_ID at its prompt.

  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam scopes update

Upsert a custom scope.

Replaces the custom scope ID, e.g. acme.vehicle\_manage, with the JSON in `--file`, or creates
it where none exists (an upsert): its domain and description, a map of translations such
as `{"en": "Manage vehicles"}`.
With metadata.version as read, Emporix changes it only if that is still its version.
Emporix answers with the id of one it created, and with nothing when it replaced one.
Access controls grant scopes ([`epx iam access-controls update`](/emporix-cli/commands/iam#epx-iam-access-controls-update)).
It changes who may do what in the tenant.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the iam.scope\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx iam scopes update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx iam templates

Read IAM templates.

Reads IAM access control templates: sets of access controls that groups are built from
(`-o json` lists them).
list sorts by id unless `--sort` says otherwise; end another order with ,id:asc (e.g.
name.en:asc,id:asc), as Emporix wants a direction on every field, so pages do not overlap.

Requires the iam.template\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx iam templates [flags]`, `epx iam templates [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx iam templates list`](#epx-iam-templates-list)\
  List IAM templates.

## epx iam templates list

List IAM templates.

Reads IAM access control templates: sets of access controls that groups are built from
(`-o json` lists them).
list sorts by id unless `--sort` says otherwise; end another order with ,id:asc (e.g.
name.en:asc,id:asc), as Emporix wants a direction on every field, so pages do not overlap.

Requires the iam.template\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx iam templates list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, NAME, ACCESS CONTROLS.
- `--language <language>`\
  Language of localized table text; a missing translation shows another, labeled (`-o json` prints all). Default: `en`.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx imports

> Read import configurations, runs and imported records; start and schedule runs.

## epx imports

Reads the Import Service, which imports master data from external sources into Emporix:
configurations, their streams (each imports one source entity into an Emporix type),
schedules and runs, the errors and diagnostics of a run, the records imported, statistics,
job groups, health thresholds and the tenant's import limits. Emporix allows these reads
only with importtool.import\_trigger, with which epx also starts, retries, cancels and schedules runs.

Its reads require the importtool.import\_trigger scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.
Its writes require the importtool.import\_trigger scope.

**Command:** `epx imports [flags]`, `epx imports [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx imports configurations`](#epx-imports-configurations)\
  Read import configurations; start and schedule their runs.
- [`epx imports health-thresholds`](#epx-imports-health-thresholds)\
  Show the thresholds that rate the health of import streams.
- [`epx imports job-groups`](#epx-imports-job-groups)\
  List the job groups that scope the import statistics.
- [`epx imports license`](#epx-imports-license)\
  Show the tenant's import limits.
- [`epx imports records`](#epx-imports-records)\
  List the imported records of a type.
- [`epx imports runs`](#epx-imports-runs)\
  Read, cancel and retry import runs.
- [`epx imports statistics`](#epx-imports-statistics)\
  Show the import statistics of the last 30 days.
- [`epx imports streams`](#epx-imports-streams)\
  Read import streams and the records they imported.
- [`epx imports types`](#epx-imports-types)\
  List the types that hold imported records.

## epx imports configurations

Read import configurations; start and schedule their runs.

Reads import configurations, each a set of streams that run together: ENABLED says
whether it is active, VERSION counts its changes and MODIFIED is when it last changed. Its
description, source connection, creator and health thresholds are only in `-o json`. The
service returns the configurations whole, so they are read with one request.

Its reads require the importtool.import\_trigger scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.
Its writes require the importtool.import\_trigger scope.

**Command:** `epx imports configurations [flags]`, `epx imports configurations [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx imports configurations delete-schedule`](#epx-imports-configurations-delete-schedule)\
  Delete the run schedule of a configuration.
- [`epx imports configurations get`](#epx-imports-configurations-get)\
  Show one configuration.
- [`epx imports configurations list`](#epx-imports-configurations-list)\
  List import configurations.
- [`epx imports configurations runs`](#epx-imports-configurations-runs)\
  List the runs of a configuration.
- [`epx imports configurations schedule`](#epx-imports-configurations-schedule)\
  Show the run schedule of a configuration.
- [`epx imports configurations stream-order`](#epx-imports-configurations-stream-order)\
  Show the order the streams of a configuration run in.
- [`epx imports configurations streams`](#epx-imports-configurations-streams)\
  List the streams of a configuration.
- [`epx imports configurations trigger`](#epx-imports-configurations-trigger)\
  Start an import run of a configuration.
- [`epx imports configurations update-schedule`](#epx-imports-configurations-update-schedule)\
  Upsert the run schedule of a configuration.

## epx imports configurations delete-schedule

Delete the run schedule of a configuration.

Deletes the schedule of the configuration CONFIGURATION\_ID, which then runs only when it
is triggered. Emporix answers alike when there is no schedule, also of a configuration that
was deleted.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type CONFIGURATION\_ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.

**Command:** `epx imports configurations delete-schedule CONFIGURATION_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.

  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

## epx imports configurations trigger

Start an import run of a configuration.

Starts an import run of the configuration CONFIGURATION\_ID, a DELTA run unless `--mode` FULL,
and prints the run, QUEUED until a worker of the Import Service takes it. `--file` gives the
body instead, e.g. `{"mode": "FULL", "dryRun": true, "streamIds": ["ID"]}` for a dry run of
some streams, which maps and checks records but writes none. A configuration that has a run
QUEUED, RUNNING or RESUMABLE already is a conflict (exit 5). Emporix answers a run that it
refuses, e.g. of streams whose mappings were never published, as any other: the run ends
ABORTED, which `--wait` reports.
CONFIGURATION\_ID is the ID that [`epx imports configurations list`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-configurations-list) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--wait` then reads the job again every `--poll-interval`, as [`epx imports runs get`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-runs-get)
does and with the importtool.import\_trigger scope too, saying on standard error how its status
changes, until it ends: then it prints the job and exits 0 if it ended SUCCEEDED, else 1.
When `--wait-timeout` passes first, it prints the job as last read and exits 1; the job goes
on. When a read of the job fails, it prints the job as last read and exits as that read
does, e.g. 4 when the job is not found.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.

**Command:** `epx imports configurations trigger CONFIGURATION_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--mode <MODE>`\
  The MODE of the run, DELTA when not given: FULL or DELTA.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--poll-interval <duration>`\
  How often `--wait` reads the run, 1s or more (only with `--wait`). Default: `5s`.
- `--wait`\
  Wait until the run ends, then print it.
- `--wait-timeout <duration>`\
  How long `--wait` waits, 1s or more (only with `--wait`). Default: `30m`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx imports configurations trigger 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7 --mode FULL --wait
```

## epx imports configurations update-schedule

Upsert the run schedule of a configuration.

Sets when the configuration CONFIGURATION\_ID runs by itself, creating its schedule where
it has none (an upsert), and prints the schedule. `--cron` is a Spring cron expression with
six fields, seconds first, e.g. `"0 0 2 * * *"` for 02:00 every day (Emporix refuses one with
five: 400 Bad Request), evaluated in `--timezone`, an IANA time zone such as Europe/Berlin.
The schedule runs the configuration unless `--enabled=false`, which keeps it without running
it: epx always sends enabled, as the schedule is replaced whole. `--file` gives the body
instead.
CONFIGURATION\_ID is the ID that [`epx imports configurations list`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-configurations-list) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.

**Command:** `epx imports configurations update-schedule CONFIGURATION_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--cron <EXPRESSION>`\
  The Spring cron EXPRESSION of the schedule, six fields (required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--enabled`\
  Whether the schedule runs the configuration (`--enabled=false:` not). Default: `true`.
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--timezone <ZONE>`\
  The IANA time ZONE the expression is evaluated in.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx imports configurations update-schedule 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7 --cron "0 0 2 * * *" --timezone Europe/Berlin
```

  Print table and csv without the header row.
