## epx imports runs cancel

Cancel an import run.

Asks the import run ID to stop, and prints what Emporix answers: whether it accepted the
cancellation. A QUEUED run is CANCELLED at once; a running one stops when it can, or with
`--force` at once, which also unblocks its configuration. A RESUMABLE run stops only with
`--force`: without it, a conflict (exit 5). Emporix answers a run that is unknown or ended
already with 409 Conflict and `"accepted"`: false, which epx prints as the answer (exit 5).
ID is the one that [`epx imports configurations runs CONFIGURATION_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-configurations-runs) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.

**Command:** `epx imports runs cancel ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--force`\
  Stop the run at once.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx imports runs diagnostics

List the source rows behind a run's repeated keys and missing parents.

Reads the source rows behind a run's feed-quality counters, which do not fail a run: KIND is
REPEATED\_KEY for a row whose KEY the run had already imported (OCCURRENCE times before), or
UNRESOLVED\_PARENT for a child line whose parent was missing: LINKING FIELD and LINKING VALUE
are the parent key it points at, WAITING LINES the lines waiting for that parent. The service
keeps a capped sample per stream and kind; `-o json` says how many rows it recorded, its cap
and whether a stream reached it (the run's counters give the totals). Every recorded row is
read, up to 50000; a run that recorded more fails, and its rows are read per stream:
[`epx api get /importtool/{tenant}/runs/RUN_ID/diagnostics -p streamId=ID -p limit=50000 --scope importtool.import_trigger`](/emporix-cli/commands/api#epx-api-get).
RUN\_ID is the ID that [`epx imports configurations runs CONFIGURATION_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-configurations-runs) shows; an unknown one lists nothing.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx imports runs diagnostics RUN_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting importtool.import\_trigger, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among KIND, STREAM, KEY, LINKING FIELD, LINKING VALUE, WAITING LINES, OCCURRENCE.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx imports runs get

Show one run.

Reads import runs; a run's ID is the one that [`epx imports configurations runs CONFIGURATION_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-configurations-runs) shows.

or ABORTED (refused: nothing was read), MODE FULL or DELTA, followed by dry run for a run that

read and FAILED those that failed. `-o json` adds its other counters, message and queue position.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx imports runs get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting importtool.import\_trigger, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, STATUS, MODE, STARTED, FINISHED, READ, FAILED.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx imports runs retry

Run the failed records of an import run again.

Starts a run that imports again only the records that failed in the import run ID, and
prints it, QUEUED until a worker takes it; the run ID keeps its counters. A configuration
that has a run QUEUED, RUNNING or RESUMABLE already is a conflict (exit 5).
ID is the one that [`epx imports configurations runs CONFIGURATION_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-configurations-runs) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--wait` then reads the job again every `--poll-interval`, as [`epx imports runs get`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-runs-get)
does and with the importtool.import\_trigger scope too, saying on standard error how its status
changes, until it ends: then it prints the job and exits 0 if it ended SUCCEEDED, else 1.
When `--wait-timeout` passes first, it prints the job as last read and exits 1; the job goes
on. When a read of the job fails, it prints the job as last read and exits as that read
does, e.g. 4 when the job is not found.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.

**Command:** `epx imports runs retry ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--poll-interval <duration>`\
  How often `--wait` reads the run, 1s or more (only with `--wait`). Default: `5s`.
- `--wait`\
  Wait until the run ends, then print it.
- `--wait-timeout <duration>`\
  How long `--wait` waits, 1s or more (only with `--wait`). Default: `30m`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx imports runs streams

Show the progress of each stream of a run.

Reads the progress of each stream of an import run: STATUS is QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED,
PARTIAL, FAILED, SKIPPED or ABORTED (not run because of its configuration, such as mappings
never published, as MESSAGE says), then the records the stream read, created, updated,
skipped as unchanged, deleted and failed to import. A queued run lists nothing yet.
RUN\_ID is the ID that [`epx imports configurations runs CONFIGURATION_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-configurations-runs) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx imports runs streams RUN_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting importtool.import\_trigger, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among STREAM, STATUS, READ, CREATED, UPDATED, SKIPPED, DELETED, FAILED, MESSAGE.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx imports statistics

Show the import statistics of the last 30 days.

Reads the import statistics of the last 30 days for the whole tenant: RUNS counts the runs
started, SUCCEEDED, PARTIAL, FAILED and CANCELLED how they ended, ACTIVE those queued or
running now, and RECORDS READ and RECORDS FAILED the records. `-o json` adds the rates, a daily
series, each stream's health, the failing streams, an error breakdown and the streams added
or removed. Another window or scope, e.g. one configuration ([`epx imports job-groups`](/emporix-cli/commands/imports#epx-imports-job-groups) lists
sets of them): [`epx api get /importtool/{tenant}/stats -p configId=ID -p from=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z -p granularity=WEEK --scope importtool.import_trigger`](/emporix-cli/commands/api#epx-api-get).

Requires the importtool.import\_trigger scope.
Opt-in: epx requests a write-capable scope for a read only when given `--allow-write-scope`.

**Command:** `epx imports statistics [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--allow-write-scope`\
  Opt in to requesting importtool.import\_trigger, which can also change data (required).
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among RUNS, SUCCEEDED, PARTIAL, FAILED, CANCELLED, ACTIVE, RECORDS READ, RECORDS FAILED.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx indexing

> Read and configure search index providers; reindex.

## epx indexing

Reads and configures the search index providers (e.g. Algolia) and starts and follows
reindex jobs.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Its writes require the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing [flags]`, `epx indexing [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx indexing providers`](#epx-indexing-providers)\
  Read, create, update and delete index providers.
- [`epx indexing reindex`](#epx-indexing-reindex)\
  Reindex every product (deprecated by Emporix).
- [`epx indexing reindex-jobs`](#epx-indexing-reindex-jobs)\
  Read and start reindex jobs.

## epx indexing providers

Read, create, update and delete index providers.

Reads index provider configurations. Search and write keys are only in `-o json`;
[`epx indexing providers public`](/emporix-cli/commands/indexing#epx-indexing-providers-public) shows what a storefront sees and needs no scope.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Its writes require the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing providers [flags]`, `epx indexing providers [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx indexing providers create`](#epx-indexing-providers-create)\
  Create an index provider configuration.
- [`epx indexing providers delete`](#epx-indexing-providers-delete)\
  Delete an index provider configuration.
- [`epx indexing providers get`](#epx-indexing-providers-get)\
  Show one provider.
- [`epx indexing providers list`](#epx-indexing-providers-list)\
  List index providers.
- [`epx indexing providers public`](#epx-indexing-providers-public)\
  Read index providers as a storefront sees them.
- [`epx indexing providers update`](#epx-indexing-providers-update)\
  Replace an index provider configuration.

## epx indexing providers create

Create an index provider configuration.

Creates the configuration of an index provider, whose ID is the provider's name.
The JSON in `--file` holds provider (ALGOLIA or BATTERY\_INCLUDED, required), active,
applicationId, indexName, searchKey, writeKey and, for BATTERY\_INCLUDED, excludedMixinKeys
or includedMixinPaths. Only one provider can be active at a time. Emporix checks the keys
of BATTERY\_INCLUDED before it stores them: it refuses invalid ones (400 Bad Request, exit 1)
and stores nothing when it cannot check them (502 Bad Gateway).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing providers create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx indexing providers create --file algolia.json --dry-run
```

## epx indexing providers delete

Delete an index provider configuration.

Deletes the configuration of PROVIDER, as [`epx indexing providers list`](/emporix-cli/commands/indexing#epx-indexing-providers-list) shows it.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type PROVIDER at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing providers delete PROVIDER [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx indexing providers update

Replace an index provider configuration.

Replaces the configuration of PROVIDER, as [`epx indexing providers list`](/emporix-cli/commands/indexing#epx-indexing-providers-list) shows it. The
reference documents not found (exit 4) for an unknown one, as update creates none; for
BATTERY\_INCLUDED Emporix checks the write key first, so an invalid configuration is answered
400 before that (the not-found answer was not checked with a valid key).
The JSON in `--file` holds provider (ALGOLIA or BATTERY\_INCLUDED, required), active,
applicationId, indexName, searchKey, writeKey and, for BATTERY\_INCLUDED, excludedMixinKeys
or includedMixinPaths. Only one provider can be active at a time. Emporix checks the keys
of BATTERY\_INCLUDED before it stores them: it refuses invalid ones (400 Bad Request, exit 1)
and stores nothing when it cannot check them (502 Bad Gateway).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing providers update PROVIDER [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx indexing providers update ALGOLIA --file algolia.json
```

## epx indexing reindex

Reindex every product (deprecated by Emporix).

Reindexes every product of the tenant, sending the mode FULL, the only one there is, unless
`--file` gives the body. Emporix has deprecated this endpoint: [`epx indexing reindex-jobs create`](/emporix-cli/commands/indexing#epx-indexing-reindex-jobs-create)
starts a reindex job instead, which its `--wait` follows. For BATTERY\_INCLUDED, Emporix checks
the stored keys first (400 Bad Request when they are invalid, 502 when it cannot check them).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing reindex [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx indexing reindex --dry-run
```

## epx indexing reindex-jobs

Read and start reindex jobs.

Reads reindex jobs and their progress. Emporix fails when asked for the number of jobs,
so list cannot check it: a job that moves between pages while they are read can be shown
twice or missed.

Its reads require the indexing.search\_view scope.
Its writes require the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing reindex-jobs [flags]`, `epx indexing reindex-jobs [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx indexing reindex-jobs create`](#epx-indexing-reindex-jobs-create)\
  Start a reindex job.
- [`epx indexing reindex-jobs get`](#epx-indexing-reindex-jobs-get)\
  Show one reindex job.
- [`epx indexing reindex-jobs list`](#epx-indexing-reindex-jobs-list)\
  List reindex jobs.

## epx indexing reindex-jobs create

Start a reindex job.

Starts a job that indexes every entity of a type again: PRODUCT, ORDER or a custom entity
type ([`epx custom-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/custom-entities#epx-custom-entities-list)); with `--rag`, it also embeds products for RAG search.
Emporix answers with the job, or with the job of that type that is IN\_PROGRESS already.
A job is PENDING while others take its turn, PUBLISHED once every entity was sent to the
index and SUCCESS once the index took them all. For BATTERY\_INCLUDED, Emporix checks the
stored keys before it starts a PRODUCT job (400 Bad Request when they are invalid, 502 when
it cannot check them).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--wait` then reads the job again every `--poll-interval`, as [`epx indexing reindex-jobs get`](/emporix-cli/commands/indexing#epx-indexing-reindex-jobs-get)
does and with the indexing.search\_view scope too, saying on standard error how its status
changes, until it ends: then it prints the job and exits 0 if it ended SUCCESS, else 1.
When `--wait-timeout` passes first, it prints the job as last read and exits 1; the job goes
on. When a read of the job fails, it prints the job as last read and exits as that read
does, e.g. 4 when the job is not found.

Requires the indexing.search\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing reindex-jobs create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--entity-type <TYPE>`\
  The TYPE of the entities to reindex: PRODUCT, ORDER or a custom entity type (required without `--file`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--poll-interval <duration>`\
  How often `--wait` reads the reindex job, 1s or more (only with `--wait`). Default: `5s`.
- `--rag`\
  Embed products for RAG search too (PRODUCT only).
- `--wait`\
  Wait until the reindex job ends, then print it.
- `--wait-timeout <duration>`\
  How long `--wait` waits, 1s or more (only with `--wait`). Default: `30m`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx indexing reindex-jobs create --entity-type PRODUCT --rag --wait
epx indexing reindex-jobs create --file reindex.json --yes
```

## epx indexing reindex-jobs get

Show one reindex job.

Reads reindex jobs and their progress. Emporix fails when asked for the number of jobs,
so list cannot check it: a job that moves between pages while they are read can be shown
twice or missed.

Requires the indexing.search\_view scope.

**Command:** `epx indexing reindex-jobs get ID [flags]`

# epx invoice-jobs

> Create and read invoice jobs.

## epx invoice-jobs

Creates and reads the jobs that generate the invoices of orders.

Its reads require the invoice.invoice\_view scope.
Its writes require the invoice.invoice\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx invoice-jobs [flags]`, `epx invoice-jobs [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx invoice-jobs create`](#epx-invoice-jobs-create)\
  Start an invoice job.
- [`epx invoice-jobs get`](#epx-invoice-jobs-get)\
  Show the status of an invoice job.

## epx invoice-jobs create

Start an invoice job.

Starts a job that generates the invoices of orders: of those that `--order` names
(`--type` MANUAL, which requires one at least), or of those ready for an invoice that the
tenant's invoice configuration selects (`--type` AUTOMATIC, which takes no `--order`).
Without an invoice configuration of the tenant's own, an order is ready for an invoice when
its mixins.generalAttributes.extendedOrderStatus is 70, 75 or 76 ([`epx orders create`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-create)
stores 10; [`epx orders patch`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-patch) changes it); the job's entry of an order with 10 fails as not
ready. Invoicing a ready order calls the tenant's Pick-Pack service: where that service is
not reachable, the entry fails at the VALIDATION step.
Emporix answers with the job's id (jobId), which [`epx invoice-jobs get ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/invoice-jobs#epx-invoice-jobs-get) reads.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the invoice.invoice\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx invoice-jobs create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `--order <ID>`\
  The ID of an order to invoice, repeatable (only with `--type` MANUAL, which requires it).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--type <TYPE>`\
  The TYPE of job: MANUAL or AUTOMATIC (required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx invoice-jobs create --type MANUAL --order O1001 --order O1002
epx invoice-jobs create --type AUTOMATIC --yes
```

## epx invoice-jobs get

Show the status of an invoice job.

Reads an invoice job: STATUS is IN\_PROGRESS or DONE and TYPE MANUAL (orders chosen when
the job was created) or AUTOMATIC (orders that the tenant's configuration selects). ORDERS
counts the orders the job processed, of which INVOICED got an invoice, FAILED did not and
PENDING wait for one. Each order's entry in invoices (orderId and status; errorStep and
message for a failure, e.g. an order not ready for invoicing; for a success, the reference
documents the invoice number and download link) is only in `-o json`.
ID is the job id that creating the job returned. Emporix answers an unknown job with
500 Internal Server Error (the reference documents 404), so get fails with exit code 1.

Requires the invoice.invoice\_view scope.

**Command:** `epx invoice-jobs get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among STATUS, TYPE, ORDERS, INVOICED, FAILED, PENDING.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx labels

> Read, create, change and delete labels.

## epx labels

Reads labels, the badges shown on products. OVERLAY is the label's overlay flag and
POSITION its overlay position, as sent; MEDIA is the id of its image (image URLs are only
in `-o json`), and DESCRIPTION is often HTML.

Its reads need no OAuth scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx labels [flags]`, `epx labels [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx labels create`](#epx-labels-create)\
  Create a label.
- [`epx labels delete`](#epx-labels-delete)\
  Delete a label.
- [`epx labels get`](#epx-labels-get)\
  Show one label.
- [`epx labels list`](#epx-labels-list)\
  List labels.
- [`epx labels patch`](#epx-labels-patch)\
  Change members of a label.
- [`epx labels update`](#epx-labels-update)\
  Replace a label.

## epx labels create

Create a label.

Creates a label from the JSON in `--file`, such as
`{"name": "Free shipping", "description": "<p>Ships free</p>", "overlay": {"isTrue": true, "position": 1}}`,
and prints the label that Emporix answers with. Emporix generates its id unless the JSON names one;
an id that exists already is a conflict.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the label.label\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx labels create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx labels delete

Delete a label.

Deletes the label ID.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the label.label\_delete scope.

**Command:** `epx labels delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\

- `--yes`\

# epx legal-entities

> Read and change legal entities (B2B companies); read their parents.

## epx legal-entities

Reads and changes legal entities, the companies of B2B customers and their subsidiaries,
personal data included.
create and update ID (an upsert) send the JSON body of `--file`; delete ID sends none.

Its reads require the customermanagement.legalentity\_read scope.
Its writes require the customermanagement.legalentity\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx legal-entities [flags]`, `epx legal-entities [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx legal-entities create`](#epx-legal-entities-create)\
  Create one legal entity.
- [`epx legal-entities delete`](#epx-legal-entities-delete)\
  Delete one legal entity.
- [`epx legal-entities get`](#epx-legal-entities-get)\
  Show one legal entity.
- [`epx legal-entities hierarchy`](#epx-legal-entities-hierarchy)\
  List a legal entity and its parents.
- [`epx legal-entities list`](#epx-legal-entities-list)\
  List legal entities.
- [`epx legal-entities search`](#epx-legal-entities-search)\
  Search legal entities.
- [`epx legal-entities update`](#epx-legal-entities-update)\
  Upsert one legal entity.

## epx legal-entities create

Create one legal entity.

Creates the legal entity that the JSON body of `--file` describes, shaped as
[`epx legal-entities get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/legal-entities#epx-legal-entities-get) prints one:
name (required), type (COMPANY, the default, or SUBSIDIARY), parentId (the legal
entity a subsidiary belongs to), legalInfo, accountLimit, customerGroups (IAM groups),
entitiesAddresses and approvalGroup (its customer locations and contact assignments),
restrictions and mixins; parentId, customerGroups, entitiesAddresses and approvalGroup must
name items that exist (400 Bad Request, exit 1, otherwise), the last three each as
`{"id": ...}` or in full, as get prints it.
Without an id, Emporix makes one, and answers with it; an id that exists already is a
conflict (exit 5).
A create that Emporix refuses as a conflict may still make the IAM customer groups of
the legal entity.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the customermanagement.legalentity\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx legal-entities create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx legal-entities delete

Delete one legal entity.

Deletes the legal entity ID; it sends no body.
ID is the ID that [`epx legal-entities list`](/emporix-cli/commands/legal-entities#epx-legal-entities-list) shows; an unknown one is answered as one that Emporix deleted (204 No Content).
The assignments are the contact assignments of it and of its subsidiaries and the segment
assignments that name it; the IAM customer groups those still in its customerGroups. Its
customer locations stay, and its customers no longer name it (one with no other legal
entity becomes a B2C customer).

Deletes the legal entity with its subsidiaries, assignments and IAM customer groups with one request, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the customermanagement.legalentity\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx legal-entities delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx legal-entities get

# epx media

> Read, upload, link and change media assets.

## epx media

Reads media assets: files Emporix stores (BLOB) or links to files elsewhere (LINK). ACCESS
is PUBLIC or PRIVATE; STATUS is PENDING until an upload completes, then READY or empty;
BYTES is the file size as sent, and REFERENCES the items an asset belongs to (type and
id). URLs are only in `-o json`; [`epx media download-url`](/emporix-cli/commands/media#epx-media-download-url) gives one that downloads the file.

Its reads require the media.asset\_read scope.
Its writes require the media.asset\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx media [flags]`, `epx media [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx media create`](#epx-media-create)\
  Create a media asset: a link, or a file to upload.
- [`epx media delete`](#epx-media-delete)\
  Delete a media asset.
- [`epx media download-url`](#epx-media-download-url)\
  Show a URL that downloads an asset.
- [`epx media get`](#epx-media-get)\
  Show one asset.
- [`epx media list`](#epx-media-list)\
  List media assets.
- [`epx media patch`](#epx-media-patch)\
  Change members of a media asset.
- [`epx media start-upload`](#epx-media-start-upload)\
  Start an upload of a file straight to storage.
- [`epx media update`](#epx-media-update)\
  Replace a media asset, or the file of one.

## epx media create

Create a media asset: a link, or a file to upload.

Creates a media asset from the JSON in `--file` and prints its id. A LINK asset points to a
file elsewhere, e.g. `{"type": "LINK", "access": "PUBLIC", "url": "https://example.com/a.pdf"}`.
A BLOB asset is a file that Emporix stores: `--upload` PATH sends the file in a
multipart/form-data form, with the JSON of `--file` as its body field, e.g.
`{"type": "BLOB", "access": "PRIVATE", "details": {"filename": "a", "mimeType": "application/pdf"}}`.
Emporix takes a file of up to 30 MB including the form; a large file may need a longer
`--timeout`, e.g. `--timeout` 5m, as it bounds the whole request.
Without `--upload`, the JSON of a BLOB asset is refused before anything is sent, as Emporix
takes one only with its file.
refIds assigns the asset to items, e.g. `[{"type": "PRODUCT", "id": "100200"}]`; an asset of a
PRODUCT or CATEGORY must be PUBLIC. An id that exists already is a conflict (exit 5).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the media.asset\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx media create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON in PATH, sent byte for byte: the request body, or the body field of the form of a file to upload (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--upload <PATH>`\
  Upload the file in PATH (up to 30 MB including the form) as the file of a BLOB asset, in a multipart/form-data form with the JSON of `--file`; a large file may need a longer `--timeout`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx media create --file link.json --dry-run
epx media create --upload manual.pdf --file manual.json
```

## epx media delete

Delete a media asset.

Deletes the media asset ID, and the file of a BLOB asset. An unknown ID is no error: Emporix
answers as for a deleted asset.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the media.asset\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx media delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx media download-url

Show a URL that downloads an asset.

Reads a URL that downloads an asset. For a private stored file it is a signed URL that
works without a token until EXPIRES (15 minutes by default), so treat it as a secret; for
a public file or a link, PROVIDER CLOUDINARY or LINK, it is the asset's permanent URL.
Reading the URL of a pending upload whose file is stored makes Emporix complete it; one
whose file is not stored yet fails.
ASSET\_ID is the ID that [`epx media list`](/emporix-cli/commands/media#epx-media-list) shows; an unknown one is not found.

Requires the media.asset\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx media download-url ASSET_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among PROVIDER, EXPIRES, URL.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx media get

Show one asset.

Reads media assets: files Emporix stores (BLOB) or links to files elsewhere (LINK). ACCESS
is PUBLIC or PRIVATE; STATUS is PENDING until an upload completes, then READY or empty;
BYTES is the file size as sent, and REFERENCES the items an asset belongs to (type and
id). URLs are only in `-o json`; [`epx media download-url`](/emporix-cli/commands/media#epx-media-download-url) gives one that downloads the file.

Requires the media.asset\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx media get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, TYPE, ACCESS, STATUS, FILE, MIME TYPE, BYTES, REFERENCES.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx media list

List media assets.

Reads media assets: files Emporix stores (BLOB) or links to files elsewhere (LINK). ACCESS
is PUBLIC or PRIVATE; STATUS is PENDING until an upload completes, then READY or empty;
BYTES is the file size as sent, and REFERENCES the items an asset belongs to (type and
id). URLs are only in `-o json`; [`epx media download-url`](/emporix-cli/commands/media#epx-media-download-url) gives one that downloads the file.

Requires the media.asset\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx media list [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, TYPE, ACCESS, STATUS, FILE, MIME TYPE, BYTES, REFERENCES.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx media patch

  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.

  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx media start-upload

Start an upload of a file straight to storage.

Starts an upload session: creates a PENDING BLOB asset from the JSON in `--file`, as create
takes it (`"uploadType"`: `"form"` asks for a form instead of a PUT for a PRIVATE asset), and
prints where to send its file: the method, URL and headers or form fields of a request to
the storage (GCS for a PRIVATE asset, CLOUDINARY for a PUBLIC one), valid for 15 minutes
or an hour, so treat it as a secret. epx does not send the file there; once the storage
has it, the asset is READY. Emporix enables direct uploads per tenant; elsewhere it answers
403 Forbidden (exit 1) and creates no asset.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the media.asset\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx media start-upload [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx media update

Replace a media asset, or the file of one.

Replaces the media asset ID with the JSON in `--file`; its type and access cannot change.
The JSON of a LINK asset gives its url; a BLOB asset is replaced with its file: `--upload` PATH
sends the new file in a multipart/form-data form, with the JSON as its body field
(up to 30 MB including the form; a large file may need a longer
`--timeout`, e.g. `--timeout` 5m). [`epx media patch`](/emporix-cli/commands/media#epx-media-patch) changes a BLOB asset without sending its
file again.
Without `--upload`, the JSON of a BLOB asset is refused before anything is sent, as Emporix
takes one only with its file.
An unknown ID is not found (exit 4).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PUT. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the media.asset\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx media update ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON in PATH, sent byte for byte: the request body, or the body field of the form of a file to upload (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--upload <PATH>`\
  Upload the file in PATH (up to 30 MB including the form) as the file of a BLOB asset, in a multipart/form-data form with the JSON of `--file`; a large file may need a longer `--timeout`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx orders

> Read, create and change orders and their status.

## epx orders

Reads, creates and changes sales orders, personal data included, and their status:
[`epx orders transition`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-transition) moves an order to another status, `add-entries` and `recalculate`
change its entries, and `split` splits it into sub-orders by vendor.

Its reads require the order.order\_read scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx orders [flags]`, `epx orders [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx orders add-entries`](#epx-orders-add-entries)\
  Add products to an order, or change its entries.
- [`epx orders count`](#epx-orders-count)\
  Count orders.
- [`epx orders create`](#epx-orders-create)\
  Create an order.
- [`epx orders delete`](#epx-orders-delete)\
  Delete one order.
- [`epx orders get`](#epx-orders-get)\
  Show one order.
- [`epx orders history`](#epx-orders-history)\
  Show the status changes of an order.
- [`epx orders list`](#epx-orders-list)\
  List orders.
- [`epx orders patch`](#epx-orders-patch)\
  Change members of an order.
- [`epx orders recalculate`](#epx-orders-recalculate)\
  Set the delivered amounts of an order and recalculate it.
- [`epx orders search`](#epx-orders-search)\
  Search orders.
- [`epx orders split`](#epx-orders-split)\
  Split an order into sub-orders by vendor.
- [`epx orders transition`](#epx-orders-transition)\
  Move an order to another status.
- [`epx orders transitions`](#epx-orders-transitions)\
  List the statuses an order can move to next.
- [`epx orders update`](#epx-orders-update)\
  Replace an order.

## epx orders add-entries

Add products to an order, or change its entries.

Adds products to the order ORDER\_ID, or changes the quantity of its entries, and
recalculates it: the JSON object in `--file` holds entries, each with the productId of a
product to add or the entryId of an entry to change (an id in the order's entries, as
[`epx orders get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-get) prints them), and its quantity; 0 removes the entry.
Emporix answers with the order recalculated, which it stores only with `--store`: without
it, the order stays as it is. Emporix refuses to change the entries of a COMPLETED order
with 400 Bad Request (exit 1).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the order.order\_update scope.

**Command:** `epx orders add-entries ORDER_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--store`\
  Store the recalculated order; without it, Emporix only answers with it.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders count

Count orders.

Prints the number of sales orders, or of those that an Emporix q filter finds
(`--query`), which Emporix reports in a header without sending the orders: a master order
and each of its sub-orders count once, as list lists them. `-o json` prints the number alone.
Emporix counts 0 for a filter on id or customer.id although list finds the orders (seen
live): list them instead.

Requires the order.order\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx orders count [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among COUNT.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, passed as given, e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders create

Create an order.

Creates an order on behalf of a customer from the JSON object in `--file`, shaped as
[`epx orders get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-get) prints one (entries, customer, siteCode, currency and
calculatedPrice among others). Emporix makes the order's id and answers with it: an id in
the body is ignored, so sending the body again creates another order (with checkout
true, at most one per cartId). It stores the status CREATED for IN\_CHECKOUT, and sets
mixins.generalAttributes (extendedOrderStatus `"10"`, orderNumber and customerFirstOrder)
whatever the body says; [`epx orders patch`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-patch) can change them afterwards, e.g. to make the
order ready for [`epx invoice-jobs create`](/emporix-cli/commands/invoice-jobs#epx-invoice-jobs-create). It also adds an address of the order to the
customer's addresses, as a default one tagged shipping and billing, so a customer who had
a default address then has two default addresses.

Give the order's and its entries' metadata.mixins the URLs of the schemas of their mixins,
as orders placed in a checkout carry them: without them, [`epx orders add-entries --store`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-add-entries),
`recalculate`, `patch --recalculate` and `split` fail on the order with 400 Bad Request
(exit 1).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the order.order\_create scope.

**Command:** `epx orders create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders delete

Delete one order.

Deletes the order ID; it sends no body.
ID is the ID that [`epx orders list`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-list) shows.

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the order.order\_delete scope.

**Command:** `epx orders delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders get

Reads sales orders, personal data included. TYPE is MASTER\_ORDER or SUB\_ORDER for an order
split, for example by vendor: the master and its sub-orders are all listed, so do not add
up their totals. STATUS is IN\_CHECKOUT, CREATED, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, SHIPPED or COMPLETED,
CUSTOMER the customer's email (or name), ITEMS the number of order entries and TOTAL the

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders patch

Change members of an order.

Changes the members of the order ID that the JSON object in `--file` gives, such as its
shippingAddress or mixins, and keeps the others.
Emporix does not check the order's metadata.version: it applies the change whatever version
the body names, and does not answer a stale one with 409 Conflict; an unknown order is not
found (exit 4).
ID is the ID that [`epx orders list`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-list) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends PATCH. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

`--completed` also requests the order.order\_update\_completed scope.

Requires the order.order\_update scope.

**Command:** `epx orders patch ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--completed`\
  For an order that is COMPLETED, which Emporix changes only with one more scope (requests order.order\_update\_completed too).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--recalculate`\
  Have Emporix recalculate the whole order, coupon discounts included.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders recalculate

Set the delivered amounts of an order and recalculate it.

Sets the amounts delivered of entries of the order ORDER\_ID and recalculates the
order: the JSON object in `--file` holds entries, each with its entryId (an id in the
order's entries, as [`epx orders get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-get) prints them) and deliveredAmount, and
optionally deliveredAmountInPc and unit, the unit of deliveredAmount (e.g. GRM).
Emporix refuses to recalculate a COMPLETED order with 400 Bad Request (exit 1), whatever
the scopes.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Emporix answers with a sentence of text, which epx prints as a JSON string.

Requires the order.order\_update scope.

**Command:** `epx orders recalculate ORDER_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders search

Search orders.

Reads the sales orders, personal data included, that an Emporix q filter finds
(`--query`; without it, every order).
It reads and shows them as [`epx orders list`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-list) does.

Changes nothing: Emporix serves this read as POST with a JSON body, which the
flags make or `--body` gives whole.

Requires the order.order\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx orders search [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--body <FILE>`\
  Send the JSON request body in FILE as given (- reads standard input) instead of the one the other flags make.
- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, TYPE, STATUS, CREATED, CUSTOMER, SITE, ITEMS, TOTAL.
- `--limit <n>`\
  Print at most n items; paged reads stop early where they safely can (0: every item).
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.
- `--query <filter>`\
  Emporix q filter, sent as given in the request body, not in the URL (empty: no filter), e.g. code:(A1,A2); space-separated conditions must all match (fields mostly as in `-o json`).
- `--sort <order>`\
  Emporix sort order, passed as given, e.g. code or name.en:desc,code; fields mostly as in `-o json` (Emporix may ignore an unknown one).
- `--stream`\
  Print items as JSON Lines as soon as they are checked, page by page on paged lists, reading up to 10000 pages where a list without it stops after 1000: a check failing on a later page exits 1 after the pages before it (excludes `-o`, `--columns` and `--no-headers`).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders split

Split an order into sub-orders by vendor.

Splits the order ORDER\_ID into sub-orders, one per vendor of its entries, sending
splitBy VENDOR\_ID, the only criterion that Emporix offers, unless `--file` gives the body.
Emporix splits only an order with status CREATED that was not split before and has no
discounts: it becomes the MASTER\_ORDER of the SUB\_ORDERs that the response names. An order
whose entries name no vendor stays as it is (the response names no subOrders); an order
split before, or a sub-order, is refused with 400 Bad Request (exit 1).

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the order.order\_update scope.

**Command:** `epx orders split ORDER_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders transition

Move an order to another status.

Moves the order ORDER\_ID to the status that `--status` names, one that
[`epx orders transitions ORDER_ID`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-transitions) lists: CONFIRMED or DECLINED from CREATED, COMPLETED or
DECLINED from CONFIRMED, and none from COMPLETED or DECLINED. Emporix refuses another with
403 Forbidden (exit 1) and says why, and answers the order's own status as done,
without an entry in its history. ORDER\_ID is the ID that [`epx orders list`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-list) shows.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the order.order\_update scope.

**Command:** `epx orders transition ORDER_ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--status <STATUS>`\
  The STATUS to move the order to: IN\_CHECKOUT, CREATED, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, SHIPPED or COMPLETED (required without `--file`).
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

## epx orders update

Replace an order.

Replaces the order ID with the order in `--file`, a JSON object as
[`epx orders get ID -o json`](/emporix-cli/commands/orders#epx-orders-get) prints it.

**Command:** `epx orders update ID [flags]`

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--recalculate`\
  Have Emporix recalculate the whole order, coupon discounts included.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx payment-modes

> Read, create, update and delete payment modes.

## epx payment-modes

Reads the tenant's payment modes, and creates, updates and deletes them (create and
update send the JSON of `--file`). Provider configurations hold credentials, which the reads
show only in `-o json` and the writes send and print as given. [`epx payment-modes public`](/emporix-cli/commands/payment-modes#epx-payment-modes-public)
shows what a storefront sees and needs no scope.

Its reads require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.
Its writes require the payment-gateway.paymentmodes\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-modes [flags]`, `epx payment-modes [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx payment-modes create`](#epx-payment-modes-create)\
  Create a payment mode.
- [`epx payment-modes delete`](#epx-payment-modes-delete)\
  Delete a payment mode.
- [`epx payment-modes get`](#epx-payment-modes-get)\
  Show one payment mode.
- [`epx payment-modes list`](#epx-payment-modes-list)\
  List payment modes.
- [`epx payment-modes public`](#epx-payment-modes-public)\
  Read payment modes as a storefront sees them.
- [`epx payment-modes update`](#epx-payment-modes-update)\
  Update a payment mode.

## epx payment-modes create

Create a payment mode.

Creates the payment mode in `--file`, a JSON object with its code and provider (both
required; PROVIDER as list shows it), active, and the provider's configuration: a map of
string values such as Spreedly/GatewayToken, credentials included. Emporix answers with
the payment mode, its configuration included, or, for a code that another mode has, with
400 Bad Request (exit 1); the reference documents 409 Conflict (exit 5) for that case instead.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the payment-gateway.paymentmodes\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-modes create [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx payment-modes create --file invoice.json --dry-run
```

## epx payment-modes delete

Delete a payment mode.

Deletes the payment mode ID, which storefronts then no longer offer.

ID is the ID that [`epx payment-modes list`](/emporix-cli/commands/payment-modes#epx-payment-modes-list) shows; an unknown one is not found (exit 4).

Deletes data, which cannot be undone.
On a terminal, epx sends DELETE only once you type ID at its prompt.
`--yes` sends without asking (required without a terminal);
`--dry-run` prints the request instead of sending it.

Requires the payment-gateway.paymentmodes\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-modes delete ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

# epx payment-transactions

> Read payment transactions; authorize, capture, refund and cancel payments.

## epx payment-transactions

Reads payment transactions, personal data included, and runs payments through the
tenant's payment providers: authorize starts a transaction for an order, capture collects
an authorized amount, refund returns a captured one and cancel voids an authorization.
Capture, refund and cancel move money.

Its reads require the payment-gateway.paymenttransactions\_read scope.
Its writes require different OAuth scopes; the help of each names them.

**Command:** `epx payment-transactions [flags]`, `epx payment-transactions [command]`

**Flags:** only the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Subcommands**

- [`epx payment-transactions authorize`](#epx-payment-transactions-authorize)\
  Authorize a payment.
- [`epx payment-transactions cancel`](#epx-payment-transactions-cancel)\
  Cancel an authorized payment.
- [`epx payment-transactions capture`](#epx-payment-transactions-capture)\
  Capture an authorized payment.
- [`epx payment-transactions get`](#epx-payment-transactions-get)\
  Show one payment transaction.
- [`epx payment-transactions list`](#epx-payment-transactions-list)\
  List payment transactions.
- [`epx payment-transactions refund`](#epx-payment-transactions-refund)\
  Refund a captured payment.

## epx payment-transactions authorize

Authorize a payment.

Authorizes the payment of an order with a payment mode, as `--file`, a JSON object, gives
them: order.id, paymentModeId, amountToAuthorize and currency, and what the provider
needs, such as creditCardToken. The provider reserves the amount, which capture then
collects. Emporix answers with the paymentTransactionId and, where the customer must
finish the payment with the provider, where to send them (externalPaymentRedirectURL).

Emporix answers whether the operation succeeded (successful). epx prints the response and
exits with 1 unless it says that it did: where it says that it failed (successful false,
with a message), and where it does not say, when it may have been carried out all the same.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the payment-gateway.authorize\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-transactions authorize [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`; required).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx payment-transactions authorize --file authorize.json --dry-run
```

## epx payment-transactions cancel

Cancel an authorized payment.

Cancels the authorized payment of transaction ID: the provider releases the amount that
it reserved.

This moves money: the confirmation names the transaction in the URL that it shows. ID is
the ID that [`epx payment-transactions list`](/emporix-cli/commands/payment-transactions#epx-payment-transactions-list) shows; an unknown one is not found (exit 4).

Emporix answers whether the operation succeeded (successful). epx prints the response and
exits with 1 unless it says that it did: where it says that it failed (successful false,
with a message), and where it does not say, when it may have been carried out all the same.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the payment-gateway.cancel\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-transactions cancel ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx payment-transactions cancel T1 --dry-run
```

## epx payment-transactions capture

Capture an authorized payment.

Captures `--amount` in `--currency` of the authorized payment of transaction ID, at most the
amount authorized: the provider collects it from the customer. Emporix answers with the
provider's captureId, which refund `--capture-id` takes.

This moves money: the confirmation names the transaction in the URL that it shows. ID is
the ID that [`epx payment-transactions list`](/emporix-cli/commands/payment-transactions#epx-payment-transactions-list) shows; an unknown one is not found (exit 4).

Emporix answers whether the operation succeeded (successful). epx prints the response and
exits with 1 unless it says that it did: where it says that it failed (successful false,
with a message), and where it does not say, when it may have been carried out all the same.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the payment-gateway.capture\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-transactions capture ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--amount <AMOUNT>`\
  The AMOUNT to capture, e.g. 3.99 (required without `--file`).
- `--currency <CURRENCY>`\
  The CURRENCY of `--amount`, e.g. EUR (required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx payment-transactions capture T1 --amount 3.99 --currency EUR --dry-run
```

## epx payment-transactions get

Show one payment transaction.

Reads payment transactions, personal data included. PAYMENT MODE is the id of the payment
mode used, and ENTRIES the operations the provider ran, in the order sent: type and amount,
marked failed when they failed. Payment details (such as bank details and pay-by-link URLs),
card tokens and the provider's requests and responses are only in `-o json`. list's `--sort`
takes only createdDate (e.g. createdDate:desc); Emporix rejects other and several fields.

Requires the payment-gateway.paymenttransactions\_read scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-transactions get ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--columns <names>`\
  Print only these columns of table and csv, in this order: comma-separated names (any case) among ID, PROVIDER, PAYMENT MODE, ENTRIES.
- `--no-headers`\
  Print table and csv without the header row.
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Output format: table, json, yaml or csv (csv: the table's rows; json and yaml: the whole response). Default: `table`.

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

List payment transactions.

Reads payment transactions, personal data included. PAYMENT MODE is the id of the payment

## epx payment-transactions refund

Refund a captured payment.

Refunds `--amount` in `--currency` of the captured payment of transaction ID, at most the
amount captured: the provider returns it to the customer. Where the payment was captured
more than once, `--capture-id` names the capture to refund.

This moves money: the confirmation names the transaction in the URL that it shows. ID is
the ID that [`epx payment-transactions list`](/emporix-cli/commands/payment-transactions#epx-payment-transactions-list) shows; an unknown one is not found (exit 4).

Emporix answers whether the operation succeeded (successful). epx prints the response and
exits with 1 unless it says that it did: where it says that it failed (successful false,
with a message), and where it does not say, when it may have been carried out all the same.

Changes data: on a terminal, epx asks before it sends POST. `--yes` sends without
asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -); `--dry-run` prints the request
instead of sending it.

Requires the payment-gateway.refund\_manage scope.

**Command:** `epx payment-transactions refund ID [flags]`

**Flags**

- `--amount <AMOUNT>`\
  The AMOUNT to refund, e.g. 3.99 (required without `--file`).
- `--capture-id <ID>`\
  The ID of the capture to refund, as capture answered it.
- `--currency <CURRENCY>`\
  The CURRENCY of `--amount`, e.g. EUR (required without `--file`).
- `--dry-run`\
  Print the request instead of sending it (excludes `-o`).
- `--file <PATH>`\
  JSON request body in PATH, sent byte for byte instead of the one that epx makes (- reads standard input; sending it then needs `--yes`).
- `-o, --output <format>`\
  Format of the response: json or yaml. Default: `json`.
- `--yes`\
  Send without asking (required without a terminal, or with `--file` -).

Also takes the [global flags](/emporix-cli/commands#global-flags).

**Examples**

```sh
epx payment-transactions refund T1 --amount 3.99 --currency EUR --dry-run
```
